article_content: Curtis Elton is a lively nine-year-old boy with a passion for football, One Direction, and the cartoon Phineas and Ferb. But when he sits at the grand piano in his family’s living room, something extraordinary happens. He becomes utterly still — fingers poised — then erupts into a flawless performance of Bach’s Prelude and Fugue in D minor. Curtis has just become the youngest person in the world to earn the Associate of Trinity College London (ATCL) diploma — a prestigious qualification equivalent to the first year of a university music degree. The journey took nearly two years of daily two-hour practice sessions. He performed the demanding exam in a church hall in St Albans, playing for over 30 minutes entirely from memory, alongside two adult candidates aged 19 and 38. His mother, Haley, a professional concert pianist and teacher, first introduced him to music at age three. He begged to play while she practiced, and within weeks, he was learning scales. His first complete piece? 'Yankee Doodle.' Soon after, he mastered the Pink Panther theme and Beethoven’s Ode to Joy. By age four, Curtis could read music at sight and passed his Grade One exam — so small, exam staff initially thought his mother was the candidate. He went on to become the youngest ever to achieve Grade Eight in the UK. His first public performance came at age six, raising funds for the homeless with a Schumann piece. Since then, he’s played at the Chopin Museum in Mallorca and in front of over 2,000 people at Birmingham’s ICC. In 2011, Yamaha sponsored him, providing instruments for performances. Not all roads have been smooth. Curtis was devastated when he was unexpectedly cut from Britain’s Got Talent after a standing ovation — despite having packed his suitcase and booked a London hotel. 'I was looking forward to playing for the Queen,' he says wistfully. Despite his fame, Curtis’s life remains grounded. He attends Haberdashers’ Aske’s Boys’ School, prioritizes homework over practice, and plays football and ice skating with his sister Sophia. Practice only happens after schoolwork is done, and concerts are limited to weekends and holidays. Haley insists she’s no 'Tiger Mother.' 'I never pushed him,' she says. 'He loved it from the start. He’s happy, balanced, and has normal friends.' Looking ahead, Curtis plans to release his debut album in November, study composition and conducting, and eventually attend university for politics and mathematics. When asked if he’ll become a professional pianist, he smiles: 'If my piano gets very good, I’d love to play with an orchestra. But I’d also like to be Prime Minister… and maybe a doctor.' With his infectious energy, humility, and love for both music and life beyond the keys, Curtis Elton isn't just a prodigy — he’s a reminder that greatness can thrive in balance.

Uskoro je usvojio temu iz 'Pink Panthera' i Beethovenovu 'Odu radosti'. U četiri godine Kurtis je mogao čitati glazbu na prvi pogled i položio ispit za Grade One — bio je toliko mali da su ispitioci mislili da je njegova majka kandidat. Kasnije je postao najmlađi ikada koji je stekao Grade Eight u Velikoj Britaniji. Prvi javni nastup imao je u šestoj godini, prikupljajući sredstva za beskućnike s komadom Schumanna. 'Svakako sam se nadao da ću svirati za kraljicu,' kaže s tužnim osmijehom. Unatoč slavi, Kurtisov život ostaje zemaljski. Pohađa školu Haberdashers’ Aske’s Boys’ School, prioritet mu je domaći zadatak, a ne vježba, i igra nogomet i klizanje na ledu sa svojom sestrom Sophiom. 'Voli to od samog početka. Sretn je, uravnotežen i ima normalne prijatelje.' Gledajući unaprijed, Kurtis planira objaviti svoj debitantski album u studenom, učiti komponiranje i dirigiranje, te eventualno pohađati sveučilište za politologiju i matematiku. Kad ga pitaju hoće li postati profesionalni pijanista, on se osmjehne: 'Ako mi se klavir vrlo dobro razvije, volio bih svirati s orkestrom. Ali volio bih i postati premijer... možda i liječnik.' Sa svojom zaraznom energijom, skromnošću i ljubavlju prema glazbi i životu izvan klavira, Kurtis Elton nije samo prodigija — on je podsjetnik da se veličina može razvijati i u ravnoteži.

article_content: Nestled in Vietnam’s misty southern highlands, the Dalat Nuclear Research Institute sits atop a mountain — far from the town’s romantic image as a honeymoon destination. Inside a cylindrical concrete building, a 500-kilowatt pool-type reactor once held highly enriched uranium (HEU), a material capable of fueling nuclear weapons. Built in 1963 with U.S. assistance, the reactor initially used American HEU. After closing in 1975 following the Vietnam War, it was rebuilt by the Soviet Union and reopened in 1983 with Soviet-supplied HEU — a Cold War relic. For decades, few questioned the security of the material, despite its potential appeal to terrorists. Just 25 kilograms of HEU — easily disguised when encased in aluminum — can be used to construct a crude nuclear bomb. Its radiation is faint, detectable only by specialized sensors. This reality became chillingly clear during a rare, classified mission to remove the fuel. In September 2007, CNN was granted exclusive access to document a joint U.S.-Russian operation, coordinated by the Department of Energy and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), to replace the HEU with low-enriched uranium (LEU), which cannot be weaponized. Vietnam agreed to surrender its HEU in exchange for international support in developing peaceful nuclear energy. Upon arrival in Dalat, journalists donned lab coats and entered the reactor chamber. There, Vietnamese scientists handed over the fuel rods — slender aluminum tubes resembling table legs — to Russian experts, who handled them with minimal protective gear. One journalist held a rod barehanded: the ease of concealment was undeniable. The LEU fuel was then lowered into the reactor pool. When the control room gauges hit 'criticality,' applause broke out. The Vietnamese, eager to validate the new fuel’s performance, watched closely — their priority: reliable energy, not weapons. The HEU rods were sealed in two blue steel cylinders, certified by the IAEA, loaded onto a military truck, and escorted by armed soldiers through Dalat’s winding roads to the airport. There, soldiers hoisted the cylinders onto a Vietnamese military helicopter, which flew them to Ho Chi Minh City. From there, they were transferred to a Russian Ilyushin-76 bound for the Ural Mountains, where the material will be blended into non-weapons-grade form. Despite lingering wartime tensions — 'The last time Americans were here was when you bombed us,' one soldier remarked — journalists were permitted inside the aircraft. As the plane took off, the team, including Vietnamese troops and international experts, erupted in applause. This was the 13th such mission. Together, the U.S. and Russia have now removed 442 kilograms of HEU from 11 nations — enough for over 17 bombs. Yet, experts warn: half the job remains.
translated_content: Smješten u maglovitom jugozapadnom području Vijetnama, Nuklearni istraživački institut Dalat nalazi se na vrhu planine — daleko od romantičnog ugleda grada kao destinacije za medeni mjesec. U cilindričnoj betonskoj zgradi, 500-kilovatski reaktor tipa bazena nekad je sadržavao visoko obojeni uranijum (HEU), materijal sposoban da proizvede nuklearnu bombu. Izgrađen 1963. godine s pomoću SAD-a, reaktor je prvo koristio američki HEU. Nakon zatvaranja 1975. godine nakon Vijetnamskog rata, obnovljen je od strane Sovjetskog Saveza i ponovno otvoren 1983. godine s sovjetskim HEU-om — ostatak Hladnog rata. Decenijama su rijetko postavljali pitanja sigurnosti ovog materijala, unatoč njegovoj potencijalnoj privlačnosti za teroriste. Samo 25 kilograma HEU-a — lako sakrivajućih se kada su obloženi aluminijem — može se koristiti za izradu grubog nuklearnog oružja. Njegova radijacije je slabija, otkriva se samo posebnim senzorima. Ta stvarnost postala je užasavajuće jasna tijekom rijetke, klasificirane misije kojom je uklonjen gorivni element. U rujnu 2007. godine, CNN je dobio isključivi pristup dokumentiranju zajedničke operacije SAD-Rusija, koordinirane od strane Ministarstva energije SAD-a i Međunarodne agencije za atomsku energiju (IAEA), kako bi zamijenili HEU niskoozbiljenim uranijumom (LEU), koji ne može biti korišten za oružje. Vijetnam je pristao predati svoj HEU u razmjeni za međunarodnu podršku u razvoju mirnih nuklearnih energijskih programa. Prilikom dolaska u Dalat, novinari su obukli laboratorijske košulje i ulazili u reaktorsku sobu. Tamo su vijetnamski znanstvenici prenijeli gorivne šipke — tanka aluminijumska cijevi koje podsjećaju na noge stola — ruskim stručnjacima, koji ih su držali s minimalnom zaštitom. Jedan novinar je držao šipku golim rukama: jednostavnost sakrivanja bila je očigledna. LEU gorivo je onda spušteno u bazen reaktora. Kada su kazaljke u kontrolnoj sobi dostigle 'kritičnost', razbila se aplauz. Vijetnamski stručnjaci, željni provjeriti učinkovitost novog goriva, pažljivo su gledali — njihov prioritet: pouzdana energija, ne oružje. HEU šipke su bile zapečaćene u dvije plave čelične cilindre, certificirane od strane IAEA-a, opterećene na vojno kamionu i pratnjene naoružanim vojnicima kroz vijugave ceste Dalata do zrakoporta. Tamo su vojnici podigli cilindre na vijetnamski vojni helikopter, koji ih je preveo u Ho Ši Min City. Odande su prebačeni na ruski Ilijušin-76 koji je putovao prema Uralskim planinama, gdje će se materijal pretvoriti u oblik koji se ne može koristiti za oružje. Unatoč trajnim ratnim tenzijama — 'Posljednji put kad su Amerikanci ovdje bili bio je kada ste nas bombardirali,' rekao je jedan vojnik — novinarima je dopušten pristup unutar aviona. Dok je avion poletio, tim, uključujući vijetnamske vojnike i međunarodne stručnjake, proplakao je aplauzom. Ovo je bila 13. takva misija. Uzajamno, SAD i Rusija uklonile su 442 kilograma HEU-a iz 11 zemalja — dovoljno za više od 17 bombi. Ali stručnjaci upozoravaju: ostalo je još pola posla.

article_content: For barbecue enthusiasts, mastering the perfect burger is an art—but it’s also a potential health risk if done incorrectly. As grills ignite across the country this weekend, dietitian Dr. Cara Rosenbloom is issuing a crucial warning: undercooked burgers can harbor dangerous bacteria. Unlike whole cuts of beef, where surface bacteria are eliminated by searing, minced beef can contain E. coli throughout the patty due to the grinding process. This means the interior must reach the same high temperature as the exterior to ensure safety. Dr. Rosenbloom, author of the blog 'Words To Eat By,' emphasizes that both the outside and inside of a burger must be cooked to at least 71°C (160°F). Unlike chicken, whose dangers are widely understood, many people remain unaware that ground beef requires the same rigorous cooking standards. The problem? Infected meat often looks and smells perfectly normal—you cannot visually detect E. coli contamination. Food safety experts also stress simple but vital precautions: wash hands frequently, especially after handling raw meat; never reuse marinades that touched raw ingredients; always use separate plates for raw and cooked foods; and invest in a digital food thermometer to verify internal temperatures. In England and Wales, around 90,000 food poisoning cases are officially recorded annually—but experts believe the true number may approach one million, as most victims never seek medical care or submit samples. E. coli, particularly the O157 strain, can cause severe symptoms including bloody diarrhea and abdominal cramps. In children under five, it can trigger hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), a life-threatening condition that destroys red blood cells and leads to kidney failure. Research shows survivors of severe foodborne illness are at increased risk of long-term complications—including diabetes, hypertension, arthritis, kidney disease, heart attacks, and strokes—sometimes triggered by toxins released by the bacteria. Experts recommend that individuals who have suffered severe E. coli infections undergo regular kidney and blood pressure monitoring to catch late-onset complications early.
translated_content: Za ljubitelje roštilja, savršeno pečenje burgera je umjetnost — ali može biti i potencijalna zdravstvena opasnost ako se učini pogrešno. Dok se roštilji upaljuju širom zemlje ovog vikenda, prehranjenica dr. Cara Rosenbloom izdaje ključno upozorenje: nepečeni burgeri mogu sadržavati opasne bakterije. U suprotnosti od cijelih komada mesa, gdje su površinske bakterije uništene pečenjem, mrvljeno meso može sadržavati E. coli cijelim paticom zbog procesa mrvljenja. To znači da unutrašnjost mora dostići istu visoku temperaturu kao i vanjska površina kako bi bila sigurna. Dr. Rosenbloom, autorka bloga 'Words To Eat By', naglašava da vanjski i unutrašnji dio burgera moraju biti pečeni na barem 71°C (160°F). U suprotnosti od pilećeg mesa, čije opasnosti su široko poznate, mnogi ljudi nisu svjesni da mrvljeno meso zahtijeva iste stroge standarde kuhanja. Problem? Zaraženo meso često izgleda i miriše potpuno normalno — ne možete vizualno otkriti kontaminaciju E. coli-om. Stručnjaci za sigurnost hrane također naglašavaju jednostavne, ali ključne mjere: često perite ruke, posebno nakon rukovanja sirovim mesom; nikad ne ponovno koristite marinade koje su dodirivale sirovo meso; uvijek koristite različite tanjire za sirovo i kuhano hranu; i uložite u digitalni termometar za hranu kako biste provjerili unutarnju temperaturu. U Engleskoj i Walesu, godišnje je zabilježeno oko 90.000 slučajeva otrovanja hrane — ali stručnjaci vjeruju da pravi broj može doseći jedan milijun, jer većina žrtava nikad ne traži medicinsku pomoć ili ne dostavlja uzorke. E. coli, posebno strop O157, može izazvati ozbiljne simptome uključujući krvavi proljev i grčeve u trbuhu. Kod djece mlađe od pet godina može izazvati hemolitičko uremijski sindrom (HUS), životno opasan stanje koje uništava crvene krvne stanice i dovodi do oštećenja bubrega. Istraživanja pokazuju da su preživjeli teških oblika otrovanja hrane pod većom opasnošću za dugotrajne komplikacije — uključujući dijabetes, hipertenziju, artritis, bolesti bubrega, infarkte i moždane udare — ponekad izazvane toksinima koji ih oslobađaju bakterije. Stručnjaci preporučuju da osobe koje su preživjele teške infekcije E. coli redovito prolaze kontrolu krvnog tlaka i funkcije bubrega kako bi ranije otkrile kasne komplikacije.

article_content: On the morning of December 26, the day after Christmas, Jin Ackerman, 25, allegedly murdered Antonino Isnit, 58, during a robbery at a Walgreens store in Las Vegas. According to police, Ackerman entered the store around 4 a.m., wearing gray clothing, a black pea coat, and a surgical mask. He asked a female employee to help him find another mask and requested to use the bathroom. Once inside, he forcibly shoved her in, emptied her pockets, and handcuffed her. He then attached a silencer to a pistol he carried. The employee was paged by Isnit, who noticed her absence. Ackerman instructed her to act normally and warned her not to cry, saying the silencer was 'for Tony.' When Isnit arrived at the front, the woman convinced him to take a break while she opened the safe. Ackerman stole between $5,000 and $7,000. But when Isnit returned and asked why he was still there, Ackerman reportedly said, 'Sorry Tony, but you know me,' before shooting him dead. Eleven shell casings were found near Isnit’s body. Police confirmed that Ackerman and Isnit worked together at the same Walgreens location on W. Cheyenne Ave. in 2011. Ackerman was fired from a different Walgreens location—the Venetian Hotel branch—in July 2013 for improperly accessing employee records. Authorities also link him to a similar armed robbery at another Walgreens on Christmas Eve, where he reportedly wore a surgical mask. Ackerman was arrested by a SWAT team at his home on Friday after a seven-hour search. He now faces one count of murder, four counts of kidnapping, two counts of robbery, and two counts of burglary—all with a firearm. A makeshift memorial has been established by community members for Isnit, who was the primary caregiver for his 91-year-old mother.

article_content: On June 20, 2012, Britain experienced its hottest day of the month — officially marking the start of summer — with temperatures peaking at 22.5°C (72.5°F) in Northolt, west London. This surpassed the previous monthly high of 21.9°C (71.4°F). Other warm spots included Pershore (22.1°C) and Cardiff (21.6°C). However, by nightfall, a dramatic shift occurred: up to 40mm of rain fell across southern England and South Wales, triggering weather alerts. The Met Office warned of torrential downpours and potential surface flooding, particularly in the South West. Forecasters predict this pattern will persist. Simon Keeling of WeatherOnline noted that July will begin with unsettled conditions, as low-pressure systems linger near the UK, bringing prolonged showers and brisk winds. August looks even less promising — described as potentially an 'umbrella month' rather than a 'bucket-and-spade month.' Major summer events face disruption: Royal Ascot’s Ladies’ Day, the Formula 1 Grand Prix at Silverstone, The Open golf championship, and the London Olympics are all at risk of being affected by rain. Meanwhile, tourism operators report significant losses. Staycation bookings have dropped as holidaymakers cancel trips due to forecasts. In Guernsey, cruise ship cancellations have led to an estimated 7,000 fewer affluent visitors. Hotel and retail businesses, still recovering from the recession, are especially vulnerable. Yet amid the gloom, nature offered a bright spot: an unusually abundant bloom of buttercups. Student Maddi Ridley captured the beauty of the golden flowers in the New Forest. But this natural bounty has unintended consequences — the RSPCA has issued a warning to horse owners about 'buttercup burn,' a skin irritation caused by ranunculin in the plants. In contrast, continental Europe baked under extreme heat: Rome hit 37°C, and Vienna reached 34°C. The UK’s damp, cool summer stands in sharp contrast to both last year’s scorching Glastonbury Festival — when temperatures soared to 33°C — and this year’s barren festival grounds, left empty due to the Olympics. Clarification: Radar imagery referenced in the original article mistakenly suggested rainfall rates of '32mm per minute' — this is physically implausible. The color-coded map actually represents total accumulated rainfall over a 12–24 hour period, not per-minute intensity. The revised version omits this misleading detail.

Velika Britanija je doživjela najtopliji dan u mjesecu — službeno označavajući početak ljeta — s temperaturama koje su dosegle 22,5 °C (72,5 °F) u Northoltu, zapadni London. Ovo je premašilo prethodni mjesečni rekord od 21,9 °C (71,4 °F). Druga topla mjesta uključuju Pershore (22,1 °C) i Cardiff (21,6 °C). Međutim, do noći došlo je do dramatične promjene: do 40 mm kiše padlo je preko južne Engleske i juga Walesa, što je dovelo do izdavanja vremenskih upozorenja. Met Office je upozorio na olujne obilne kiše i potencijalno povišenje površinskih voda, posebno u jugozapadnoj Engleskoj. Prognozatori predviđaju da će se ovaj uzorak nastaviti. Simon Keeling iz WeatherOnline primjetio je da će srpanj početi nestabilnim vremenom, jer će niski pritisak ostati blizu Ujedinjenog Kraljevstva, donoseći produžene kiše i hladne vjetrove. August izgleda još lošije — opisan kao moguće 'mjesec kišobrana', a ne 'mjesec kante i lopatice'. Veliki ljetni događaji suočeni su s ometanjima: Djevojčičin dan na Royal Ascotu, Velika nagrada Formule 1 u Silverstonu, Otvoreno prvenstvo u tenisu i Olimpijske igre u Londonu svi su pod prijetnjom kiše. U međuvremenu, turistički operateri prijavljuju značajne gubitke. Rezervacije domaćih odmorista su se smanjile jer su putnici otkazali putovanja zbog prognoza. U Guernseyju, otkazivanja brodova za krstarenje dovelo je do procijenjenih 7.000 manje bogatih posjetitelja. Hoteli i trgovci, koji su još uvijek u oporavku od recesije, posebno su ugroženi. Ipak, u sredini tamnih vremena, priroda je ponudila svjetlu stranu: neočekivano obilno cvjetanje žutih ružičica. Studentica Maddi Ridley snimila je ljepotu zlatnih cvjetova u New Forestu. Ali ova prirodna darovitost ima neželjene posljedice — RSPCA je izdala upozorenje vlasnicima konja o 'oštećenju od ružičica', kožnu iritaciju uzrokovanu ranunkulinom u cvjetovima. U suprotnosti, kontinentalna Europa pekla se pod ekstremnom toplinom: Rim je dostigao 37 °C, a Beč 34 °C. Vlažno, hladno ljeće u Velikoj Britaniji nalazi oštar kontrast s prošlogodišnjim vrućim Glastonbury Festivalom — kada su temperature dosegle 33 °C — i ovogodišnjim praznim terenom festivala, koji je ostao prazan zbog Olimpijskih igara. Precizacija: Radar slike spomenute u izvornom članku pogrešno su sugerirale da su kišne stope bile '32 mm po minuti' — ovo je fizički nemoguće. Bojna škala zapravo predstavlja ukupnu akumuliranu kišu tijekom 12–24 sati, a ne intenzitet po minuti. Ovaj izmjereni tekst izostavlja ovu zavaravajuću informaciju.

article_content: New research challenges long-standing advice that pregnant women need vitamin D supplements to boost their baby’s bone development. A major study involving nearly 4,000 mothers found no meaningful connection between the mother’s vitamin D levels during pregnancy and the bone strength of their child at age 10. Despite this, UK health authorities like the NHS still recommend a daily 10-microgram supplement for all expectant and nursing mothers, based on the belief that vitamin D supports skeletal growth. The findings, published in The Lancet, measured vitamin D levels across all trimesters and assessed children’s bone mineral content (BMC) at nearly 10 years old. While vitamin D levels were naturally higher in summer and lower among smokers and non-white mothers, none of these variations correlated with differences in BMC. Experts like Professor Debbie Lawlor from the University of Bristol concluded there’s ‘no strong evidence’ to support universal supplementation. However, other specialists, including Dr Tony Falconer of the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, stress that certain women—such as those with darker skin, obesity, limited sun exposure, or poor dietary intake—are at greater risk of deficiency and should still be encouraged to take supplements. The consensus? One-size-fits-all guidance may not be necessary, but personalized care remains critical.

Unatoč tome, britanske zdravstvene vlasti poput NHS-a i dalje preporučuju dnevnu dozu od 10 mikrograma za sve trudnice i dojilje, jer se vjeruje da vitamin D pomaže u razvoju kostiju. Pronađeni rezultati, objavljeni u časopisu The Lancet, mjerili su razine vitamina D tijekom svih trimesjeca i procjenjivali sadržaj minerala u kostima (BMC) djece u dobi od skoro 10 godina. Iako su razine vitamina D bile prirodno više u ljetnim mjesecima i niže kod pušačica i majki s tamnijom kožom, nijedna od ovih varijacija nije bila povezana s razlikama u BMC-u. Stručnjaci poput profesorice Debbie Lawlor sa Sveučilišta Bristol zaključili su da ne postoji 'jači dokaz' za univerzalnu suplementaciju. Međutim, drugi stručnjaci, uključujući dr. Tonia Falconera iz Kraljevskog kollegija akushera i ginekologa, naglašavaju da određene žene—poput onih s tamnijom kožom, gojaznosti, ograničenim izlaganjem suncu ili lošom prehranom—imaju veći rizik od deficita i da im se i dalje preporučuje uzimanje dodataka. Konsenzus? Jedna velika preporuka možda nije potrebna, ali personalizirana njega ostaje ključna.

article_content: For many, university is a time for new experiences and connections—but a troubling trend revealed by The Debrief shows that some students are jeopardizing their health by skipping condoms during casual encounters. One 20-year-old student from the University of Exeter admitted to having unprotected sex with a peer who openly disclosed he had chlamydia. 'He was honest about it—we even joked about it that night—but I let passion take over,' she said, requesting anonymity. 'I knew it was treatable, and I figured I might not even catch it. So I just thought, f*** it. I was drunk, too. Now I can't believe how reckless I was—what if he had something worse?' She isn’t alone. Research from UKMedix.com found that 19% of 18- to 30-year-olds would have sex with someone knowing they have an STI. Of those, 39% say they’ve already done so. Another 26% believe using protection makes transmission impossible, while 11% admit they simply 'let passion get the better of them.' At Oxford University, a recent study found that 39% of students have willingly engaged in unprotected sex. Meanwhile, clinics report rising STI rates alongside falling testing numbers. Victoria Leonard, nurse manager at Brook’s youth health service, noted that STI positivity rates jumped from 6.8% to 7.6% in just one year—even as fewer students sought testing. Linda Ahearne of the London College of Arts described a 'massive STI problem' among students, despite widespread awareness campaigns. 'They’re having more unprotected sex and delaying testing,' she said. William Wright, a 19-year-old student at Loughborough University, compared unprotected sex to earning a trophy. 'I never use condoms—and neither do most guys I know,' he said. 'It’s uncomfortable, dulls sensation, and feels unnatural to stop mid-intimacy. Girls sometimes ask, but few insist. And honestly? Everything’s treatable these days.' But STIs don’t always show symptoms. Signs may include unusual discharge, pain during urination, rashes, or bleeding. Testing often involves urine samples, swabs, or blood tests—and is quick, confidential, and free at most clinics. Many STIs, including chlamydia, gonorrhea, herpes, HPV, and HIV, can also be spread through oral sex. Condoms remain the most effective protection. Most infections are curable with antibiotics, but early detection is critical. For more info, visit brook.org.uk.

Jedna 20-godišnja studentica s Univerziteta u Exeteru priznala je da je imala nezaštićeni spolni odnos s vršnjakom koji je otvoreno rekao da ima hlamidiju. Victoria Leonard, menadžerica medicinskog osoblja za mlade u Brook službi u Salfordu i Boltonu, primjetila je da su stope pozitivnih rezultata STD-a skočile s 6,8% na 7,6% samo za jednu godinu – čak i kad je manje studenata tražilo testiranje. Mnogi STDovi, uključujući hlamidiju, gonoreju, herpes, HPV i HIV, također se mogu prenijeti putem oralnog seksa. Kondomi ostaju najučinkovitija zaštita. article_content: At least 12 people were killed and more than 130 injured on Tuesday when two explosions struck an Interior Ministry building in Mansoura, a city in Egypt’s Nile Delta, according to Egyptian media reports. Earlier, the semi-official Al Ahram news agency cited the Health Ministry as reporting 14 deaths, but the toll was later revised downward—reasons for the change were not immediately clear. Among the injured was the head of the Dakahlia governorate’s security directorate, according to the state-run MENA news agency. Part of the building collapsed after the blasts, with one explosion occurring on an upper floor followed by a car bomb, MENA reported. Egypt’s interim Prime Minister Hazem al-Beblawi condemned the attack as a terrorist incident, vowing that those responsible would not go unpunished. While he did not explicitly name the Muslim Brotherhood—the political group backing ousted President Mohamed Morsy—he referred to the organization as a terrorist group in his national address. The Muslim Brotherhood responded on Twitter, strongly condemning the 'cowardly bombing in #Mansoura' and expressing deep condolences to the victims’ families. In September, an Egyptian court banned the Muslim Brotherhood’s activities and froze its assets, significantly diminishing its political influence. Witness Ahmed El Shabrawy described heavy damage at the scene, saying he watched residents pull a man from the rubble. He estimated dozens of vehicles were damaged and noted extensive structural destruction around the blast zone. At least ten ambulances responded, and blood donation centers became so overwhelmed that staff turned away volunteers. CNN initially learned of the explosions through social media. The attack comes ahead of Egypt’s constitutional referendum on January 14–15, which proposes banning religious parties and expanding military authority. The current constitution was suspended after a military coup in July removed Morsy, who had been democratically elected. Since then, protests—and occasional violent incidents, including bombings—have occurred nearly daily. On December 12, a car bomb injured 20 police recruits. On Sunday, Ansar Jerusalem, a jihadist group linked to attacks in the Sinai Peninsula, posted an online message urging army and police personnel to resign, stating: 'With your staying in these institutions from evening to morning, you are incurring the anger of Allah.' No group has yet claimed responsibility for Tuesday’s bombing. Meanwhile, Morsy, an Islamist leader, faces multiple charges—including escape from prison in 2011, raiding other prisons, and killing soldiers in Rafah. He and 132 others are scheduled to stand trial, according to state media. Morsy has been in custody since his removal from office.

Ranije, polu službeni novinski kanal Al Ahram navodio je da je Ministarstvo zdravstva prijavilo 14 mrtvih, ali je broj kasnije smanjen na 12 — razlozi za promjenu nisu bili odmah jasni. Bratstvo muslimana odgovorilo je na Twitteru, jačo osuđujući 'hrabrost napada u #Mansoura' i izražavajući duboke sažaljenje obiteljima žrtava. Trenutni ustav je suspendiran nakon vojnog puča u srpnju koji je svrgnuo Mursija, koji je bio demokratski izabran. Od tada su se gotovo svakodnevno događali protesti — a ponekad i nasilni incidenti, uključujući i bombe. 12. prosinca je automobilska bomba povrijedila 20 regruta policije. Nedjelju je Ansar al-Jerusalem, jihadistsko grupiranje povezano s napadima na Sinaj, objavilo online poruku kojom poziva vojne i policajce da napuste službu, navodeći: 'S time što ostajete u ovim institucijama od večeri do jutra, privlačite božju nesretnost.' Nijedna grupa još nije preuzela odgovornost za srijednji napad. Međutim, Mursi, islamski lider, suočen je s više optužbi — uključujući bijeg iz zatvora 2011., napade na druge zatvore i ubojstva vojnika u Rafahu. On i 132 druga osobe trebaju stati pred sud, prema državnim medijima. Mursi je u pritvoru otkad je svrgnut.

article_content: A recent investigation has revealed that the world’s wealthiest individuals are concealing an estimated £13 to £20 trillion in offshore accounts — an amount exceeding the combined economic output of the United States and Japan. This hidden wealth, largely shielded by legal loopholes and professional intermediaries, is depriving governments of vital tax revenue and fueling public distrust in democratic institutions. Led by James Henry, a former chief economist at McKinsey, the report titled 'The Price of Offshore Revisited' draws on data from the World Bank, IMF, UN, and central banks to map how ultra-high-net-worth individuals — just 92,000 people globally — control over £6.3 trillion in secret assets. These funds flow primarily through jurisdictions like the Cayman Islands, Switzerland, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong, which are ranked among the most secretive financial centers. But the problem isn’t limited to remote islands. The report highlights that many of the world’s largest financial hubs — including those in Europe and North America — are deeply involved in enabling financial secrecy. Even prestigious banks like UBS are estimated to manage trillions in hidden client wealth. According to John Christensen of the Tax Justice Network, the true scale of hidden wealth may be even greater, as it excludes non-financial assets such as private jets, luxury yachts, fine art, and prime real estate. He warns that when citizens perceive the system as rigged — where the rich pay little while ordinary people shoulder the burden — faith in democracy itself begins to crumble. Globally, governments lose roughly $250 billion each year due to offshore tax evasion. In some nations, the amount of capital fleeing abroad exceeds their foreign debt. The Tax Justice Network argues this secrecy distorts markets, fuels corruption, and disproportionately harms both developing economies and struggling European states like Greece and Portugal. If just 30% of the interest earned on these hidden assets were taxed, it could generate an additional £121 billion annually for public coffers worldwide — enough to fund education, healthcare, and infrastructure in countless communities.

Ova skrivena bogatstva, uglavnom zaštićena zakonskim rupama i profesionalnim posrednicima, oduzimaju vladama ključne porezne prihode i hrane javnu nevjernost u demokratske institucije. Ova sredstva protječu uglavnom kroz jurisdikcije poput Kajmanskih ostrva, Švicarske, Luksemburga i Hong Konga, koje se smatraju među najtajnijim financijskim centrima. Ali problem nije ograničen na udaljene otoke. Izvještaj naglašava da mnogi od najvećih financijskih centara na svijetu — uključujući one u Europi i Sjevernoj Americi — duboko su uključeni u omogućavanje financijske tajnosti. Čak i prestižne banke kao što su UBS procjenjuju se da upravljaju trilijunima u skrivenim klijentskim sredstvima. Prema Johnu Christensenu iz Mreže za poresku pravdu, stvarna veličina skrivenog bogatstva može biti još veća, jer ne uključuje ne-finansijska imovine poput privatnih aviona, luksuznih jachta, umjetničkih djela i primarnog nekretnina. Mreža za poresku pravdu tvrdi da ova tajnost izobličuje tržišta, hrani korupciju i nepravedno pogađa i razvijajuće i razvijene zemlje, poput Grčke i Portugala. Ako bi se samo 30% kamate na ova skrivena sredstva oporezivalo, moglo bi se godišnje generirati dodatnih 121 milijardu funti za državne blagajne širom svijeta — dovoljno da se finansiraju obrazovanje, zdravstvo i infrastruktura u beskrajno mnogo zajednica.

article_content: For nearly two decades, breast surgeon Ian Paterson performed hundreds of high-risk, non-standard operations on women across NHS and private hospitals in the West Midlands — often without proper consent or medical justification. Many of these procedures, known as 'cleavage-sparing mastectomies,' intentionally left behind breast tissue to enhance appearance, despite clear national guidelines warning that such practices dramatically increase cancer recurrence risk — by as much as 50% in some cases. Colleagues first raised alarms as early as 2003, yet hospital administrators ignored repeated warnings. Even after internal reviews recommended restrictions, Paterson continued operating until 2011. He was suspended that year, but kept his salary for another 18 months. One of the most heartbreaking cases involves Marie Pinfield, a 48-year-old policewoman diagnosed with aggressive breast cancer in 2006. She explicitly requested a double mastectomy to eliminate all cancer risk. Instead, Paterson performed a cleavage-sparing procedure, leaving behind tissue she later believed contributed to her death in 2008 at age 50. Her sister, Shirley Moroney, has spent years demanding justice, calling the official inquiry into the matter a 'farce' and a 'whitewash' — especially since its author, Sir Ian Kennedy, never spoke directly with Paterson. An independent report concluded the scandal was less about one rogue surgeon and more about a culture of silence and institutional failure. Yet victims argue that avoiding accountability for Paterson — who now faces potential criminal charges — undermines the entire process. Over 4,500 women may have received substandard care, with hundreds now pursuing legal action. Some believe Paterson misled healthy women into unnecessary surgeries, turning medical treatment into a cosmetic enterprise. The case exposes deep flaws in oversight: whistleblowers were silenced, protocols were broken, and lives were lost — all while the system looked away.

Ovaj slučaj otkriva duboke mane u nadzoru: javnici su bili ušutkani, protokoli su kršeni, a životi su izgubljeni — dok je sustav gledao drugamo.

article_content: Rory McIlroy capped off another stunning week by winning the WGC-Bridgestone Invitational, edging out Sergio Garcia in a thrilling final round at Firestone Country Club. His closing 66 sealed a two-stroke victory — the same margin as his recent Open Championship triumph — and propelled him back to world No. 1 for the first time since March last year. Alongside the Claret Jug, he now holds his first World Golf Championship title, cementing a remarkable two-week surge. McIlroy didn’t start the day leading, but he exploded out of the gates with three straight birdies. When Garcia dropped a shot on the third hole — after a wild drive accidentally hit a spectator, knocking a diamond from her ring (luckily recovered) — McIlroy flipped the script and took the lead. Though Garcia fought back, tying the score by the turn, McIlroy’s steady pressure proved too much. A bogey on the 15th and a missed 10-foot birdie putt on the 17th sealed Garcia’s fate. Meanwhile, Scott’s late collapse — three consecutive bogeys from the 14th — handed McIlroy the No. 1 spot without needing to wait. The Northern Irishman stayed focused, ignoring the hype and sticking to his pre-tournament plan: build momentum, don’t celebrate prematurely. On the leaderboard, Americans Keegan Bradley and Patrick Reed emerged as Ryder Cup standouts. Bradley tied for fourth, continuing his strong form since Medinah, while Reed carded a final-round 65 to clinch one of the last automatic spots after Dustin Johnson withdrew. Elsewhere, Phil Mickelson (62) and Lee Westwood (63) delivered bright spots with impressive rounds, but Britain’s quartet — Donaldson, Gallacher, Donald, and Poulter — all finished well off the pace. Despite the heartbreak, Garcia showed remarkable class. After years of losing to Tiger Woods, he now watches a new generation rise — and he’s cheering it on. The two shared warm words on the 18th fairway and a genuine handshake on the green. It was a moment of quiet respect between rivals, not resentment.

Njegov zatvarajući 66 osigurao je dvostroku pobjedu — istu razliku kao i njegova nedavna pobjeda na Open Championshipu — i vratilo ga je natrag na prvo mjesto u svjetskom rang listi po prvi put otkako je otišao s vrha u ožujku prošle godine. Uz Claret Jug, sada drži i svoju prvu naslovnicu Svjetskog prvenstva u golfu, čime je potvrdio izvanredan dvotjedni uspon. McIlroy nije počeo dan vodeći, ali je eksplozivno započeo s tri uzastopne birdije. Kada je Garcia izgubio bod na trećoj rupi — nakon što mu je divlja udarac pogodio gledateljicu i iskočio dijamant iz njezina prstena (srećom pronađen) — McIlroy je preokrenuo situaciju i preuzeo vodstvo. Iako se Garcia borio natrag, izjednačivši rezultat do polovice, McIlroyjeva stabilna pritisnja bila su prevelika. Bogey na 15. rupi i propuštena birdija od 10 stopa na 17. rupi zaključili su Garciovu sudbinu. U međuvremenu, kasni pad Scotta — tri uzastopna bogeya s 14. rupom — dao je McIlroyu prvo mjesto bez potrebe za čekanjem. Sjevernoirski igrač ostao je fokusiran, ignorirajući haos i pridržavajući se svog prijedtakmičkog plana: graditi impulz, ne slaviti unaprijed. Na ljestvici, američki igrači Keegan Bradley i Patrick Reed izdvojili su se kao kandidati za Ryder Cup. Bradley je bio povezan na četvrtom mjestu, nastavljajući svoju jaku formu otkako je bio na Medinahu, dok je Reed napravio zatvarajući 65 da bi osigurao jedno od zadnjih automatskih mjesta nakon što je Dustin Johnson povukao svoju kandidaturu. Unatoč srčanoj tužnosti, Garcia je pokazao izuzetnu klasu. Nakon godina gubitaka od Tiger Woodsa, sada gleda kako raste nova generacija — i podržava ju. Dvojica su razmjenjivala tople riječi na 18. rupi i autentični pozdrav na završnoj zeleni. To je bio trenutak tihe poštovanja između rivala, a ne mržnje.

article_content: Every morning, nurses and case managers with HOPICS drive through South Los Angeles, searching for people living in RVs, under bridges, and among tangled tents. Their mission: meet clients where they are — not in clinics, but on the streets. One such worker, nurse Anthony Velbis, checks on Anthony Boladeres, whose swollen leg may stem from unmanaged diabetes. Velbis gently cleans the wound as Boladeres explains he avoids hospitals due to stigma. 'It’s nice being able to meet the client where they’re at,' Velbis says. This is the reality of homelessness outreach: constant movement, limited tools, and deep emotional labor. Across L.A. County, more than 75,000 people are unhoused — and the numbers keep climbing. For every 207 people who find housing, 227 more lose theirs. HOPICS, one of 169 outreach teams funded by the county and local agencies, tries to bridge the gap. They hand out hygiene kits, clean needles, condoms, and connect people to legal aid, mental health services, and temporary motel stays. But these are Band-Aids on a hemorrhage. As one coordinator, Mychal Johnson, puts it: 'You want to help so badly, but when someone’s ready for housing… there’s nothing waiting.' Some residents, like Andy Romero, have been on the streets for nearly 20 years. He remembers being 12 when his parents split. 'You got to work with what you got,' he says. Others are in crisis: a woman hiding abuse, another begging for rehab. Johnson, who also serves as a minister, talks her through panic, persuading her sister — struggling with severe mental illness — to take the van to safety. The woman arrives at the shelter tearful, silent. A guard takes her sheet. ‘She won’t need this,’ he says. A case manager quietly saves it anyway. Critics like Pete White of the LA Community Action Network call this system the 'outreach industrial complex' — a well-intentioned distraction. 'Why hire thousands of workers if there aren’t thousands of homes?' he asks. L.A. voters approved $1.2 billion for permanent housing in 2016, but construction lags. Meanwhile, rents soar, and encampments grow. County officials like Cheri Todoroff defend outreach as the critical first step: 'We escort people to apartments, help with forms, pay deposits.' But for many, that help comes too late. At day’s end, the team packs up. One woman made it to safety. One man got his wound cleaned. One ID application was started. Tomorrow, they’ll return — to the same RVs, the same tents, the same impossible math. The work isn’t glamorous. But for those who show up, day after day, it’s the only thing keeping hope alive.

Njihov cilj: susretati klijente tamo gdje su — ne u klinikama, već na ulicama. Jedan od takvih radnika, medicinska sestra Anthony Velbis, posjećuje Anthonyja Boladeresa, čiji otok na nogi može biti posljedica nekontroliranog dijabetesa. Velbis pažljivo očisti ranu dok Boladeres objašnjava da izbjegava bolnice zbog stigme. 'Lijepo je moći susresti klijenta tamo gdje je,' kaže Velbis. To je stvarnost rada u pružanju pomoći bezdomnicima: stalno kretanje, ograničeni resursi i duboka emocionalna potreba. U cijelom okrugu Los Anđelesa više od 75.000 ljudi je bez doma — a broj se nastavlja povećavati. Za svakih 207 ljudi koji pronađu stan, 227 ih gubi. HOPICS, jedan od 169 timova za pomoć koji su financirani od strane okruga i lokalnih agencija, pokušava popraviti tu prazninu. Daju higijenske kitove, čiste igle, kondome i povezuju ljude s pravnim pomoću, psihološkom podrškom i privremenim smještajem u motelima. Ali to su zalihe na otvorenoj rani. Kako kaže koordinator Mychal Johnson: 'Želiš pomoći toliko, ali kad netko bude spreman za stan… ništa ne čeka.' Neke osobe, kao što je Andy Romero, bile su na ulicama skoro dvadeset godina. Sjeća se kako je imao 12 godina kad su mu roditelji razdvojeni. 'Moraš raditi s onim što imaš,' kaže on. Drugi su u krizi: žena koja skriva zlostavljanje, druga koja moli za liječenje. Johnson, koji također radi kao svećenik, razgovara s njom kroz paniku, uvjeravajući njezinu sestru — koja pati od teške psihičke bolesti — da uđe u kamion i ode na sigurno. Žena stigne u sklonište, suzna i tiha. Čuvar uzme njezin prostranac. 'Nećeš ga trebati,' kaže on. Službenik za slučajeve tiho ga sačuva. Kritičari poput Peta Whitea iz LA Community Action Network-a nazivaju ovaj sustav 'industrijom pomoći' — dobro namjernu distrakciju. 'Zašto zapošljavati tisuće radnika ako nema tisuće domova?' pita on. Glasovi u Los Anđelesu su odobrili 1,2 milijarde dolara za trajni stan u 2016., ali građevine kasne. U međuvremenu, najam raste, a naselja se šire. Funkcionari kao što je Cheri Todoroff branite pomoć kao ključni prvi korak: 'Pratimo ljude do stanova, pomažemo s formulama, plaćamo depozite.' Ali za mnoge, ta pomoć dolazi prekasno. Na kraju dana, tim pakira stvari. Jedna žena je stigla na sigurno. Jedan muškarac je dobio liječenje rane. Jedna prijava za identifikaciju je započeta. Sutra će se vratiti — na iste kamper, iste šatore, istu nemoguću matematiku. Posao nije glamurozan. Ali za one koji dolaze dan nakon dana, to je jedina stvar koja održava nade.

article_content: When Ashton Kutcher decides which technology startups to invest in, he sometimes thinks about pilgrims. 'What would happen if a pilgrim had seen a computer in action in Massachusetts back in the day?' Kutcher said onstage at a technology conference on Tuesday. 'They probably would have killed that person and called them a witch, because ultimately they would have seen it as magic.' In an analogy-laden interview at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference, Kutcher described how he selects from the myriad small companies that appeal to him for funding. The 'Two and a Half Men' actor has emerged as a prominent investor in Silicon Valley startups, using both his own money and funds from his investment firm, A-Grade Ventures. He was also an early celebrity adopter of Twitter. 'We're all kind of on a witch hunt, really,' Kutcher told fellow venture capitalists in the room. 'I like to learn how magic tricks work.' Though considered a flashy outsider by many, Kutcher is quickly gaining support from entrepreneurs eager to leverage his fame. He describes himself as a seasoned marketer—a former model who launched an acting career and sold films to high-profile producers. He has provided financial and promotional support to companies including Airbnb, the room-rental platform; Flipboard, the iPad news aggregator that competed with CNN’s Zite; and Foursquare, the location-check-in app. He sometimes hides his affiliation to avoid overshadowing the startups. 'Disclosing that I'm an investor can sometimes be detrimental to the company,' Kutcher said. 'I try not to talk about it until the company has gained enough public awareness and its story has matured enough not to be disrupted by my involvement.' This strategy recently landed him in trouble when he edited a section of Conde Nast’s Details magazine promoting tech companies he was financially involved in—without disclosing his relationships. While the U.S. Federal Trade Commission has rules requiring journalistic disclosure, it stated last month that it does not plan to investigate the matter.

'Vjerojatno bi ubili tu osobu i nazvali je vješticom, jer bi u konačnici to vidjeli kao magiju.' U intervjuu punom analoga na TechCrunch Disrupt konferenciji, Kutcher je opisao kako bira iz mnoštva malih tvrtki koje ga zanimaju za financiranje. Glumac iz 'Dvije i pol muškaraca' postao je poznat ulagač u startupovima iz Silicon Valleya, koristeći svoje vlastite novce i sredstva iz njegove ulagačke tvrtke, A-Grade Ventures. Također je bio jedan od prvih poznatih korisnika Twittera. 'Svi mi zapravo smo na lovu na vješice,' rekao je Kutcher ostalim riziknim kapitalistima u prostoriji. 'Volim saznati kako funkcioniraju čarolije.' Iako se smatra šikanim vanjskom osoba u mnogim krugovima, Kutcher brzo dobiva podršku od poduzetnika koji žele iskoristiti njegovu slavu. Sam sebe opisuje kao iskusnog marketinškog stručnjaka — bivšeg modela koji je pokrenuo karijeru glumca i prodavao filmove visokoprofilnim producentima. Pružio je financijsku i promotivnu podršku tvrtkama poput Airbnba, platforme za iznajmljivanje soba; Flipboarda, agregatora vijesti za iPad koji je bio konkurent CNN-ovom Ziteu; i Foursquarea, aplikacije za provjeru lokacije. Ponekad skriva svoju pripadnost kako ne bi zasjenio startape. 'Objavljivanje da sam ulagač ponekad može biti štetno za tvrtku,' rekao je Kutcher. 'Pokušavam ne govoriti o tome dok tvrtka ne stekne dovoljno javne svijesti i dok se njezina priča ne dovoljno zrelo razvije da ne bi bila ometena mojim sudjelovanjem.' Ova strategija nedavno ga je uvela u probleme kada je uređivao dio časopisa Conde Nast Details u kojem je promovirao tehnološke tvrtke u koje je financijski uključen, bez otkrivanja svojih veza. Iako U.S. Federal Trade Commission ima pravila o otkrivanju u novinarstvu, ona je prošli mjesec izjavila da ne planira istraživati ovaj slučaj.

article_content: On September 27, 2011, during a BBC Radio 4 interview on Woman’s Hour, Deputy Labour Leader Harriet Harman made an unintended slip, momentarily referring to David Miliband as the candidate she hoped would become Prime Minister — confusing him with his younger brother, Ed Miliband, the current Labour leader. Harman swiftly corrected herself, clarifying: 'I hope we will get Ed Miliband elected as Prime Minister for the next election, and then he will be Prime Minister for ten years — so not in the next ten years, no.' The gaffe came amid continued public and media attention on the strained relationship between the Miliband brothers following Ed’s narrow victory over David in the 2010 leadership contest. Though David had stronger backing from MPs, MEPs, and grassroots members, Ed secured victory through union support. While advocating for the principle that Labour’s leadership team should always include a woman, Harman acknowledged that the current leader, Ed, is male. When asked who she believed might be Labour’s first female leader, she declined to speculate, likening the question to asking a woman who her second husband might be: 'If you’re still on your first, you don’t want to talk about the second one. It’s just not a conversation you can have.' At the time of the interview, David Miliband had attended only one event at the Labour Party Conference and was scheduled to travel to the United States while Ed delivered his keynote leadership speech.

Harman je odmah ispravila svoju pogrešku, objasnivši: 'Nadam se da ćemo dobiti Eda Milibanda izabranim za premijera na sljedećim izborima, a onda će biti premijer deset godina — dakle, ne u sljedećih deset godina, ne.' Ova greška došla je u vrijeme kada su javnost i mediji nastavili proučavati napon između braće Miliband jer je Ed uspio uspješno pobijediti Davida u borbi za vođstvo 2010. godine. Iako je David imao jaču podršku među članovima parlamenta, europarlamentarima i redovnim članovima stranke, Ed je pobijedio zbog podrške sindikata. Dok je zagovarala princip da tim za vođstvo Labour stranke uvijek treba uključivati ženu, Harman je priznala da je trenutni predsjednik, Ed, muškarac. U vrijeme intervjua, David Miliband posjetio je samo jedan događaj na konferenciji Labour stranke i bio je u planu da putuje u Sjedinjene Američke Države dok je Ed održavao svoj ključni govor o vođstvu.

article_content: In a dramatic political shift, Israel’s Knesset has voted to dissolve and hold an early parliamentary election on January 22, 2013 — months ahead of the originally planned October vote. The decision follows Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s announcement that his coalition could no longer agree on a sustainable budget. Citing the need for stable governance amid economic pressures and rising regional threats, particularly from Iran, Netanyahu argued that fresh elections would allow the public to choose leaders best equipped to handle these challenges. 'As prime minister, my duty is to place the country’s needs above all else,' he said, stressing that a long-term budget could not be passed without consensus. Key coalition allies — including the ultra-Orthodox Shas party and Avigdor Lieberman’s nationalist Yisrael Beytenu — refused to back spending cuts targeting low-income households and large families. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Ehud Barak insisted on protecting military funding. With these three critical blocs opposing the proposed budget, Netanyahu concluded that legislative deadlock was inevitable, leaving an election as the only viable path forward. Economic data from the Bank of Israel showed modest growth projections of 3.3% for 2013, with inflation holding steady at 2.6% through the third quarter, underscoring the delicate balance between fiscal restraint and social support.
translated_content: U spektakularnom političkom potezu, Kneset je glasovao za raskid i održavanje ranih parlamentarnih izbora 22. siječnja 2013. — mjesecima prije izvorno planiranih izbora u listopadu. Odluka slijedi nakon objave premijera Benjamina Netanjahua da njegova koalicija više ne može postići sporazum o održivom proračunu. Navodeći potrebu za stabilnom vladavinom u vrijeme ekonomskog pritiska i rastućih regionalnih prijetnji, posebno od Irana, Netanjahu je tvrdio da bi novi izbori omogućili javnosti da odabere vođe najbolje opremljene da riješe te izazove. 'Kao premijer, moja dužnost je staviti potrebe zemlje iznad svega drugoga,' rekao je, naglašavajući da dugoročni proračun ne može biti prolazan bez konsenzusa. Ključni saveznici koalicije — uključujući ultrapravoslavnu stranku Šas i nacionalističku Yisrael Beytenu Avigdora Liebermana — odbili su podržati smanjenja troškova namijenjena obiteljima s niskim prihodima i velikim obiteljima. Međutim, ministar obrane Ehud Barak insistirao je na zaštiti vojnih sredstava. S tim triju ključnih blokova koji se protive predloženom proračunu, Netanjahu je zaključio da je zakonski staz u blokadi neizbježan, ostavljajući izbore kao jedini mogući izlaz. Podaci iz Banke Izraela pokazali su umjerene projekcije rasta od 3,3% za 2013. godinu, s inflacijom koja je ostala stabilna na 2,6% do kraja trećeg kvartala, ističući osjetljivu ravnotežu između fiskalne ograničenosti i socijalne podrške.

article_content: Actress Mackenzie Phillips has spoken candidly about her tumultuous life, attributing her struggles with addiction and trauma to a deep-rooted genetic predisposition—not merely the pressures of fame. In a recent appearance on 'The Oprah Winfrey Show,' she disclosed that she endured a decade-long incestuous relationship with her father, legendary musician John Phillips, beginning in 1979. The abuse, she said, started on the night before her planned wedding to Jeff Sessler, a member of the Rolling Stones’ circle, during a drug-fueled encounter. Phillips, best known for her role as Julie Cooper on the 1970s sitcom 'One Day at a Time,' has long been open about her battles with cocaine addiction, multiple arrests, and rehab stays. But in her memoir, 'High on Arrival'—named after a song her father wrote for her—she reveals the deeper wound: sexual abuse by her parent. She ended the relationship after becoming pregnant and discovering she couldn’t determine whether her child’s father was her husband or her father. She chose to terminate the pregnancy. Born Laura Mackenzie Phillips in 1959 to John Phillips and Baltimore socialite Susan Adams, Mackenzie lived a fractured childhood. While her mother raised her as a 'proper lady,' weekends with her father exposed her to rock legends like Paul McCartney and Mick Jagger. By age 10, he taught her to roll a joint; at 11, she tried cocaine; at 12, she lost her virginity. Her acting career soared early—with roles in 'American Graffiti' and later 'One Day at a Time'—but addiction quickly followed. Arrested in Los Angeles after collapsing on quaaludes, she received a chilling response from her father: 'Congratulations! Now you’re a real Phillips.' Her erratic behavior disrupted filming, and she missed the 1980–81 season of her show while in rehab. She later rejoined her father and stepmother at Fair Oaks psychiatric hospital, where they were being treated for narcotics-related charges. In her memoir, she describes finding a package containing her father’s autobiography alongside an eighth of an ounce of cocaine. Flipping through the book, she discovered her life reduced to a clinical index: 'arrested on drug charges,' 'drug use by,' 'rape.' 'I felt like I wasn’t a real person,' she wrote, 'just a list of incidents and accidents.' Though her career revived in the 1990s with guest roles on 'Beverly Hills, 90210,' 'Melrose Place,' and Disney’s 'So Weird,' and she later gave birth to her son Shane, relapses persisted. She was arrested again in 2008 en route to a 'One Day at a Time' reunion. Since then, she says she has remained drug-free. Even now, Phillips insists she does not hate her father. 'I have to say that I loved my father, and I still do,' she told Oprah. 'I’ve been trying to come to terms with this very difficult past.'

Na nedavnom nastupu na 'Oprah Winfrey Show' otkrila je da je pretrpjela desetogodišnji incestuozni odnos s ocem, legendarnim glazbenikom Johnom Phillipsom, koji je počeo 1979. godine. Zloupotreba, rekla je, počela je noć prije njenog planiranog vjenčanja s Jeffom Sesslerom, članom kruga Rolling Stonesa, tijekom događaja pod utjecajem droga. Phillipsova, najpoznatija po ulozi Julie Cooper u sjajnoj seriji iz 1970-ih 'One Day at a Time', dugo je otvoreno govorila o svojim borbama s kokainom, višestrukim hapšenjima i boravcima u liječenju. Rođena kao Laura Mackenzie Phillips 1959. godine od Johna Phillipsa i socijalne kraljice iz Baltimora, Susane Adams, Mackenzie je živjela razdvojenim djetinjstvom. Dok ju je majka odgojila kao 'pravilnu djevojku,' vikendovi s ocem izlagali su je rock legendama poput Paula McCartneya i Micka Jaggera. U 10 godina naučila ju je uvijati duhan; u 11 je probala kokain; u 12 je izgubila djevičanstvo. Njezina glumačka karijera brzo je napredovala — uloge u 'American Graffiti' i kasnije u 'One Day at a Time' — ali ovisnost je uslijedila brzo. U svom memoaru opisuje kako je pronašla paket koji sadrži očevu autobiografiju uz osminu unije kokaina. Listajući knjigu, otkrila je kako joj je život sveden na klinički indeks: 'uhvaćena zbog droga,' 'upotreba droga,' 'silovanje.' 'Osjećala sam da nisam prava osoba,' napisala je, 'već popis događaja i nesreća.' Iako joj je karijera obnovljena u 1990-ima s gostujućim ulogama u 'Beverly Hills, 90210,' 'Melrose Place' i Disneyjevoj seriji 'So Weird,' te kasnije rođenjem sina Shana, povratci su nastavili. Ponovno je uhvaćena 2008. godine na putu do sastanka 'One Day at a Time'. Od tada kaže da je ostala bez droga. Čak i sada, Phillips insistira da ne mrzi svog oca. 'Moram reći da sam voljela svog oca, i još uvijek volim,' rekla je Oprah. 'Pokušavam se pomiriti s ovim vrlo teškim prošlošću.'

article_content: The morning after Argentina lifted the 1978 World Cup, the country’s police chief made a striking claim: twelve million people flooded central Buenos Aires — and not a single glass was shattered. It was a moment of collective release, raw and peaceful, in a nation that had spent years living under the shadow of terror. Just months before, the streets of Buenos Aires were haunted by silence. Thousands of dissidents had vanished — taken by the military dictatorship known as the Dirty War. Their families stood outside the Casa Rosada, crying out for answers that never came. Meanwhile, imprisoned critics could hear the distant chants of football fans from their detention centers, barely a mile away from where history would unfold. Enter César Luis Menotti — the visionary coach who refused to play by the regime’s rules. While the generals dreamed of a glittering victory to distract from their crimes, Menotti chose players based on character, not club loyalty. He turned his back on Boca Juniors — dubbed the 'Butchers of Buenos Aires' for their brutal style — selecting only one player from their ranks: the elegant full-back Alberto Tarantini. His decision was an act of rebellion. Threatened with death if Argentina lost, Menotti simply lit another cigarette and kept coaching. His team responded with breathtaking football — fluid, fearless, and full of soul. Ossie Ardiles danced through defenses; Mario Kempes scored with purpose; Daniel Passarella led with grit. When Argentina crushed Peru 6-0 in a match that sparked accusations of fixing, the world doubted. But the Argentine people didn’t buy it. The Peruvians had nearly equalized twice. The goals were earned. And in a country where truth was scarce, this felt real. The final against the Netherlands was electric. Rene van de Kerkhof wore a plaster cast — disputed, then permitted. The crowd roared as Kempes opened the scoring. The Dutch tied it late. The tension was unbearable. Then, in extra time, Kempes struck again. Bertoni sealed it. And when the whistle blew, the city exploded — not with violence, but with joy. Thousands poured into the streets. Cars were abandoned. People ran atop buses and trucks, lifted by the tide of emotion. That night, Menotti kept his promise: he ran bare-chested through the Avenida 9 de Julio, scarf tied like a warrior’s bandana, surrounded by thousands who’d finally felt free again. It wasn’t just a football win. It was a reclamation. A nation that had been told it was unworthy — by its own government — was reminded of its dignity, its passion, its spirit. Decades later, as Brazil prepares for its own carnival, the message remains: sometimes, sport doesn’t just entertain. It heals.
translated_content: Jutro nakon što je Argentina osvojila Svjetsko prvenstvo 1978. godine, načelnik policije izjavio je zapanjujuću tvrdnju: dvanaest milijuna ljudi popunilo je centar Buenos Airesa — i nijedna čaša nije razbijena. To je bio trenutak kolektivne olakšice, sirov i miran, u zemlji koja je godinama živjela u sjenu terora. Samom mjesecima prije, ulice Buenos Airesa bile su okovane tišinom. Tisuće dissidenata nestale su — odvedene od vojne diktature poznate kao Prljavi rat. Njihove obitelji stajale su ispred Casa Rosade, vikajući za odgovorima koji nikada nisu stigli. U međuvremenu, zatvorenici su mogli čuti udaljene povike navijača iz svojih zatvorskih centara, malo više od milje od mjesta gdje će se dogoditi povijest. Uđite César Luis Menotti — vizionar trenera koji je odbio igrati po pravilima režima. Dok su generali sanjali sjajnu pobjedu kako bi odlučili pažnju od svojih zločina, Menotti je birao igrače prema karakteru, a ne klubskoj lojalnosti. Okrenuo je leđa Boki Juniors — poznatoj kao 'Mačkari iz Buenos Airesa' zbog njihove brutalne igre — te izabrao samo jednog igrača iz njihovog sastava: elegantičnog punog braniča Alberta Tarantinija. Njegova odluka bila je akt pobune. Pretnja smrću ako Argentina izgubi, Menotti je jednostavno upalio još jednu cigaretu i nastavio s treningom. Njegov tim odgovorio je oduševljavajućom nogometnom igrom — tekućom, bezbojnom i punom duše. Ossie Ardiles plesao je kroz obranu; Mario Kempes zabijao je sa svrhom; Daniel Passarella vodio je s hrabrošću. Kad je Argentina razbila Peruvijancima 6-0 u utakmici koja je izazvala optužbe za podmuklost, svijet je sumnjao. Ali argentinacima to nije vjerovalo. Peruvijanci su skoro izjednačili dva puta. Golovi su bili zasluženi. A u zemlji gdje je istina bila rijetka, ovo se osjećalo kao stvarno. Finalna utakmica protiv Holandije bila je električna. Rene van de Kerkhof nosio je gipsani omet — osporavan, ali dopušten. Tisuće su vikale kad je Kempes otvorio rezultat. Holandija je izjednačila kasno. Napon je bio neodrživ. Zatim, u produžecima, Kempes je ponovo udario. Bertoni je zaključio. I kad je sirnulo, grad je eksplodirao — ne s nasiljem, već sa radošću. Tisuće su se izlile na ulice. Automobili su ostavljeni. Ljudi su trčali preko autobusa i kamiona, uzdignuti valom emocija. Te noći Menotti je ispunio obećanje: trčao je bez košulje kroz Avenidu 9 de Julio, šaljući ga kao vojnički obavezni trak, okružen tisućama ljudi koji su konačno osjetili slobodu. To nije bila samo nogometna pobjeda. To je bio oporavak. Zemlja kojoj je rečeno da je nedostojna — od njenih vlasti — podsjetila se na svoj dostojanstvo, svoju strast, svoj duh. Dekade kasnije, dok se Brazili spremaju na svoj karneval, poruka ostaje: ponekad, sport ne samo zabavlja. On liječi.

article_content: At 32, Martin Tatta doesn’t train horses — he converses with them. Growing up on Estancia La Bamba de Areco in Argentina, where his parents worked, he spent his childhood alongside horses, not as livestock, but as companions. By the time he was a teenager, ranch owners noticed how effortlessly he connected with them — how they followed him, leaned into his touch, and seemed to understand his quiet cues. They encouraged him to share what he did naturally, and today, thousands of visitors come from around the world to watch his performances. In his shows, Tatta does things most would consider impossible: he stands upside down on Primavera’s neck, sits calmly beneath her hooves, and lets her roll onto her back so he can rest his head on her belly like a pillow. These aren’t tricks forced with pressure or pain. They’re the result of years of mutual trust built through patience, consistency, and respect. Each of the six horses he performs with takes between one and a half years to prepare — not because they’re stubborn, but because, like children, they learn in bursts. Some days they’re brilliant; other days, they need space. Tatta says he doesn’t possess any magical talent. 'It’s just listening,' he explains. 'If you pay attention, horses tell you exactly what they need.' While some of his movements echo historical practices — such as using a horse’s body for cover during hunting — Tatta doesn’t claim direct lineage to any specific Indigenous group. He simply honors the quiet wisdom of working *with* animals, not against them. His colleague Mara Felices recalls, 'For Martin, horses weren’t animals — they were family. He rode them to school, slept beside them, talked to them. That’s how he learned.' Now a freelance performer, Tatta’s fame is spreading beyond Argentina. But for him, the real reward isn’t applause — it’s the quiet moment after the show, when Primavera nuzzles his cheek, and they both just breathe together.
translated_content: Na 32 godine Martin Tatta ne trenira konje — razgovara s njima. Odrastajući na Estancia La Bamba de Areco u Argentini, gdje su njegovi roditelji radili, proveo je djetinjstvo uz konje, ne kao stoku, već kao društvo. Kada je bio tinejdžer, vlasnici imanja primijetili su kako bez truda uspostavlja vezu s njima — kako ga slijede, naginju se njegovom dodiru i čini se da razumiju njegove tihe znakove. Podstakli su ga da dijeli ono što je prirodno radio, a danas tisuće posjetitelja dolaze iz cijelog svijeta da gledaju njegove predstave. U svojim predstavama, Tatta radi stvari koje većina smatra nemogućima: stoji okrenut prema dolje na vratu Primavere, sjedi mirno ispod njenih kopita i dopušta joj da se okrene na leđa tako da može položiti glavu na njezin trbuh poput jastuka. To nisu trikovi nametnuti silom ili bolom. To su rezultat godina međusobne povjerenja izgrađenih strpljenjem, konzistentnošću i poštovanjem. Svaki od šest konja koje koristi za predstave priprema se između jedne i pol i dvije godine — ne zato što su uporni, već jer, kao djeca, uče u serijama. Neki dani su sjajni, drugi dani trebaju prostor. Tatta kaže da ne posjeduje nikakav čarobni dar. 'To je samo slušanje,' objašnjava. 'Ako pažljivo slušate, konji vam točno kažu što trebaju.' Iako neki njegovi pokreti podsjećaju na povijesne prakse — poput korištenja tijela konja kao zaklona tokom lova — Tatta ne tvrdi direktnu povezanost s bilo kojom određenom indijanskom skupinom. On jednostavno poštuje tihu mudrost rada *s* životinjama, a ne protiv njih. Njegova koleginica Mara Felices sjeća se: 'Za Martina, konji nisu bili životinje — bili su obitelj. Vožio ih je u školu, spavao pored njih, razgovarao s njima. Tako je naučio.' Danas je slobodan izvođač, a njegova slava širi se izvan Argentine. Ali za njega, prava nagrada nije pljesak — to je tihi trenutak nakon predstave, kad Primavera lagano pritisne njegovu bok, a oni oboje jednostavno dišu zajedno.

article_content: Mariam Khaowleh, a 40-year-old Syrian mother of four, lies wrapped in bandages, her body scarred not by war, but by her own hand. In a quiet hospital room in Lebanon, she speaks through an intercom, her voice trembling with exhaustion and grief. 'I chose death,' she says, 'because I couldn’t bear watching my children starve.' Her husband, Ahmad, watches from behind the glass, tears streaking his face. He remembers the woman who laughed beside him 24 years ago — now barely recognizable, her spirit broken by years of hunger and bureaucracy. The family fled Homs two years ago, hoping for safety in Lebanon. But survival became a daily battle. Three of their children suffer from a rare blood condition that demands specific nutrition — food they could no longer afford. Aid from the UN and WFP kept them alive, until last year, when a reassessment labeled them ‘not vulnerable enough.’ Mariam visited the UNHCR office in Tripoli again and again. 'I begged them,' she says. 'I told them they made a mistake.' Instead of help, she says she was shouted at, mocked, told to leave. 'If you won’t give me food, what choice do I have?' she pleaded. 'I’ll burn myself so you feel what I feel.' Days later, she doused herself in gasoline outside the same office. Witnesses say she collapsed, engulfed in flames within seconds. 'She didn’t scream,' one bystander recalls. 'She just burned — like a candle no one bothered to light.' The UN denies any mistreatment, claiming no record of her appeals. Yet they confirm they’re now covering her full medical bills and reassessing her family’s eligibility. They also say they offered housing relocation — a proposal the family refused, fearing for their daughters’ safety. In her pain, Mariam still thinks of her children. 'I worked so hard for their education,' she whispers. 'I wanted them to be doctors, teachers — not ghosts of hunger.' She begs the world to hear her: 'Don’t let this happen to another mother. Feel my heart. It’s already ash.' As the number of Syrian refugees in Lebanon surpasses one million, Mariam’s story is no longer just hers — it’s a mirror held up to a system failing those it swore to protect.

U tihoj bolnici u Libanu, govori kroz interkom, glas joj trema od iscrpljenosti i žalosti. 'Izabrala sam smrt,' kaže, 'jer nisam mogla gledati kako moja djeca umiru od glad.' Njezin muž, Ahmad, gleda s druge strane stakla, suze mu teku po licu. Sjeća se žene koja je smijala pored njega prije 24 godine — sada gotovo neprepoznatljiva, njezin duh slomljen godinama glad i birokracije. Obitelj je pobjegla iz Homsa prije dvije godine, nadajući se sigurnosti u Libanu. Ali opstanak je postao svakodnevna borba. Tri njihova djeteta trpe rijetku bolest krvi koja zahtijeva posebnu prehranu — hranu koju više nisu mogli priuštiti. Pomoć od Ujedinjenih naroda i Svjetskog programa za hranu održavala ih je na životu, sve dok prije godinu dana procjena nije označila njih kao 'ne dovoljno ranjive.' Mariam je ponavljano dolazila na uređaj UNHCR-a u Tripoliju. 'Molila sam ih,' kaže. 'Rekla sam im da su pogriješili.' Umjesto pomoći, kaže da su je vrijeđali, smijali se i naređivali joj da ode. 'Ako mi ne date hranu, što mi je ostalo?' molila je. 'Zapalit ću se da biste osjetili što ja osjećam.' Danima kasnije, zalila se benzinom van istog centra. Svjedoci kažu da je pala na tlo i trenutno je bila okružena plamenom. 'Nije vikala,' sjeća se jedan prolaznik. 'Samo je gorjela — poput sveće koju nitko nije htio upaliti.' Ujedinjeni narodi odbijaju da je bilo zlostavljanja, tvrdeći da nemaju zapis o njezinim zahtjevima. Međutim, potvrđuju da sada pokrivaju sve njezine medicinske troškove i ponovno procjenjuju pristup obitelji pomoći. Također kažu da su ponudili naseljavanje u zajednički dom — ponudu koju je obitelj odbila, bojeći se za sigurnost svojih kćeri. U svojoj bolu, Mariam i dalje misli na svoja djeca. 'Toliko sam se trudila za njihovu edukaciju,' šapće. 'Željela sam da budu liječnici, učitelji — ne duhovi gladi.' Molim svijet da me čuje: 'Ne dopustite da se to dogodi drugoj majci. Osjetite moje srce. Već je pepel.' Kako broj sirijanskih izbjeglica u Libanu premašuje jedan milijun, Mariamina je priča više nije samo njena — to je ogledalo koje se drži pred sustavom koji je obećao zaštititi one koji su ga najviše potrebovali.

article_content: In Baghdad, diplomats from Iran and six major world powers met to find common ground on Tehran’s nuclear activities—a critical moment amid rising regional tensions. The group, known as the P5+1, presented a detailed, phased plan asking Iran to take verifiable steps demonstrating its program is peaceful. In return, they offered technical support for civilian nuclear projects and economic aid, though no immediate sanctions relief was promised. Iran responded with its own proposals, but experts say they fall short of addressing core international worries, particularly around uranium enrichment beyond 20%, which can be rapidly scaled to weapons-grade levels. Meanwhile, the IAEA announced a breakthrough: Iran agreed to move forward with a structured inspection plan, including potential access to the Parchin military site, long suspected of hosting weapons-related experiments. Though details remain scarce, both sides described the talks as constructive. Israel, however, remains unconvinced. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that concessions would be dangerous, insisting Iran must shut down all enrichment operations and dismantle the Fordow facility buried under a mountain. As economic pain mounts—with 80% of Iran’s revenue tied to oil, and a new EU embargo looming in July—the pressure on Tehran to compromise grows. Behind closed doors, senior officials from the EU and Iran completed bilateral talks, setting the stage for a final plenary. While no deal is expected yet, diplomats say meaningful progress is possible—if both sides stay serious.

Grupa poznata kao P5+1 predstavila je detaljan, faza po faza plan koji traži od Irana da poduzme provjerljive korake koji pokazuju da je njegov program mirnog karaktera. U zamjenu, ponudili su tehničku podršku za građanske nuklearne projekte i ekonomsku pomoć, iako nijedna odmahšnja sankcija nije bila obećana. Dok ekonomska bol raste — s 80% iranskih prihoda vezanih za ulje, a novi europski embargo dolazi u srpnju — tlak na Teheran da se pomiri raste. Između zatvorenih vrata, visoki zvaničnici iz Europske unije i Irana završili su dvosjestrane razgovore, pripremajući put za završnu plenarnu sjednicu. article_content: After spending four years in self-imposed exile, former Pakistani president and military leader Pervez Musharraf has returned to Pakistan with a bold plan: to run in the country’s upcoming national elections. To shape public perception, he’s taken to social media, posting casual photos of himself working out, eating local food, and posing beside ornamental swords in his Karachi home. One caption reads: 'Starting my day with a workout. Feel very energized.' Another, featuring a bodyguard standing alert, declares: 'Taliban threat? NOT ON MY WATCH!!!' — a defiant nod to his controversial pro-U.S. stance after 9/11. At 69, Musharraf remains a polarizing figure. Militants despise him for aligning with Washington after the terrorist attacks, and many Pakistani lawyers still resent his 2007 decision to suspend the chief justice of the Supreme Court — a move that triggered nationwide protests. His return has been met with death threats, and just days after arriving, a lawyer hurled a shoe at him in a Karachi courthouse. Though the footwear missed its target, the gesture carried deep symbolic weight: in Muslim cultures, throwing shoes is a profound act of disrespect. Despite facing serious criminal charges — including complicity in the 2006 killing of Baloch leader Akbar Bugti and the 2007 assassination of former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto — Musharraf has been granted extended pre-emptive bail. Judges have given him 21 more days in the Bhutto and Bugti cases, and 15 additional days regarding his alleged illegal dismissal of judges. He is also under a travel ban. Meanwhile, his campaign imagery includes a photo with boxer Amir Khan and a selfie taken mid-flight back to Pakistan, captioned with pride: 'Pakistan First!'

article_content: The former home of Oscar G. Mayer Sr.—son of Oscar F. Mayer, founder of the Oscar Mayer Company—is now on the market for $1.75 million in Evanston, Illinois. The 1901 mansion spans 7,401 square feet, with six bedrooms and four bathrooms. Though many windows are boarded up and restoration is urgently needed, original features such as woodwork, staircases, a curved tower, and a ballroom remain intact. Oscar G. Mayer Sr. lived in the home from 1927 until his death in March 1965. The property is currently being sold by the estate of former resident Sigmund Eisenschenk, with court approval granted in autumn 2014. According to Krist Hartzell of the Evanston History Center, the home was designed by architects Hallburg & Sturm and is recognized as a local landmark. She expressed relief that the home is finally on the market, noting widespread community concern over its deterioration. The Oscar Mayer Company introduced its iconic Wienermobile in 1936 and launched its famous jingle, 'Oh, I'd love to be an Oscar Mayer wiener,' in 1963. Oscar G. Mayer Jr., his son, later became company chairman before retiring in 1977 and passing away in 2009.

article_content: The United Nations Security Council passed a resolution on Tuesday aimed at combating piracy along the Horn of Africa by allowing military forces to pursue pirates onto land in cases of 'hot pursuit.' Military forces from multiple countries, including the United States and France, are patrolling pirate-infested waters off Somalia, where attacks have surged this year. According to the International Maritime Bureau, nearly 100 vessels have been targeted, and almost 40 have been hijacked. The unanimous resolution expands existing counter-piracy measures by explicitly permitting national and regional forces to chase pirates into Somalia — the primary base for many attackers. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice attended the U.N. session and emphasized U.S. support for the resolution: 'I wouldn't be here seeking authorization to go ashore if the U.S. government — perhaps most importantly, the president of the United States — were not behind this resolution.' When asked if U.S. troops would soon conduct ground operations, Rice declined to speculate, stating, 'The United States is part of an international effort. We have naval forces involved. This resolution clarifies that the maritime boundary cannot serve as a safe haven for pirates. Decisions on hot pursuit will be made case by case.' Rice described piracy off Somalia as 'a symptom' of two decades of instability, poverty, and lawlessness, urging the U.N. to consider authorizing a peacekeeping operation. She noted recent attacks underscore the growing threat: 'Pirates endanger commerce, security, and above all, the principle of freedom of navigation.' Increased patrols have led to more frequent confrontations. In one recent incident, Indian officials captured 23 suspects allegedly attempting to hijack a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Aden. The Indian Navy also seized two small boats and a substantial cache of arms and equipment, including 12 Somali and 11 Yemeni nationals.
