article_content: Secret evidence implicating leading law firms and insurance companies in phone hacking, surveillance, and data theft is set to be examined by MPs. A confidential report submitted to the Leveson Inquiry into press standards reveals that hackers and private investigators were routinely paid to obtain sensitive information on individuals and corporations. Among the practices uncovered in the now-leaked Serious Organised Crime Agency (SOCA) report were live telephone interceptions, computer hacking, police corruption, and the illegal acquisition of itemised phone bills. The report suggests that 80% of phone hacking was carried out not by journalists, but by private investigators working for blue-chip companies, wealthy individuals, and even local councils. Keith Vaz, Chair of the Commons Home Affairs Select Committee, believes this evidence was deliberately withheld during a prior parliamentary investigation into private investigators. He plans to recall relevant witnesses. Lord Justice Leveson is under scrutiny for failing to mention these non-media abuses in his final 1,987-page report, despite being briefed on them. The report, dated 2008 and codenamed Project Riverside, was privately submitted to his inquiry but excluded from his conclusions. Firms such as Mishcon de Reya and Arnold & Porter are alleged to have hired agencies like Surrey-based Carratu, which subcontracted work to criminals Sharon and Stephen Anderson — later convicted of 55 violations of the Data Protection Act. Local authorities reportedly paid investigators to track down council tax, rent, and parking fine defaulters. One investigator allegedly used a bugging device installed by a BT-trained engineer to intercept landline calls. SOCA, which once styled itself as 'Britain’s FBI', reportedly took no action to stop the illegal trade, despite having documented it. The BBC did not report the leak in its main broadcasts or on its dedicated Leveson Inquiry webpage, despite extensive coverage of the inquiry itself. Critics argue that the lack of prosecution reflects systemic failures: penalties for such crimes remain minimal — often capped at £5,000 — despite offences carrying potential life sentences under charges like conspiracy to commit misconduct in a public office. Law firms, insurers, and public bodies claim ignorance, asserting they believed data was obtained legally — though many of their methods violated multiple statutes.
translated_content: Tajni dokazi koji uključuju vodeće pravne i osiguravajuće firme u hakiranju telefona, nadzoru i krađi podataka bit će istraživani od strane članova Parlamenta. Povjerenički izvještaj dostavljen Levesonovoj istrazi o standardima tiska otkriva da su hakeri i privatni detektivi redovito plaćani da dobiju osjetljive informacije o pojedincima i korporacijama. Među praksama otkrivenim u sada otkrivenom izvještaju Agencije za ozbiljni organizirani kriminal (SOCA) bile su žive slušanje telefonskih razgovora, hakiranje računala, korupcija policije i nezakonito sticanje detaljnih telefonskih računa. Izvještaj sugerira da je 80% hakiranja telefona obavljeno ne od strane novinara, već od privatnih detektiva koji su radili za velike kompanije, bogate pojedince i čak lokalne vlasti. Keith Vaz, predsjednik Odbora za unutrašnje poslove Komune, smatra da su ti dokazi namjerno sakriveni tijekom ranije parlamentarne istraže o privatnim detektivima. Planira pozvati odgovarajuće svjedoke. Gospodin sudac Leveson je pod optužbama zbog toga što nije spomenuo te ne-medijalne zloupotrebe u svom krajnjem, 1.987-straničnom izvještaju, iako je bio obaviješten o njima. Izvještaj, datiran 2008. godine i označen kao Projekt Riverside, bio je privatno dostavljen njegovoj istrazi, ali izostao je iz njegovih zaključaka. Firme poput Mishcon de Reya i Arnold & Porter navode se kao one koje su angažirale agencije poput Surrey-based Carratu, koja je dodjeljivala poslove kriminalcima Sharon i Stephen Anderson — kasnije osuđenima na 55 kršenja Zakona o zaštiti podataka. Lokalne vlasti su, prema izvještajima, plaćale detektive da prate one koji su dužnici poreza na nekretnine, najma i kazni za parkiranje. Jedan detektiv je, kako se tvrdi, koristio uređaj za sluskanje koji je instaliran od strane inženjera iz BT-a kako bi uhvatio pozive na stacionarnim telefonima. SOCA, koja se jednom nazivala 'britanski FBI', izgleda da nije poduzela nikakve mjere da zaustavi nezakonitu trgovinu, iako je dokumentirala tu praksu. BBC nije objavila otkrivanje u svojim glavnim emisijama niti na svojoj posebnoj web stranici posvećenoj istrazi o standardima medija, iako je detaljno pokrivala samu Levesonovu istražu. Kritičari tvrde da nedostatak progona otkriva sustavne propuste: kazne za takve zločine ostaju minimalne — često ograničene na 5.000 funti — iako bi takva djela mogla donijeti doživotnu kaznu po optužbi zločina zavjere za zloupotrebu javne službe. Pravne firme, osiguravajuće kuće i javne institucije tvrde da nisu znale, tvrdeći da su vjerovale da su podaci dobiveni legalno — iako su mnoge od njihove metode kršile više zakona.

article_content: A British judge has come under fire after publicly commending a convicted burglar for displaying 'courage' — remarks that triggered widespread condemnation and an official inquiry. Judge Peter Bowers, presiding over the case of 26-year-old Richard Rochford at Teesside Crown Court, opted not to impose a custodial sentence despite Rochford’s history of repeated offenses. Instead, he handed down a suspended 12-month prison term, telling Rochford: 'It takes a huge amount of courage to break into someone’s home. I wouldn’t have the nerve.' The comments, widely shared online, provoked outrage among victims’ groups, lawmakers, and even Rochford’s own mother, Caroline Whitehouse, who called the judge’s statement 'out of order' and 'shameful.' Prime Minister David Cameron, who has personally experienced two burglaries, responded on ITV, asserting unequivocally: 'Burglary is not bravery — it’s cowardice. It’s a hateful crime that leaves deep psychological scars.' Rochford, who admitted to a string of burglaries in February and had previously served three years for arson, later expressed remorse, revealing he was heavily dependent on valium at the time — taking 60 to 70 tablets daily. 'I don’t think burglary is courageous,' he said. 'I felt awful. I can barely remember doing it.' The Office for Judicial Complaints has opened an investigation into whether Judge Bowers’ statements breached judicial conduct standards. Conservative MP Philip Davies questioned how such views could persist within the judiciary. While the judge cited concerns about prison effectiveness, critics argue that normalizing criminal behavior undermines public trust and victim safety.

Sudac Peter Bowers, koji je vodio slučaj 26-godišnjeg Richarda Rochforda na Sudu za kaznena djela u Teessideu, odlučio je ne namijeniti zatvorsku kaznu, unatoč Rochfordovoj povijesti ponovljenih kršenja. Umjesto toga, dao mu je suspendiranu kaznu od 12 mjeseci, rekavši Rochfordu: 'Zahtijeva veliku hrabrost da se uđe u netrovu kuću. Ja ne bih imao hrabrosti.' Komentari, koji su se širili po internetu, izazvali su bijes među skupinama žrtava, zakonodavcima i čak i Rochfordovom majkom, Caroline Whitehouse, koja je nazvala sudčeve riječi 'neodgovarajućima' i 'sramotnim'. Premijer David Cameron, koji je osobno bio žrtva dviju krađa, odgovorio je na ITV-u, nedvosmisleno tvrdeći: 'Krađa nije hrabrost — to je strah. To je mrzovoljno kazneno djelo koje ostavlja duboke psihološke rane.' Rochford, koji je priznao niz krađa u veljači i ranije proveo tri godine u zatvoru zbog požara, kasnije je izrazio žaljenje, otkrivši da je tada bio teško ovisan o valijumu — uzimao je 60 do 70 tabletacija dnevno. 'Ne mislim da je krađa hrabro djelo,' rekao je. 'Osjećao sam se grozno. Gotovo se ne sjećam da sam to uopće učinio.' Ured za tužbe protiv sudaca pokrenuo je istraživanje o tome jesu li sudčeve izjave prekršile standarde sudskog ponašanja. Konzervativni zastupnik Philip Davies pitao je kako takvi pogledi mogu opstati u sudstvu. Iako je sudac naveo zabrinutost zbog učinkovitosti zatvora, kritičari tvrde da normalizacija kriminalnog ponašanja podkopava javno povjerenje i sigurnost žrtava.

article_content: By Jack Doyle, Home Affairs Correspondent. Last updated at 9:13 AM on 9 December 2011. Belgian police have warned that British border officials could face arrest if they attempt to stop migrants traveling on Eurostar trains bound for London — even if those travelers hold tickets only to Lille. This practice, known as the 'Lille Loophole,' allows hundreds of migrants to evade UK border controls by exploiting a gap in the Schengen Area’s free-movement rules. Migrants purchase inexpensive tickets — sometimes as low as £23 — from Brussels to Lille, enabling them to bypass UK immigration checks at the Brussels Eurostar terminal. Once aboard, they remain on the train past Lille, traveling undetected through the Channel Tunnel to London, where passport inspections are rare. Belgian authorities maintain that detaining or questioning passengers with valid Lille tickets violates the Schengen Agreement, which permits unrestricted travel within participating EU nations. One Belgian officer reportedly told a UK official: 'This has got to stop. You are not in Britain now, you are in Schengen. If they make a complaint, you will be arrested.' UK Border Agency figures reveal a sharp rise in the use of this route: 80 migrants were caught in the first six months of 2011, compared to 240 in the following five months — up from just 14 in all of 2010. Officials believe the actual number is far higher, as only detected cases are recorded. There are growing fears that the loophole could be exploited by terrorists or human traffickers, with some officers reporting up to 20 suspicious passengers on a single train. One officer also alleged that Belgian police may be using the loophole to remove migrants from Brussels streets — though this claim has not been independently verified. UK Immigration Minister Damian Green confirmed that the government is actively negotiating with Belgian authorities and Eurostar to close the loophole. The Belgian government has so far declined to comment.

Ova praksa, poznata kao 'Lille šprica', omogućuje stotinama migranata da izbjegnu britanske granične kontrole iskorištavanjem praznine u pravilima slobodnog kretanja Schengenske zone. Migranti kupuju jeftine karte — ponekad za samo 23 funte — iz Bruxellesa u Lille, što ih omogućuje da preskoče britanske carinske kontrole na Eurostar terminalu u Bruxellesu. Jednom kad uđu u vlak, ostaju na njemu nakon Lilla, putujući neprimijećeno kroz Kanalski tunel do Londona, gdje su provjere pasoša rijetke. Belgijske vlasti tvrde da zadržavanje ili ispitivanje putnika s važećim kartama za Lille krši Schengenski sporazum, koji dopušta neograničeno kretanje unutar sudionika EU-a. Jedan belgijski oficir je izvještavao kako je rekao britanskom službeniku: 'Ovo mora prestati. Vi više niste u Britaniji, vi ste u Schengenu. Ako podnesete žalbu, bit ćete arrestirani.' Podaci Britanske agencije za granice pokazuju oštar porast korištenja ovog puta: 80 migranata uhvaćeno je u prvih šest mjeseci 2011., usporedo s 240 u sljedećih pet mjeseci — od samo 14 u cijeloj 2010. godini. Službenici vjeruju da je stvarni broj mnogo veći, jer se bilježe samo uhvaćeni slučajevi. Rastuće su brige da bi ovaj propust mogao biti iskorišten od strane terorista ili ljudskih trgovaca, s nekim službenicima koji izvještavaju o do 20 sumnjivih putnika na jednom vlaku. Jedan službenik je također tvrdio da belgijska policija može koristiti ovaj propust kako bi uklonila migrante s ulica Bruxellesa — iako ova tvrdnja nije neovisno potvrđena. Britanski ministar za imigraciju Damian Green potvrdio je da vlada aktivno pregovara s belgijskim vlastima i Eurostarom kako bi zatvorila ovaj propust. Belgijska vlada je do sada odbila komentirati.

article_content: Nine months after the disappearance of 16-year-old Anne Hill from Edmond, Oklahoma, her body remains unrecovered despite an intensive search effort. In October, authorities charged 16-year-old Chadd Raymond with first-degree murder and 17-year-old Chloe Marie Thomas with being an accessory to murder. However, prosecutors later dropped charges against Thomas pending proceedings in juvenile court. According to investigators, Thomas stated that Raymond killed Anne during a movie night at either her or Raymond’s home, then, with her help, placed the body in the back seat of Anne’s white Chevrolet and transported it to a wooded, rural area in Edmond — though she cannot recall the precise location. Raymond has pleaded not guilty and denies all allegations. Anne was last seen on April 12, after telling her mother she was going to watch a movie at a friend’s house. She never returned. Her car was found a week later in an Edmond neighborhood, abandoned and untouched. She had recently received the keys to the vehicle and had been upset about a strict curfew, leading her to stop answering her phone that night. Her mother, Lori Hill, described Anne as 'vivacious, outgoing, never met a stranger' — emphasizing that she was not the type to run away. A heartfelt voicemail left by Lori still plays on Anne’s phone: 'Anne, I hope that’s you... I’ll come get you wherever you are.' To aid in the search, the family enlisted private investigator Darcie Scoon, coordinator of the Center for Search and Investigation. So far, volunteers have combed through over 2,000 rural acres and traveled more than 200 miles without success. Scoon has released a detailed map identifying high-priority search zones based on Thomas’s descriptions: areas near highways (within 5 miles), with wooded perimeters, oil or pump sites in open fields, and nearby white structures such as houses. Some locations also feature natural or man-made rock formations. Sunday marked what would have been Anne’s 17th birthday. Her family continues to plead for public assistance — not just to bring closure, but so Anne can be laid to rest with dignity.
translated_content: Devet mjeseci nakon nestajanja 16-godišnje Anne Hill iz Edmonda, Oklahoma, njezino tijelo ostaje nepronađeno, unatoč intenzivnim traganjima. U listopadu su vlasti optužile 16-godišnjeg Chadda Raymond za ubistvo prve stupnja i 17-godišnju Chloe Marie Thomas kao pomagača u ubistvu. Međutim, tužilaštvo je kasnije povuklo optužbe protiv Thomas zbog čekanja na postupak u sudu za maloljetnike. Prema istraživačima, Thomas je izjavila da je Raymond ubio Anne tijekom gledanja filma kod nje ili kod Raymond-a, a zatim, uz njenu pomoć, stavio tijelo na zadnje sjedalo Anne-inog bijelog Chevroleta i prevezao ga u šumovitu, ruralnu lokaciju u Edmondu — iako ne može sjetiti se točnog mjesta. Raymond je priznao nevinost i odbija sve optužbe. Anne je posljednji put viđena 12. travnja, nakon što je rekla majci da ide gledati film kod prijatelja. Nikada se nije vratila. Njezin auto je pronađen tjedan dana kasnije u Edmondu, napušten i nepromijenjen. Nedavno je dobila ključeve od tog automobila i bila je ljuta zbog stroge zakazane dobi, pa je prestala odgovarati na telefon te noći. Njezina majka, Lori Hill, opisala je Anne kao 'živahnu, izlaznu, nikad nije upoznala stranca' — naglašavajući da nije tip djevojke koja bi pobjegla. Srce grabeći glasovni poruka koju je Lori ostavila na Anne-inom telefonu još se svira: 'Anne, nadam se da si ti... Doći ću te dobiti gdje god si.' Da bi pomogli u traženju, obitelj je angažirala privatnu istražiteljicu Darcie Scoon, koordinatoricu Centra za pretragu i istraživanje. Do sada su volonteri pregledali preko 2.000 ruralnih hektara i prešli više od 200 milja bez uspjeha. Scoon je objavila detaljan kartu koji identificira prioritetne zone za pretragu temeljene na Thomas-inim opisima: područja blizu cesta (unutar 5 milja), s šumovitim rubovima, uljnim ili pumpanim lokacijama na otvorenom terenu i nedalekim bijelim građevinama poput kuća. Neka mjesta također imaju prirodne ili umjetne stijenske formacije. Nedjelja je označila dan koji bi bio njezini 17. rođendan. Njezina obitelj nastavlja moliti javnost za pomoć — ne samo kako bi došla do zaključka, već i kako bi Anne mogla biti sahranjena s dostojanstvom.

article_content: Marcos Rojo’s girlfriend, Eugenia Lusardo, has posted a heartfelt message on Instagram suggesting that the Argentina defender’s move to Manchester United is imminent. The 24-year-old has been a key target for manager Louis van Gaal this summer. Rojo previously described joining United as a 'dream' and expressed deep admiration for Van Gaal. On Tuesday, Lusardo shared a photo of the couple with the caption: 'Congratulations on this new stage of your life. We love you greatly and we are always with you. You deserve this and much more.' Rojo, known for his extensive tattoos, bears several meaningful designs: 'Pride' on his right leg, 'Glory' on his left, 'For My Family' across his chest, and a tribute to Estudiantes de la Plata and their 2009 Copa Libertadores victory. In an interview with Argentina’s Continental radio station — widely cited in national media — Rojo said: 'It’s a dream to play for Manchester United. I’m very proud of the opportunity to work with Louis van Gaal. I spoke with Juan Sebastián Verón about United during our time at Estudiantes. I’ve always admired English football and believe I’ll adapt easily.' The transfer has faced complications due to a dispute between Sporting Lisbon and a third-party ownership entity. Rojo briefly refused to train in an attempt to expedite the move but later apologized, stating: 'There was a misunderstanding. I never wanted to do anything wrong at Sporting — I’ve always been grateful for the chances they gave me to play in Europe. If I made a mistake, I’ve apologized. I didn’t want to hurt anyone at the club.'
translated_content: Djevica Marcosa Roja, Eugenia Lusardo, objavila je srdačnu poruku na Instagramu kojom sugerira da se premještanje argentinjskog branitelja u Manchester United približava. 24-godišnjak je bio ključni cilj trenera Louisa van Gaala ovog ljetnjega tranzferskog perioda. Rojo je ranije opisao pridruživanje Unitedu kao 'san' i izrazio duboko poštovanje prema Van Gaalu. U utorak je Lusardo objavila fotografiju para s natpisom: 'Čestitke na ovoj novoj fazi života. Volimo te vrlo i uvijek smo s tobom. Zaslužuješ ovo i još više.' U intervjuu s argentinskom radijskom postajom Continental — široko citiranom u nacionalnim medijima — Rojo je rekao: 'San je igrati za Manchester United. article_content: Despite widespread reports claiming Robert Plant turned down a half-billion-pound deal to reunite Led Zeppelin, his publicist has firmly denied the story, calling it 'rubbish.' According to the UK’s Daily Mirror, Plant was reportedly offered £500 million ($800 million) for a full-band reunion, with fellow members Jimmy Page and John Paul Jones said to be ready to join. Jason Bonham, stepping in for his late father John Bonham, was also reportedly prepared to participate. The proposal, allegedly made by Virgin Group founder Richard Branson—a longtime fan—would have included concerts in London, Berlin, and New Jersey, with Branson offering private jet travel and potential future shows. The Mirror claimed that when Plant took 48 hours to consider before rejecting the offer—and reportedly tearing up the contract—it left everyone stunned, as the reunion was seen as impossible without him. But Plant’s representative clarified to the Guardian that these claims are entirely unfounded. Led Zeppelin disbanded in 1980 after John Bonham’s tragic death, though they did reunite once for a tribute concert in 2007 honoring Atlantic Records’ Ahmet Ertegun. Since then, Plant has distanced himself from the band’s legacy, focusing instead on his solo project, the Sensational Shape Shifters, and his latest album, 'Lullaby and... the Ceaseless Roar.' In interviews, including one with Rolling Stone, he’s openly criticized the endless cycle of Zeppelin nostalgia, saying, 'This propagation of myths and anti-myths will continue forever.' Meanwhile, Jimmy Page has also stated plainly: 'I don’t see it.'
translated_content: Iako su široko prijavljene vijesti da je Robert Plant odbio ugovor od pola milijarde funti za ponovno ujedinjenje Led Zeppelina, njegov je pravnik priču odbio, nazivajući je 'glupostima.' Prema britanskom Daily Mirroru, Plantu je, prema izvještajima, ponuđeno 500 milijuna funti (800 milijuna dolara) za puno ponovno ujedinjenje s ostalim članovima bendu – Jimmyjem Pageom i John Paul Jonesom – koji su, prema izvorima, bili spremni pridružiti se. Jason Bonham, sin kasnog bubnjara Johna Bonhama, također je, prema izvještajima, bio spreman sudjelovati. Ponuda, koja se navodi da je potekla od Richarda Bransona, osnivača Virgin Grupa – dugogodišnjeg obožavatelja grupe – trebala bi uključivati koncerte u Londonu, Berlinu i New Jerseyju, uz Bransonovu ponudu privatnog aviona i potencijalnih dodatnih nastupa. Daily Mirror je tvrdio da je, kad je Plant tražio 48 sati da razmisli prije nego što je odbio ponudu – i prema izvještajima raztrgao ugovor – svi su bili u šoku, jer se smatralo da je ponovno ujedinjenje nemoguće bez njega. Ali Plantov predstavnik je Guardianu pojasnio da su ove tvrdnje potpuno neosnovane. Led Zeppelin je prestao s radom 1980. godine nakon tragične smrti Johna Bonhama, iako su se jednom ponovno ujedinili za nadmemorijalni koncert 2007. godine u čast Ahmeta Erteguna, osnivača Atlantic Recordsa. Od tada se Plant udaljio od nasljeđa benda, fokusirajući se umjesto toga na svoj solistički projekt, Sensational Shape Shifters, te na svoj najnoviji album, 'Lullaby and... the Ceaseless Roar.' U intervijima, uključujući jedan sa Rolling Stoneom, otvoreno je kritizirao beskrajnu ciklus Led Zeppelin nostalgije, rekavši: 'Ova propagacija mitova i anti-mitova će trajati zauvijek.' Međutim, Jimmy Page je također jasno izjavio: 'Ne vidim to.'

article_content: In the midst of the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, people with disabilities in Gaza are enduring devastating consequences that go largely unnoticed by the world. Many cannot hear approaching airstrikes, lack functioning wheelchairs after they broke during chaotic evacuations, or are trapped in overcrowded shelters without medical care. One 60-year-old woman spends her days lying on a blanket because her wheelchair was destroyed — there's no replacement. On October 7, Hamas launched a deadly assault on southern Israel, killing around 1,400 and seizing over 200 hostages. In response, Israel initiated intense aerial bombardments and later a ground offensive across Gaza, resulting in more than 9,000 deaths, according to local health authorities. Yet even amid this carnage, aid that does enter Gaza rarely reaches those most vulnerable — especially the estimated 210,000 displaced people with disabilities. Hospitals, overwhelmed and under-resourced, lack sterile beds, oxygen, and basic supplies. Ulcers, infections, and untreated chronic conditions are spreading rapidly. Human Rights Watch interviewed 13 disabled Gazans in early November, revealing harrowing stories: a deaf sister who only knows bombs are falling when the ground shakes; a man who lost both legs in 2008 and now fears dying if his hospital is hit because he can't move. Power outages have rendered electric wheelchairs, hearing aids, and ventilators useless. Families fleeing have abandoned critical medications and mobility tools. Advocates like Reham Shaheen, a rehabilitation specialist stranded in Jordan, say these problems existed long before the war — the 16-year blockade made life difficult for disabled Palestinians, and now it’s become a death sentence. Ziad Amro, a blind activist in the West Bank, says daily communication with Gaza’s disabled community reveals total isolation — no food, water, internet, or phones. The U.N. and global powers have been slow to act. While the U.S. president recently called for a temporary pause in fighting to allow aid through, no major nation has demanded a full ceasefire. Shaheen insists the top priorities now are ending the violence and ensuring humanitarian assistance includes assistive devices and trained personnel who understand disability needs. Without this, she warns, entire populations will vanish from the record — forgotten in plain sight.
translated_content: U sredini trajnog sukoba između Izraela i Hamasa, ljudi sa invaliditetom u Gazi trpe ogromne posljedice koje ostaju uglavnom nepažljene od strane svijeta. Mnogi ne mogu čuti nadleće zračne napade, nemaju funkcionirajuće kolicie nakon što su se slomile tijekom haotičnih evakuacija ili su zarobljeni u prepunim skloništima bez medicinske njege. Jedna 60-godišnja žena provodi dane ležeći na pokrivaču jer joj je kolicie uništene — nema zamjene. 7. listopada Hamas je pokrenuo smrtonosni napad na južni Izrael, ubivši oko 1.400 ljudi i uzimajući preko 200 talaca. U odgovor, Izrael je pokrenuo intenzivne zračne napade, a kasnije i kopnenu ofanzivu cijelom Gazom, što je rezultiralo više od 9.000 smrtnih slučajeva, prema lokalnim zdravstvenim vlastima. Međutim, čak i u sredini ove katastrofe, pomoć koja ulazi u Gazu rijetko dostiže one koji su najranjiviji — posebno procijenjenih 210.000 internirano pomaknutih ljudi s invaliditetom. Bolnice, preopterećene i siromašne resursima, nemaju sterilne krevete, kisik ni osnovne opreme. Rane, infekcije i neliječeni kronični uvjeti brzo se šire. Human Rights Watch je intervjuirao 13 osoba s invaliditetom u ranom studenom, otkrivajući užasne priče: slijepa sestra koja zna da padaju bombe samo kad se zemlja tresne; muškarac koji je izgubio oba noge 2008. godine i sada se boji da će umrijeti ako mu je bolnica bombardirana jer ne može da se pomakne. Isključenja struje učinila su električna kolicie, slušalice i ventilatore neupotrebljivima. Obitelji koje bijegu ostavile su kritične lijekove i pomoćna sredstva. Praktičari poput Reham Shaheen, specijaliste za rehabilitaciju zarobljene u Jordaniu, kažu da su ovi problemi postojali i prije rata — 16-godišnja blokada je činila život težim za palestinske osobe s invaliditetom, a sada je postala smrtna presuda. Ziad Amro, slijepi aktivista s Zapadne obale, kaže da dnevna komunikacija s zajednicom osoba s invaliditetom u Gazi otkriva potpunu izolaciju — nema hrane, vode, interneta ni telefona. Ujedinjeni narodi i globalne vlasti sporo djeluju. Iako je američki predsjednik nedavno pozvao na privremenu pauzu u borbi kako bi se omogućila pomoć, nijedna velika nacija nije tražila potpuni prestanak vatre. Shaheen insistira da su najvažniji prioriteti sada prestanak nasilja i osiguranje da humanitarna pomoć uključuje pomoćna sredstva i osoblje obučeno za pomoć osobama s invaliditetom. Bez toga, upozorava, cijele populacije će nestati iz zapisa — zaboravljene na otvorenom.

article_content: Ever dreamed of renting out an entire private island for your family and friends? Sir Richard Branson’s iconic Necker Island in the British Virgin Islands is back on the rental market — with a price tag of just $60,000 per night for up to 30 adults and six children. The island’s centerpiece, the Great House, was destroyed in August 2011 when lightning struck during a storm, triggering a devastating fire. Actress Kate Winslet made headlines by helping rescue Branson’s elderly mother from the flames. Though the island has been open to renters since the fire, its capacity was reduced until recently. After a two-year reconstruction, the new Great House faithfully mirrors the original design and now serves once again as the social heart of the island — featuring a master suite, eight guest bedrooms, and a bunk room for up to six children. Scattered across Necker Island are six individual one-bedroom Bali Houses, offering serene privacy. All stays include luxurious amenities: gourmet meals and unlimited beverages (alcoholic and non-alcoholic), private boat transfers from Virgin Gorda or Beef Island (Tortola) airports, water sports, tennis, a freshwater pool, and a spacious Jacuzzi. For those who don’t need the whole island, Branson offers 'Celebration Weeks' — a chance to book individual rooms hotel-style for seven nights (or sometimes less, depending on availability). 'Necker Island has been my home for over 30 years,' Branson said. 'It’s the most beautiful place in the world. The new Great House is its beating heart — and I couldn’t be happier with how it turned out.'

Centralni objekt otoka, Velika kuća, uništen je u kolovozu 2011. kada je grom pogodio tijekom oluje i izazvao opsežan požar. article_content: (CNN) — Fulham became the sixth soccer team in England's Premier League to come under U.S. ownership when charismatic owner Mohamed Al Fayed sold the club to billionaire and NFL owner Shahid Khan. The deal, long anticipated, was confirmed on Fulham’s website on Friday. Although the selling price was not officially disclosed, multiple British media outlets reported it exceeded $225 million. Fulham stated that Khan now holds full ownership of the Cottagers, debt-free as of today. "It has been a pleasure and privilege to serve as Chairman of Fulham Football Club for 16 unforgettable years," said 84-year-old Al Fayed on the club’s website. "I am delighted to pass this great and historic club into the care of an outstanding man who has already achieved so much—and who I am confident will take Fulham to even greater heights. Through hard work, vision, and determination, Shahid Khan embodies the American success story. His accomplishments speak for themselves. I met him twice before finalizing this transaction and was deeply impressed." Al Fayed purchased Fulham in 1997 for approximately $9 million and invested roughly $300 million into the southwest London-based club, located near Harrods—the luxury department store he previously owned before selling it to Qatar Holdings for an estimated $2.3 billion in 2010. Though never competing for the Premier League title, Fulham secured its place in the world’s most-watched league after promotion from the second tier in 2001 and reached the Europa League final in 2010. Training facilities were upgraded, Craven Cottage was renovated, and the club received approval to expand its stadium capacity to 30,000. During his tenure, Al Fayed endured profound personal loss: the death of his son Dodi in the 1997 car crash that also claimed the life of Princess Diana. He remained unapologetically distinctive—commissioning a statue of his friend Michael Jackson after the singer’s 2009 death and placing it outside Craven Cottage. While some fans disapproved, Al Fayed stood by his decision. He now plans to retire and spend more time with his grandchildren. "I am sad but proud of what we’ve accomplished," Al Fayed said. "I am deeply grateful to Fulham’s fans—the most incredible in the world—who have shown me unwavering support at every home game. I would never let them down. I’ve entrusted the club to a talented, honest, and highly capable man who respects Fulham’s traditions. He is a true sportsman." According to Forbes, Khan, born in Pakistan, was worth $2.9 billion as of last March. He moved to the U.S. at age 16 to study at the University of Illinois, became a U.S. citizen, and built his fortune through Flex-N-Gate, an automotive parts manufacturer that generated $3.9 billion in sales in 2012. Khan acquired the Jacksonville Jaguars two years ago; the team will play a regular-season game in London for the next four seasons. U.S. ownership in the Premier League has had mixed results—think George Gillett and Tom Hicks at Liverpool—but Fulham fans remain hopeful. Other American-owned clubs include Manchester United, Arsenal, Aston Villa, Sunderland, and Liverpool (now under John Henry). "Fulham is the perfect club at the perfect time for me," said Khan, in his early 60s. "I don’t see myself merely as the owner—I see myself as a custodian of the club on behalf of its fans. My priority is ensuring Fulham and Craven Cottage have a sustainable, thriving future in the Premier League that generations of supporters can be proud of. We will manage finances and operations with prudence, placing youth development and community programs at the core of Fulham’s future." Fulham’s first league match under Khan’s ownership is an away fixture against Sunderland on August 17.

Ugovor, koji je bio u tijeku, potvrđen je na web stranici Fulhama u petak. Iako je cijena prodaje navedena, više britanskih medija izvještavalo je da je premašila 225 milijuna dolara. Fulham je naveo da je Khan sada potpuni vlasnik Cottagersa, bez dugova, od danas. "Bilo mi je zadovoljstvo i čast biti predsjednik Fulham Football kluba tijekom 16 nezaboravnih godina," rekao je 84-godišnji Al Fayed na web stranici kluba. "Sada sam oduševljen što ovaj veliki i povijesni klub predajem brigi i vodstvu izvanrednog čovjeka koji je već postigao mnogo i koji, siguran sam, će Fulham dovesti do još većih uspjeha. Kroz težak rad, viziju i određenost, Shahid Khan je živa ilustracija američke priče o uspjehu. Njegovi dostignuća govore same za sebe. Sreo sam ga dvaput prije nego što smo zaključili ovu transakciju i vrlo sam dobro utisnut." Al Fayed je kupio Fulham 1997. godine za približno 9 milijuna dolara i uložio oko 300 milijuna dolara u klub smješten u jugozapadnom Londonu, nedaleko od Harrodsa — luksuzne i ikonične londonske trgovine koju je Al Fayed ranije vlasnik prije nego što ju je prodao Qatar Holdings-u za procijenjenih 2,3 milijarde dolara 2010. godine. Iako nikada nije natjecao za naslov Premijer lige, Fulham je osigurao svoje mjesto u najgledanijoj ligi na svijetu nakon promocije iz druge razine 2001. godine i stigao do finale Europske lige 2010. godine. Treningi su poboljšani, Craven Cottage je obnovljen, a klub je dobio dopuštenje da poveća kapacitet stadiona na 30.000 mjesta. Tijekom njegovog razdoblja, Al Fayed je doživio duboki lični gubitak: smrt njegovog sina Dodi-ja u auto nesreći koja je također uzela život princice Diane 1997. godine. On je ostao neželjen u svojim odlukama — naručio je kip Michaela Jacksona — svog prijatelja — nakon što je pjevač umro 2009. godine i postavio ga van Craven Cottagea, koji se nalazi na obali rijeki Temze. Neki navijači nisu voljeli to, ali Al Fayed nije brinuo. Sada planira provesti više vremena s svojima unucima u penziji. "Žalim, ali ponosan sam na naše postignuće," rekao je Al Fayed. "Duboko sam zahvalan navijačima Fulhama — najdivljim navijačima na svijetu. Dali su mi podršku i ljubaznost kad god sam ih vidio na domaćim utakmicama. Nikada ih ne bih prevario. Predao sam klub talentiranom, poštenom i vrlo sposobnom čovjeku koji poštuje Fulham i njegove tradicije. On je veliki sportista." Prema Forbesu, Khan, rođen u Pakistaniu, bio je vrijedan 2,9 milijarde dolara u ožujku prošle godine. Otišao je u SAD u dobi od 16 godina da studira na Sveučilištu Illinois, postao je američki državljanin i izgradio je svoje bogatstvo kroz Flex-N-Gate, proizvođač automobilskih dijelova koji je generirao prodaju od 3,9 milijarde dolara 2012. godine. Khan je kupio Jacksonville Jaguars prije dvije godine, a tim će igrati utakmicu u Londonu sljedeće četiri godine. Američko vlasništvo u Premijer ligi imalo je različite rezultate — pomislite na Georgea Gilletta i Toma Hicksa na Liverpulu — ali navijači Fulhama ostaju optimistični. Ostale ekipa u Premijer ligi koje trenutačno vlasnici Amerikanci su Manchester United, Arsenal, Aston Villa, Sunderland i Liverpool, a zadnji je sada pod Johnom Henrijem. "Fulham je savršeni klub u savršeno vrijeme za mene," rekao je Khan, u ranoj šezdesetoj, na web stranici Fulhama. "Želim biti jasan, ne vidim sebe kao vlasnika Fulhama, već kao čuvara kluba u ime njegovih navijača. Moj prioritet je osigurati da klub i Craven Cottage imaju održivu i trajnu budućnost u Premijer ligi koju će navijači trenutnih i budućih generacija moći ponositi. Upravit ćemo financijskim i operativnim poslovima oprezno i pažljivo, stavljajući razvoj mladih i zajedničke programe kao temeljne elemente budućnosti Fulhama." Prva liga utakmica Fulhama u novoj sezoni pod Khanom je vanjska utakmica protiv Sunderlanda 17. kolovoza.

article_content: Kurdish and Iraqi forces have claimed to have regained control of the Mosul Dam — Iraq’s largest — from ISIS militants who seized it less than two weeks ago, according to an army spokesman in Baghdad. The dam, situated on the Tigris River just north of Mosul, is a critical infrastructure asset supplying water and electricity to much of northern Iraq. Its recapture would mark the first major territorial gain for anti-ISIS forces since U.S.-led airstrikes began earlier this month. However, ISIS has denied the claim, asserting it still holds the dam in a statement posted on a militant-affiliated website. The dam’s strategic importance lies not only in its utility but also in the catastrophic consequences its potential collapse could cause — threatening millions of civilians and U.S. diplomatic facilities in Baghdad. Amid the conflict, two British citizens have drawn international attention: Mohammed Abdullah, a takeaway shop owner from Liverpool, and Saman Baqu, a resident of Leeds who has lived in the UK for 12 years. Both traveled to Iraq to fight alongside Kurdish Peshmerga forces. In interviews, Abdullah expressed deep personal commitment, stating, 'I don’t care if I get killed or not... I’m here for Kurdistan, for my family.' According to Iraqi Lt. Gen. Qassim al-Moussawi, Iraqi and Kurdish troops raised the Iraqi flag over the dam on Monday and have secured its core structure. However, heavy fighting continues on the southern side, and at least 170 explosive devices have been defused — with many more believed to remain. A senior Kurdish commander, speaking anonymously, later reported that Peshmerga forces had temporarily withdrawn due to extensive minefields. The U.S. military has not confirmed direct participation in the ground operation but acknowledged conducting multiple airstrikes in the region in recent days. The White House stated the air campaign aims to prevent dam failure and protect U.S. personnel, underscoring the dam’s national security implications. Since June, ISIS’s rapid advance has displaced approximately 1.5 million Iraqis, triggering a UN emergency response. The Mosul Dam’s fate remains pivotal — not only militarily, but as a symbol of resilience amid a deepening humanitarian catastrophe.

article_content: New York (CNN) — An airport security supervisor accused of stealing from passengers and accepting bribes was granted $100,000 bail Wednesday by a U.S. magistrate judge in federal court in Newark, New Jersey. Michael Arato, 41, is seen on surveillance video at Newark Liberty International Airport, according to a federal criminal complaint. The video has not been publicly released. Arato, of Ewing, New Jersey, faces one count of accepting bribes, one count of conspiracy to commit theft, and three counts of theft by a government employee. He appeared in court handcuffed and with ankle restraints. As a supervisory transportation security officer for the TSA at Terminal B, Arato allegedly worked with a colleague to steal from passengers, particularly those departing on the 6:20 p.m. Air India flight from the B-3 checkpoint. Beginning in August 2009, the TSA and the Port Authority Police Department received numerous complaints from passengers — predominantly non-English-speaking women of Indian descent returning home after visiting the U.S. — reporting missing cash and valuables after their bags were hand-searched. Authorities launched an investigation, including covert surveillance. Arato reportedly told investigators he had considered harming himself, though his defense attorney stated he was not a flight risk and had 'too much to live for.' The colleague, who began cooperating with authorities in September 2010, admitted to stealing $400 to $700 daily from passengers since around October 2009 and sharing half with Arato. Arato also stole independently, occasionally giving portions to his accomplice. Between September 13 and October 5, Arato received $3,100 from the colleague. In recorded conversations, Arato expressed no remorse, saying, 'They’re leaving this country with our money.' On August 31, 2010, Arato stole $400 from a woman of Indian descent, later falsely claiming another officer had found the money and returned it. The co-schemer, aware the theft was unreported, alerted Arato via phone. Video footage shows Arato accepting $500 from the colleague on September 29 — laughing as he slipped the cash into his shirt pocket — and later giving the middle finger to a security camera. On October 5, after being instructed to confirm a passenger had departed without noticing the theft, Arato accepted $900. Authorities searched him that day and found $1,300 in his pocket. $1,100 matched serial numbers from money given to the co-schemer by law enforcement that day; another $100 matched prior funds. Arato admitted spending $100 on groceries. Since 2003, 162 TSA employees have been terminated for theft-related offenses. The agency emphasized that this number represents a tiny fraction of its workforce and reaffirmed its zero-tolerance policy. 'It’s sad that the reprehensible conduct of a few individuals threatens to tarnish the 50,000 honest, hard-working folks from all walks of life whose patriotism ensures the security of millions of people every single day,' said TSA spokesman Nicholas Kimball.
translated_content: New York (CNN) — Nadzornik sigurnosti zračne luke optužen za krađu od putnika i prihvaćanje mita dobio je novčanu jamnicu od 100.000 dolara u srijedu od strane saveznog sudije u federalnom sudu u Newarku, New Jersey. Michael Arato, 41 godina, vidi se na snimkama nadzora na Zračnoj luci Newark Liberty, prema saveznoj krivičnoj tužbi. Snimke nisu objavljene. Arato, iz Ewingu, New Jersey, optužen je za jedno kazneno djelo prihvaćanja mita, jedno kazneno djelo zloporabe u svrhu krađe i tri kaznena djela krađe od strane službenika vlade. Pojavio se pred sudom u rukama i s ograničenjima na nogama. Kao nadzornik transportne sigurnosti za TSA na Terminalu B, Arato je sumnjiv da je surađivao s kolegom da bi krao od putnika, posebno onih koji su odlazili na let Air India u 18:20 s B-3 kontrolne točke. Od kolovoza 2009., TSA i Policijska uprava Port Authority New York i New Jersey primili su brojne pritužbe od putnika — uglavnom neengleski govornih žena indijskog podrijetla i nacionalnosti koje su se vraćale kući nakon posjeta SAD-u — koje su prijavile nestanak novca i drugih vrijednosti nakon ručnog pretraživanja njihovih prtljaga od strane TSA zaposlenika. Vlasti su pokrenule istragu, uključujući skrivenu nadzornu opremu. Arato je prema izvještaju rekao istražiteljima da je razmišljao o samoubojstvu, iako je njegov odvjetnik za javnu branu rekao da nije rizik za bijeg i da ima 'previše za što živjeti.' Kolega, koji je počeo surađivati s vlastima u rujnu 2010., priznao je da je svaki dan krao 400 do 700 dolara od putnika od otprilike listopada 2009. i dijelio polovicu s Aratom. Arato je također sam krao, ponekad dajući dijelove svom pomagaču. Između 13. rujna i 5. listopada, Arato je primio 3.100 dolara od kolege. U snimljenim razgovorima, Arato nije pokazivao žalost, kažući: 'Ostavljaju ovu zemlju s našim novcem.' 31. kolovoza 2010., Arato je ukrao 400 dolara od žene indijskog podrijetla, a kasnije lažno tvrdio da je drugi službenik pronašao novac i vratio ga. Kolega, koji je znao da ta krađa nije bila prijavljena, obavijestio je Aratu putem mobitela. Snimke pokazuju kako je Arato prihvatio 500 dolara od kolege 29. rujna — smijući se dok je ubacio novac u džep košulje — a kasnije pokazao srednji prst na vidljivu sigurnosnu kameru. 5. listopada, nakon što je dobio naredbu da potvrdi da je putnik otišao bez primijetio da mu je novac nestao, Arato je prihvatio 900 dolara. Vlasti su izvršile pretragu tog dana i pronašle 1.300 dolara u njegovom džepu. 1.100 dolara odgovaralo je serijskim brojevima novca koji su vlasti dale kolegi taj dan; još 100 dolara odgovaralo je novcu koji su dali kolegi dan ranije. Arato je priznao da je 100 dolara potrošio na hranu. Od 2003. godine, 162 zaposlenika TSA-a otpušteno je zbog kaznenih djela vezanih uz krađu. Agencija je naglasila da taj broj predstavlja mali udio ukupnog broja zaposlenika i ponovno potvrdila svoju politiku nulte tolerancije. 'Žao mi je što se neprihvatljivo ponašanje nekoliko pojedinaca može odraziti na 50.000 poštenih, posvećenih ljudi iz svih slojeva društva čija pripadnost osigurava sigurnost milijuna ljudi svaki dan,' rekao je predstavnik TSA-a Nicholas Kimball.

article_content: This week, the Science Museum is hosting the International Living Machines conference — a global gathering where robots don’t just mimic humans, but entire ecosystems. From robots with mouse-like whiskers to humanoid dancers and machines powered by slime mould, the event reveals how nature is reshaping the future of technology. Led by the University of Sheffield, researchers from around the world are presenting biohybrid systems that fuse living organisms with mechanical parts. One standout is the BIOTACT sensor — a set of artificial whiskers modeled after those of shrews, allowing robots to navigate by touch alone. Nearby, a tiny robot shrew, called Shrewbot, tracks a moving target using only its tactile senses, proving precision doesn’t always require sight. At the heart of innovation is Tacitip, an artificial fingertip developed at Bristol Robotics Lab that replicates the complex deformation patterns of human skin during touch. Meanwhile, the HyQ robot — a 70kg, dog-sized quadruped from Italy — moves with astonishing fluidity, mimicking the gait of real mammals. But perhaps the most startling exhibits are the biohybrids. One installation features a robotic head whose expressions are driven by slime mould — a single-celled organism capable of learning and memory. As the mould responds to light and food, the robot mirrors its behavior, blurring the line between organic intelligence and programmed response. Humanoid robots like Robothespian and iCub take interaction further. Robothespian, built by Engineered Arts, converses in multiple languages, reads poetry with emotion, and even copies human gestures. iCub, part of the eFAA Project, dances with a human partner, learning movements through real-time feedback — not just mechanically, but emotionally. Even art is getting a robotic twist. Paul, a sketching robot by artist Patrick Tresset, captures portraits in real time, shifting focus between model and canvas like a human artist. Elsewhere, Konstantinos Grigoriadis’s Arachnoid robots evoke dystopian visions — sleek, spindly machines that feel less like tools and more like evolved creatures. And then there’s the ‘living wearable’ — a garment embedded with color-shifting cells that react to the wearer’s heartbeat and stress levels, turning emotion into visible hue. Professor Tony Prescott of Sheffield notes these advancements aren’t just impressive — they’re prompting urgent conversations about ethics, identity, and what it means to be human in an age where biology and machine are no longer separate. As scientists push toward seamless integration of life and technology, one thing is clear: the next generation of robots won’t just serve us — they may begin to resemble us, in form, function, and even feeling.

Od robota s vusima poput miševa do humanoidnih plesača i strojeva napajanih sluzavom gljivom, događaj otkriva kako priroda oblikuje budućnost tehnologije. Pod vodstvom Sveučilišta u Sheffieldu, istraživači iz cijelog svijeta predstavljaju biohibridne sustave koji spajaju živa bića s mehaničkim dijelovima. Jedan od izdvojenih je senzor BIOTACT — skup umjetnih vusa modeliranih nakon vusa šrepa, koji omogućuju robotima da se kreću isključivo osjetom dodira. Pored njega, mali robot šrep, zvan Shrewbot, prati pokretni cilj koristeći samo dodir, dokazujući da preciznost ne zahtijeva vid. Na srcu inovacije nalazi se Tacitip — umjetni prst koji je razvijen na Bristol laboratoriju za robotiku i ponavlja složene deformacije ljudske kože tijekom dodira. U međuvremenu, robot HyQ — 70-kilogramski, pas veličine četveronožac iz Italije — kreće se izuzetno tekuće, imitirajući korak stvarnih sisavaca. Ali možda najiznenađujući izložci su biohibridi. Jedna instalacija prikazuje robotsku glavu čije izraze upravlja sluzava gljiva — jednoćelijski organizam sposoban za učenje i pamćenje. Kako gljiva reagira na svjetlost i hranu, robot odslikava njeno ponašanje, brišući granicu između organske inteligencije i programiranog odgovora. Humanoidni roboti kao što su Robothespian i iCub nose interakciju dalje. Robothespian, stvoren od Engineered Arts, razgovara na više jezika, čita poeziju s emocijama i čak kopira ljudske geste. iCub, dio projekta eFAA, plesa s ljudskim partnerom, učeći pokrete putem stvarnog povratnog signala — ne samo mehanički, već i emocionalno. Čak i umjetnost dobiva robotski okret. Paul, robotski crtač od umjetnika Patricka Tresseta, hvata portrete u stvarnom vremenu, mijenjajući fokus između modela i crteža poput ljudskog umjetnika. Na drugom mjestu, roboti Arachnoid Konstantinosa Grigoriadisa evokiraju distopijske vizije — vladajuće, tankaste mašine koje se čine manje kao alati, a više kao evoluirana bića. A onda je tu i 'živi nosivi predmet' — odeća s umetnutim ćelijama koje mijenjaju boju i reagiraju na puls i razinu stresa nositelja, pretvarajući emocije u vidljivu boju. Profesor Tony Prescott iz Sheffielda naglašava da ovi napredci nisu samo impresivni — već potiču hitne rasprave o etici, identitetu i tome što znači biti čovjek u dobu kada biologija i stroj više nisu odvojeni. Dok istraživači teže ka besprijekornoj integraciji života i tehnologije, jedno je jasno: sljedeća generacija robota neće samo služiti nama — mogu početi ličiti na nas, po obliku, funkciji i čak osjećajima.

article_content: By Emma Clark. PUBLISHED: 09:38 EST, 5 July 2012. | UPDATED: 06:41 EST, 6 July 2012. Samantha Mawtus, pictured leaving Guildford Crown Court where she is on trial for conspiracy to commit robbery, was accused of helping plan a nighttime raid on the prestigious Pine Ridge Golf Club — despite claiming she was a victim. Managers at the club expressed sympathy for Mawtus, who said she endured a terrifying ordeal. The 27-year-old barmaid had been granted a week off to recover after the incident, but police investigations soon turned suspicion toward her after her boyfriend, Mitchell Laidlaw, 25, and his accomplice, Kieran Beatty, 23, were arrested. Prosecutor Nicola Merrick told the court that Mawtus conspired with the two men to rob the club on March 20, 2011. She noted that Mawtus was frequently short on money and had switched shifts to be working at the club that night. Her supervisor, Simon Price, allowed her to step outside for a cigarette. Moments later, a masked man entered wearing a balaclava and wielding a baseball bat. Initially thinking it was a prank, Price was quickly confronted with violence: the intruder forced him to hand over £330 from the till, then dragged him to a nearby wood, tied him to a tree, and taped his mouth shut. Twenty minutes later, Price freed himself and returned to the club, where he found Mawtus on the phone making a 999 call. Mawtus claimed she had been ambushed from behind, bound, and left helpless for 30 minutes before escaping. But investigators found a balaclava and rubber glove in her Ford Fiesta — unusually parked in the customer lot rather than the staff area. Gaffer tape matching the kind used on Price bore Beatty’s fingerprints. Crucially, phone records showed Mawtus contacted Laidlaw moments before the robbery. Prosecutors argue that while she claimed to be tied up and terrified, she was in communication with one of the attackers. Laidlaw and Beatty have both pleaded guilty to conspiracy to rob. Mawtus denies the charges, insisting she was deceived by her boyfriend. The trial continues at Guildford Crown Court.

article_content: In Louisville, Colorado, amid economic uncertainty, a new nonprofit is helping space entrepreneurs reach for the stars. eSpace — the Center for Space Entrepreneurship — provides fledgling aerospace companies with access to cutting-edge testing facilities designed to simulate the extreme conditions of space travel. From violent launch vibrations to the bitter cold and vacuum of outer space, its 'Incubator' offers tools no small startup could afford on its own. Founded last month as a partnership between SpaceDev, Inc. and the University of Colorado, eSpace aims to accelerate the development of space technology by guiding startups through NASA’s stringent requirements. 'One of the most important things in making space hardware is that it has to work in space — because you can’t repair it,' said Scott Tibbitts, eSpace’s executive director. Tibbitts knows firsthand how difficult that path can be. He founded SpaceDev after accidentally developing a paraffin-based actuator meant for hot-water heaters. When he pitched it to NASA, they saw potential — but the first unit cost $32,000 to build, forcing him to sell his Triumph sports car. 'We didn’t know anything about spacecraft,' he recalled. 'We asked if we could use Super Glue. They said, “No.”' Now, eSpace mentors new companies, helping them avoid those costly missteps. It also funds three graduate student projects at the University of Colorado, giving aspiring engineers real-world experience designing commercially viable space tech. 'These students have incredible skills — but they never considered aerospace until this program,' said eSpace director Diane Dimeff. Beyond aerospace, the ripple effects are significant. Companies like Composite Technology Development Inc. are repurposing space-grade materials for Earth-bound uses — such as insulation for wind turbines and geothermal systems. 'The space market creates high-skill jobs,' said Michael Tupper, EVP at Composite Tech. 'But the real opportunity lies in how those innovations transform other industries.' With its blend of mentorship, infrastructure, and education, eSpace isn’t just launching rockets — it’s launching careers, technologies, and a new model for how innovation thrives in tough economic times.

Od nasilnih vibracija pri lansiranju do mrzle i vakuumske prirode vanjskog prostora, njegova 'inkubatorska' postaja nudi alate koje mala tvrtka ne bi mogla priuštiti sama. Osnovana prošli mjesec kao partnerski odnos između SpaceDev, Inc. i Sveučilišta u Koloradu, eSpace ima za cilj ubrzati razvoj svemirske tehnologije tako što će voditi startape kroz stroge zahtjeve NASA-e. 'Jedna od najvažnijih stvari kod izrade svemirske opreme jest da mora raditi u svemiru — jer je nemoguće popraviti je,' rekao je Scott Tibbitts, izvršni direktor eSpace-a. Tibbitts osjeća na vlastitoj koži koliko je taj put težak. Osnovao je SpaceDev nakon što je slučajno razvio parafinski aktuator namijenjen grejalima za vodu. Kad je predložio svoj uređaj NASA-i, vidjeli su potencijal — ali prvi primjerak je koštao 32.000 dolara, što ga je prisilo prodati svoj sportski automobil Triumph. 'Nismo znali ništa o svemirskim brodovima,' sjetio se. 'Pitali smo ih možemo li koristiti Super Glue. Rekli su nam: „Ne.“' Sada eSpace mentori nove tvrtke, pomažući im izbjeći te skupove pogreške. Također financira tri projekta za studente više škole na Sveučilištu u Koloradu, dajući budućim inženjerima stvarno iskustvo u dizajniranju komercijalno primjenjive svemirske tehnologije. 'Ti studenti imaju sjajne vještine — ali nikada nisu razmišljali o svemirskoj industriji dok nije bio ovaj program,' rekla je direktorica eSpace-a Diane Dimeff. Izvan svemirske industrije, posljedice su značajne. Tvrtke poput Composite Technology Development Inc. prenamjenjuju materijale razvijene za svemir za upotrebu na Zemlji — poput toplinske izolacije za vjetrenje i geotermalne sustave. 'Svemirsko tržište stvara poslove visokih vještina,' rekao je Michael Tupper, potpredsjednik Composite Tech-a. 'Ali prava prilika leži u tome kako te inovacije transformiraju druge industrije.' Sa svojom kombinacijom mentorstva, infrastrukture i obrazovanja, eSpace ne samo lansira rakete — već lansira karijere, tehnologije i novi model kako inovacije cvjetaju u teškim vremenima.

article_content: The Daily Mail and The Daily Telegraph both celebrate what they describe as 'the biggest tax cuts since the 1980s.' The Mail’s headline adds, 'Let's hope it's just the start,' claiming the chancellor defied gloomy predictions by cutting National Insurance by 2p—a move it says sets the stage for a future tax-and-spend battle with Labour. The Telegraph reports that Conservative MPs cheered the 'good start' and called for further cuts before the next election. Associate editor Camilla Tominey described the National Insurance reduction as 'the rabbit pulled from the hat,' suggesting Chancellor Hunt sought to 'cast a new spell over the electorate.' She called the mini-budget an 'impressive feat of prestidigitation'—or conjuring—in taking the fight to Labour. Meanwhile, The Times front page declares, 'Hunt eases tax burden,' while the Financial Times counters with, 'Tax burden surges despite Hunt cuts.' The FT explains that although personal and business taxes have been reduced, overall taxation is set to reach its highest level since the Second World War. The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) warned that the plan offers only a 'modest boost to growth' and will push the tax burden upward over the next five years. The Economist labels the package a 'pre-election giveaway,' criticizing the chancellor for offering tax cuts alongside what it calls 'an ugly future for public services.' It disputes Hunt’s claim that falling inflation created fiscal space, arguing instead that higher inflation has forced revenue increases. The Guardian agrees the measures signal a shift toward election mode, with speculation of a spring general election. It echoes the Economist’s view that the 'bigger-than-expected' tax cuts will be funded by deeper cuts to public spending. The paper’s editorial states, 'This Tory pro-rich tax giveaway is paid for by bankrupting the state.' The Sun features a champagne cork popping on its front page, celebrating the January 2024 rollout of the National Insurance cut and the freeze on alcohol duty under the headline 'New Year's Wahey.' In contrast, the Daily Mirror dismisses the Autumn Statement as less fizz and more 'swizz,' arguing that millions will be worse off despite lower National Insurance payments. It cites halved economic growth forecasts and slower-than-expected inflation declines. Its headline asks: 'Do they take us all for fools?'

article_content: In 2012, Gu Kailai, the wife of then-powerful Chinese politician Bo Xilai, was accused of orchestrating the murder of British businessman Neil Heywood after he threatened to expose her illicit financial activities. According to testimony from Giles Hall, former director of UK-based company Vistarama, Gu attempted to launder £200,000 to pay for her son Bo Guagua’s tuition at Harrow School through a fabricated deal involving the import of giant helium balloons to China. In 1998, Gu approached Vistarama, which operated the Bournemouth Eye—a tethered balloon attraction—proposing a similar installation in Dalian, where Bo Xilai was mayor. During negotiations, she introduced her business partner, Patrick Devillers, and Heywood, who was mentoring her son’s education. Gu requested a £150,000 overpayment on a winch shipment, insisting the excess be used to cover Harrow fees. When Hall refused, she allegedly threatened to have him imprisoned if he ever visited China. Payments for the balloon project originated from multiple sources, including the Dalian Free Trade Zone, private firms, and Gu’s personal account at Coutts Bank—the private bank serving the British royal family. Despite the project’s completion, tensions escalated when the winch was rerouted through Beijing instead of Dalian, triggering Gu’s fury. Hall later described her as cold, secretive, and intimidating, noting that all parties signed non-disclosure agreements. Further revelations emerged linking Gu to a £1.5 million apartment in Coleherne Court, London—a historic building once home to Princess Diana. Neighbors reported Heywood held the key to the property, fueling speculation about the depth of their association, though claims of a romantic relationship were denied. Heywood was found dead in November 2011 at the Nanshan Lijing Holiday Hotel in Chongqing, reportedly poisoned with cyanide. Chinese authorities later confirmed Gu Kailai’s confession to the murder in a closed trial, aiming to contain international backlash. Meanwhile, Britain has called for a full investigation, with London coroner Dr. Andrew Jackson considering an inquest. The case coincided with another diplomatic crisis: dissident Chen Guangcheng’s dramatic escape to the US Embassy in Beijing. China responded with a media blackout, while the US dispatched Assistant Secretary of State Kurt Campbell to manage tensions. Both incidents exposed deep fissures in Sino-Western relations and raised global concerns about accountability and human rights in China.

Prema svjedočenju Gilesa Hella, bivšeg direktora britanske tvrtke Vistarama, Gu je pokušala prati 200.000 funti da bi platila školske troškove svog sina Bo Guagua na Harrowu putem izmišljene pogodbe koja je uključivala uvoz ogromnih helijumskih balona u Kinu. Tijekom pregovora predstavila je svoj poslovni partner Patricka Devillersa i Heywooda, koji je savjetovao njenog sina u obrazovanju. Gu je tražila dodatno plaćanje od 150.000 funti za dostavu dizalice, insistirajući da se višak koristi za plaćanje školskih troškova. Iako je projekt završen, naponi su se pojačali kad je dizalica poslana kroz Beijing umjesto Daliana, što je izazvalo Guin bijes. Kasnije je Hall opisao nju kao hladnu, tajanstvenu i strašnu, napominjući da su svi potpisali sporazume o očuvanju tajnosti. Dodatne informacije povezuju Gu s apartmanom od 1,5 milijuna funti u Coleherne Courtu u Londonu — povijesnoj zgradi koju je jednom stanovala princesa Diana. Heywood je pronađen mrtav u studenom 2011. godine u Nanshan Lijing Holiday Hotelu u Chongqingu, vjerojatno otrovan cijanidom. Kineske su vlasti kasnije potvrdile Gu Kailaijino priznanje ubistva u zatvorenom procesu, nastojeći spriječiti međunarodnu štetu. Međutim, Velika Britanija je zahtijevala puno istraživanje, a londonski sudac Dr. Andrew Jackson razmatra održavanje istrage. Slučaj se poklopio s drugom diplomatskom krizom: dramatičnim bijegom dissidenta Chen Guangchenga na američku ambasadu u Pekingu. Kina je odgovorila medijima s blokadom, dok su SAD poslale pomoćnika državnog tajnika Kurta Campbella kako bi upravljale naponima. Obje incidenca otkrivaju duboke pukotine u odnosima između Kine i Zapada i podižu globalne brige o odgovornosti i ljudskim pravima u Kini.

article_content: A recent survey by Preply, an online language learning company, reveals that how American workers describe their everyday work experience varies significantly based on their income. Those earning between $100,000 and $149,999 annually are the most likely to label their workday as 'annoying' — a sentiment shared by 5% of this group, which is notably higher than in other income brackets. For example, only about 3.7% of workers making $55,000 to $64,999 feel the same way, and the number drops further to 1.1% among those earning $25,000 to $54,999. The reason behind this pattern isn’t fully explained, but it may relate to higher expectations, burnout, or workplace pressures that come with mid-to-upper-tier salaries. Meanwhile, the most common overall description of a workday was simply 'busy' — selected by 42% of all respondents. Workers in the $75,000–$84,999 range were especially likely to use that term, with over half describing their days that way. On the lower end, employees earning under $55,000 were far more likely to call their routines 'routine' — and one in four reported having a 'bad boss'. Industry also plays a big role. People in healthcare, education, and construction tend to feel the most overwhelmed, while those in transportation, manufacturing, and sales often say they’re bored. Preply points out that this makes intuitive sense — imagine a nurse during a pandemic, constantly exposed to danger while saving lives. At the same time, tech professionals are the happiest, with the highest percentage saying they genuinely enjoy their jobs. And perhaps the most striking finding? Workers making over $150,000 a year are the most likely to describe their workday as 'enjoyable,' hinting that financial comfort might still play a role in workplace satisfaction.

Oni koji zarađuju između 100.000 i 149.999 dolara godišnje najčešće opisuju svoj radni dan kao 'dosadan' — osjećaj dijeli 5% ove skupine, što je značajno više nego u drugim razinama prihoda. Na primjer, samo oko 3,7% radnika koji zarađuju između 55.000 i 64.999 dolara osjeća isto, a broj pada na 1,1% među onima koji zarađuju između 25.000 i 54.999 dolara. Razlog za ovaj uzorak nije potpuno objašnjen, ali može biti povezan s većim očekivanjima, iscrpljenosti ili radnim pritiscima koji dolaze s srednjim i visokim prihodima. Međutim, najčešći opis svakodnevnog rada bio je jednostavno 'zauzet' — odabralo ga je 42% svih ispitanika. Radnici u rasponu od 75.000 do 84.999 dolara posebno su često koristili taj izraz, s preko polovice koji su opisivali svoje dane na taj način. Na nižoj razini, zaposlenici koji zarađuju manje od 55.000 dolara mnogo su češće opisivali svoje rutine kao 'rutinske' — a jedan od četvrtoro je izjavilo da ima 'lošeg šefa'. Industrija također igra veliku ulogu. Ljudi u zdravstvu, obrazovanju i građevinarstvu često se osjećaju najviše preopterećeno, dok oni u prometu, proizvodnji i prodaji često kažu da se dosađuju. Preply ukazuje da je ovo intuitivno — zamislite medicinsku sestru tijekom pandemije, stalno izloženu opasnosti dok spašava živote. U isto vrijeme, stručnjaci iz tehnologije su najviše zadovoljni, s najvećim postotkom koji kažu da stvarno uživaju u svom poslu. I možda najzanimljiviji nalaz? Zaposlenici koji zarađuju više od 150.000 dolara godišnje najvjerojatnije opisuju svoj radni dan kao 'ugodan', što ukazuje da financijska sigurnost može još uvijek imati utjecaja na zadovoljstvo na poslu.

article_content: By Laura Williamson. Follow @@laura_mail. Imagine turning up for a five-day survival course in the Scottish Highlands and finding a man known as 'Psycho' staring back at you. Stuart Pearce can just about see the funny side of his outdoor adventure last October — one part of a diverse football sabbatical that took the former England U21 manager from Cape Verde to the Canadian Rockies. He returns to the game full-time on July 1 as manager of Nottingham Forest, looking considerably refreshed and energized — even after a morning coaching children at a school near Upton Park in east London. 'We just turned up for five days in the wilds of Scotland last October with two ex-Marines,' says Pearce. 'It was brilliant, absolutely brilliant. We learned survival skills: building shelters, skinning hares.' 'To be fair, the others came from such diverse backgrounds that only two recognized me. There was a guy from Dublin, one from Southampton, myself, an ex-Marine from Alaska, a policewoman from Melbourne, and a Chinese man from the tourism industry.' 'Within a day, we were in a shelter we’d built ourselves in a woodland glade, around a campfire, chopping up rabbit to cook for dinner. It was great fun.' Pearce booked the course in January, knowing his six-year tenure as England U21 manager would end after the European Championships that summer. But any suggestion the experience revealed deep personal insights is firmly — if politely — dismissed. There has been no great spiritual awakening over the past year for this straightforward former left-back — only an opportunity to indulge his love of travel, theatre, and live music. He has already told his Forest staff to forget the 'sleeping giant' label, which implies the club has some divine right to promotion based on its past glory. 'I hate it,' he says. The same no-nonsense attitude underpins his response to questions about whether Wayne Rooney should start for England. 'I treat every player the way I always have,' he says. 'At the 2011 U21 tournament, I had to convince Theo Walcott to join and Arsène Wenger to release him — then, when his form dipped, I left him out after the first game. Theo cried, but I had no duty to pick him when Adam Johnson was playing brilliantly.' 'In 2010, Wayne should have been left out — his form was terrible. But Capello kept him in. This is England. At club level, I've always believed no matter who you are, you can come in and out of the team.' 'Brian Clough was a master at this. You knew immediately if your standards slipped, he'd bench you as an example to the rest.' 'Quarter-finals' is Pearce’s blunt assessment of England’s chances in Brazil. He also brushes off concerns about cabin fever or homesickness. 'Every time I hear a player say, 'We didn't have this or that,' I'm embarrassed for my profession — honestly. It shows a total lack of imagination and intelligence. You're there for arguably the greatest moment of your life. I played 12 years for England and only reached one World Cup Finals — in 1990. Everyone should grab these opportunities with both hands.' Pearce’s passion for wearing the England shirt has never been questioned. But he argues that talented youngsters like Luke Shaw and Ross Barkley have been rushed into the senior squad too soon. It may seem contradictory coming from a former U21 boss, but his philosophy remains consistent: English players must serve proper apprenticeships at U17, U19, and U21 levels to strengthen the senior team. He would have picked Ashley Cole — 'the best left-back England has ever had' — over Shaw. He calls his six years with the FA 'brilliant' but admits the 'politics' — the annual tug-of-war with Premier League managers over player selection — were 'a slight frustration.' 'If Luke Shaw returns from the World Cup without playing a minute, I’d call it a wasted adventure. He’d have been better off at the Toulon Tournament with the U20s or in a U21 qualifier. That’s where we keep missing the point.' 'We’ve got a lot of players in the England squad I’m not sure will deliver — for good or bad. I just hope they get minutes.' 'Too many of our young players keep missing tournaments. It’s sad. It’s not duty of care to our best talents — in our thin pool — to force them to play 90 minutes every international window. Clubs use their growth as an excuse to pull them out; agents don’t want them playing; and the players’ own egos get in the way. They don’t want it.' 'All we do is strip our talent pool bare, then leave them on the bench. We try to build the roof before the foundation — and it won’t work.' 'Psycho,' after all, knows all about surviving in the wild these days. Stuart Pearce was speaking for Chewits Sport Courses, which run across the UK and aim to give children of all abilities the chance to enjoy being active. For more information, visit: http://chewits.premiersport.org/
translated_content: Od Laura Williamson. Slijedite @@laura_mail. Zamislite da dođete na petodnevni survival kurs u škotskim visoravnima i nađete čovjeka poznatog kao 'Psiho' koji vam se gleda u oči. Stuart Pearce može malo vidjeti humor u svom izletu na otvorenom prošlog oktobra — jedan dio raznolike nogometne pauze koja ga je odvela od Kape Verdea do kanadskih Kordiljera. Vraća se u igru punom snagom 1. lipnja kao trener Nottingham Foresta, izgleda znatno osvježeno i puno energije — čak i nakon jutarnjeg treninga djece u školi blizu Upton Parka u istočnom Londonu. 'Samo smo stigli na pet dana u divljine Škotske prošlog oktobra sa dva bivša mornara,' kaže Pearce. 'Bilo je sjajno, apsolutno sjajno. Naučili smo vještine preživljavanja: izgradnja skloništa, čišćenje zeca.' 'Da budemo pošteni, ostali su dolazili iz toliko različitih dijelova svijeta da su samo dvoje prepoznali mene. Bio je momak iz Dublina, jedan iz Southamptona, ja, bivši mornar iz Aljaske, policajka iz Melburna i kineski čovjek iz turističke industrije.' 'Unutar dana, bili smo u skloništu koje smo sami sagradili u šumskoj poljani, oko vatre, rezali zeca da bismo ga kuhali za večeru. Bilo je sjajno.' Pearce je rezervirao kurs u siječnju, znajući da će njegova šestogodišnja služba kao trener Engleske U21 završiti nakon Europskog prvenstva tog ljeta. Ali bilo kakva sugestija da je iskustvo otkrilo duboke lične uvide je odbačena — ako i polagano. Nije bilo velikog duhovnog probuđenja tokom posljednje godine za ovog direktnog bivšeg lijevog bekanta — samo prilika da zadovolji svoju ljubav prema putovanjima, kazalištu i živim nastupima. Već je rekao svom timu u Forestu da zaborave oznaku 'spavajući div', koja podrazumijeva da klub ima neko božansko pravo na promociju u Premijer ligu zbog svog sjajnog prošlosti. 'Mrzim to,' kaže on. Ista bez kompromisa filozofija obuhvata njegov odgovor na pitanje da li je rasprava o tome da li Wayne Rooney treba da igra za Englesku opravdana. 'Tretiram svakog igrača onako kako sam uvijek radio,' kaže on. 'Na europskom prvenstvu U21 2011. morao sam uvjeriti Thea Walcotta da dođe i Arsèna Wengera da mi da Walcotta — ali kad mu je forma opala, izbacio sam ga nakon prve utakmice. Theo je plakao, ali nisam imao obavezu da ga izaberem kad je Adam Johnson odlično igrao.' '2010. godine Wayne bi trebao biti izbačen iz tima — njegova forma je bila strašna. Ali Capello ga je držao u timu. Ovo je Engleska. Na nivou kluba, uvijek sam mislio da ne važi ko si, možeš ući i izaći iz tima.' 'Brian Clough je bio majstor u ovome. Odmah si znao da će te izbaciti iz tima kao primjer za ostatak grupe ako padne tvoj standard.' 'Četvrtfinale' je Pearceov nedvosmisleni procjenjivanje šansi Engleske u Brazilu. On također odbacuje zabrinutosti o 'zatvorskom osjećaju' ili teškoćama sa udaljenostima od kuće. 'Svaki put kad čujem igrača da kaže 'nismo imali ovo ili ono', stidim se za svoj poziv — iskreno. To pokazuje potpunu nepoštenost i nizak intelekt, vjerojatno. Ti si tu da obaviš posao — možda najveći trenutak u tvom životu. article_content: Gareth Southgate has firmly ruled out recalling any senior England players to bolster the U21 squad, even if they remain eligible for the under-21 team. With England already top of Group One and facing Lithuania and Moldova in their final qualifying matches, Southgate insists his focus remains solely on the players currently in his fold. Names like Raheem Sterling, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, and Jack Wilshere — all of whom have progressed to the senior national team — are off the table. 'That’s not even in my thinking,' Southgate stated clearly, emphasizing that these players are now full internationals under Roy Hodgson’s leadership. He acknowledged that past U21 coaches, like Stuart Pearce, often pushed to include top-tier talent, pointing to Spain’s use of Juan Mata and Javi Martínez during their 2011 U21 Euro win. But Southgate sees things differently. 'This is standard across Europe,' he explained. 'Christian Eriksen still qualifies for Denmark’s U21s, but no one expects him to play for them.' Southgate compares his role to that of a club reserve team manager: his job is to develop the talent available, not chase stars. He believes giving younger players consistent international exposure is vital for their growth. While opponents in the upcoming play-offs may include powerhouses like Spain or Poland, Southgate isn’t worried. The squad’s recent experience at the Toulon Tournament, he says, gave them a realistic sense of the intensity they’ll face. 'We’re not short on talent,' he added. 'These boys know what’s required.'

Benjamin Colton Barnes, a 24-year-old Iraq War veteran, was discharged from the U.S. Army in 2009 for misconduct, including drunken driving and improperly transporting a privately owned weapon. He was last stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington — a base long plagued by high rates of post-traumatic stress disorder, suicides, and violent incidents among returning troops. On New Year’s Eve, Barnes allegedly opened fire at a house party in Skyway, south of Seattle, injuring four people, two critically. Police believe he then fled to Mount Rainier National Park, where he shot and killed Ranger Margaret Anderson on Sunday morning. Anderson, a 34-year-old mother of two, was enforcing winter safety checks when she was fatally shot. Barnes was found dead face down in snow days later, after a massive manhunt. Military records show Joint Base Lewis-McChord recorded 12 presumed suicides in 2011 — the highest on record — and was labeled the most troubled base in the U.S. military by Star and Stripes in 2009. Barnes had a documented history of mental health struggles. Court documents revealed he was involved in a custody dispute in July 2011, during which his ex-partner obtained a temporary restraining order, citing his suicidal tendencies, anger, and access to multiple firearms. A guardian ad litem recommended supervised visitation pending completion of mental health and domestic violence evaluations. The 2010 federal law permitting loaded firearms in national parks — making possession subject to state laws — has sparked renewed debate. Critics, including retired National Park Service officials, argue the law contributed to this tragedy. The National Rifle Association maintains that the law pertains only to possession, not use, and defends the right to self-defense against wildlife or threats. Ranger Anderson, who graduated from Westfield High School in New Jersey in 1995, had served at Mount Rainier for four years and was married to another park ranger. Her family and neighbors described her as devoted and kind. Authorities say Barnes likely entered the park to evade capture after the shooting. Parks spokesperson Kevin Bacher noted that survival in such conditions is difficult but possible — and added, 'I don’t think any of us would be sorry if he was not in a condition to fire on our searchers.'
