article_content: A British man formerly working as a doctor in the NHS has been arrested at Heathrow Airport alongside his wife after returning from Egypt. UK counter-terrorism investigators believe he spent time in Syria as a medic for an extremist group called Al Absi — a cell of approximately 40 individuals seeking to enforce Sharia law in the region. Hostages held by the group, including British photojournalist John Cantlie, reported that the man treated gunshot wounds using medical equipment branded with NHS logos. He spoke with a clear London accent and claimed to have taken a sabbatical from his job at a South London emergency department to care for wounded fighters. He reportedly told his captives he was engaged in a 'holy war' and viewed his frontline experience as training for a future in trauma medicine. Despite his medical role, Cantlie stated the man refused to send even a brief message to his girlfriend, fearing he would be executed if caught helping. The suspect, described as having a heavy beard and wearing sunglasses and a scarf, allegedly held a senior position at a South London A&E unit. Cantlie and his Dutch colleague Jeroen Oerlemans were captured in July 2012 after trying to escape their captors. They were held for a week before being rescued by the Free Syrian Army. During their captivity, the militants announced plans to execute two local men accused of spying — but spared them after they pledged loyalty to Sharia law. The 26-year-old suspect and his wife were apprehended by Scotland Yard’s Counter Terrorism Command. Investigators identified the man through NHS employment records and interviews with former colleagues. Authorities suspect his wife traveled to Egypt under the pretense of a holiday to meet him before returning together to the UK. UK officials estimate that up to 100 British nationals have traveled to Syria to join the conflict. While the vast majority of fighters are Syrians, including defectors from the regime, an increasing number of foreign extremists — particularly from Western countries — are entering the war zone. Two homes in East London have been searched as part of the investigation. The government continues to monitor citizens suspected of involvement in overseas terrorism.

article_content: For three weeks, Hamas and Israel have been locked in a deadly cycle of violence, with neither side showing signs of backing down. Both blame the other for provoking the conflict — which has claimed hundreds of lives, mostly civilians — and neither feels it has achieved its objectives. As a result, a ceasefire remains elusive. What does Hamas, the group governing Gaza and designated a terrorist organization by many Western nations, truly seek? And what would it accept to end the bloodshed? First, Hamas seeks the destruction of Israel. This goal is enshrined in its founding charter: 'Israel will exist and will continue to exist until Islam will obliterate it.' While this aim is widely condemned as extreme and unattainable, some analysts argue it reflects an enduring ideological stance. However, others suggest that even if full destruction is impractical, Hamas aims to make life in Israel so unbearable through terror that Jews will leave. Journalist Jeffrey Goldberg of The Atlantic writes: 'The goal of Hamas — the actual, overarching goal — is to terrorize the Jews of Israel, through mass murder, into abandoning their country.' He adds that Hamas believes such sacrifices are theologically justified. Second, Hamas demands an end to the Israeli blockade. Though Israel withdrew settlers and troops from Gaza in 2005, Palestinians argue they remain under occupation because Israel controls Gaza’s borders, airspace, and coastline — regulating all imports and exports. Hamas leaders, including Ismail Haniyeh and Khaled Meshaal, have repeatedly called for open border crossings with Israel and Egypt, framing the blockade as illegal collective punishment. 'The resistance is a means to an end,' Meshaal told CNN in 2012. 'The endgame is to end occupation — but the international community is not enabling us. They are biased toward Israel.' Third, Hamas insists on the release of Palestinian prisoners. In 2011, it secured the release of over 1,000 detainees in exchange for captured Israeli soldier Gilad Shalit. Many of those freed were later rearrested. Recent arrests following the June 2014 abduction of three Israeli teenagers have further inflamed tensions. Analyst Zaki Chehab argues this pattern shows Israel has broken its commitments: 'It’s a sign that Israel has not respected its agreement.' Fourth, Hamas seeks to strengthen its position among Palestinians. With little progress toward a Palestinian state and continued settlement expansion, many Palestinians view Hamas as the only force willing to resist Israel. Analyst Peter Beinart notes: 'When Hamas says, “What’s the point of accepting Israel’s right to exist if Israel will never give us a state?” — it resonates.' Since 2012, Hamas has lost regional allies, especially after Egypt’s Muslim Brotherhood government fell. Facing financial strain and declining popularity, some analysts, like Natan Sachs of Brookings, suggest Hamas may have miscalculated — or even lost control — of its militant wings, leading to this escalation.

article_content: A medical examination table once used by Dr. Harold Shipman — the UK’s deadliest serial killer — is now listed on eBay for £10,000. The blue, padded couch was part of the equipment at the Abraham Ormerod Medical Centre in Todmorden, West Yorkshire, where Shipman worked as a general practitioner in the 1970s. During this time, he began systematically killing his patients, mostly elderly women living alone, often by administering fatal doses of diamorphine. Estimates suggest he murdered between 215 and 260 people over nearly three decades. The table is currently owned by Marjorie Chakravarti, a 72-year-old former nurse who bought it for just £10 in the early 1990s from a colleague at the same clinic. She used it while studying for qualifications in physiology, massage, and aromatherapy, storing it for years in her garden shed. Now, as she downsizes due to her husband’s illness, she decided to sell it — not out of greed, she says, but because keeping it no longer makes sense. 'Buying a brand-new one today costs around £770,' she noted. 'This has history — and it’s still in decent shape.' Chakravarti says she was deeply disturbed by Shipman’s crimes. 'It’s gob-smacking that someone in a caregiving role could do something so monstrous,' she told reporters. She never met him personally; he was one of many doctors at the practice, led by Dr. Michael Grieve. She also owns the chair Shipman used but is holding off on selling it until she gauges public reaction to the table. The eBay listing has drawn attention beyond collectors — copies of victims’ death certificates and official witness statements are also being offered. While some see the sale as exploitative, others argue it’s simply an individual clearing clutter. Shipman, who was convicted in 2000 of murdering 15 patients and sentenced to 15 life terms, took his own life in 2004 in Wakefield Prison. His case triggered a sweeping government inquiry that changed how deaths are certified across Britain.

article_content: Germany has suffered a setback ahead of their World Cup quarter-final clash with France, as seven members of the squad have been affected by illness. Coach Joachim Löw confirmed the players are 'slightly ill,' primarily experiencing sore throats, but downplayed concerns. 'It’s not that bad at the moment,' he said. 'I don’t want to over-dramatise it.' However, key players such as Mats Hummels and Christoph Kramer have clearly been impacted. Hummels missed the Round of 16 match against Algeria after being bedridden the night before, while Kramer missed an entire day of training this week. Thomas Müller, who is in contention for the Golden Boot, has also displayed flu-like symptoms even before Germany’s last game. Löw attributes the outbreak to Brazil’s unpredictable climate and the team’s extensive travel between regions. 'We’re constantly moving between different climate zones,' he explained. 'It’s understandable that the players start to feel under the weather — and that the illness spreads.' The situation is particularly concerning given Germany’s pre-tournament fitness issues. Several key players — including Sami Khedira, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and Miroslav Klose — arrived in Brazil having recently recovered from long-term injuries. With Shkodran Mustafi already ruled out for the remainder of the tournament, Löw’s hopes of fielding a fully fit side now seem unrealistic.

article_content: After 40 years of dedicated service, gravedigger Ray Loxton, 59, lost his job following a widely circulated photograph that many interpreted as disrespectful. The image, published in the Shepton Mallet Journal in July 2013, showed Loxton topless in a grave, shielding his eyes from the sun — a gesture some readers mistakenly believed was a salute. Loxton explained that he was digging the grave of a close friend on a scorching June day when photographer Jason Bryant approached and asked to capture his work. 'The sun was blinding me,' Loxton said. 'I raised my hand instinctively. I had no idea anyone would think I was saluting.' The photo, part of the newspaper’s weekly 'Picture of the Week' feature, drew over 15,000 views and triggered a flood of letters — including one from Holger Harras of Evercreech, Somerset, who called it 'in poor taste' and questioned the dignity of the deceased’s final resting place. Yet not everyone agreed. Pub licensee Steve Wilson countered: 'Everyone has a right to be happy in their work. Would you rather he cried while digging?' Others praised Loxton as a local legend, noting his long-standing reputation for reliability and kindness. Despite the community’s mixed response, WJ Trotman, the funeral director who employed Loxton, ended their professional relationship, citing media attention as the reason. When contacted, Loxton expressed deep hurt: 'I’ve never had a single complaint in 30 years. I did good work. Now they’ve replaced me because of a photo.' Photographer Jason Bryant stood by the image, saying Loxton was a well-known and respected figure in the community. 'He’s a legend,' Bryant said. 'I just wanted to show real life.' John Weir of the National Society of Independent Funeral Directors noted that Trotman had made a 'commercial decision' amid growing scrutiny, though the company itself declined to elaborate.

article_content: Scientists have claimed that genetics may determine whether a person infected with Ebola survives or dies. A new study suggests DNA could be key to understanding the varying severity of the virus, which has devastated West Africa. The World Health Organization reports that nearly 5,000 people have died from Ebola, primarily in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Researchers at Washington University have identified genetic factors behind the wide range of responses to Ebola infection — from complete resistance to severe illness and death. Some individuals exposed to the virus remain asymptomatic; others experience moderate symptoms and recover; the most vulnerable suffer bleeding, organ failure, and shock. Past studies showed these differences are not due to variations in the virus itself, but rather to how the human body responds to infection. The study, conducted in a high-security biocontainment lab in Montana, used mice infected with a mouse-adapted strain of the Ebola virus responsible for the 2014 West African outbreak. While conventional lab mice died without showing symptoms, the new model revealed a spectrum of outcomes: 19% of mice fully recovered, regaining lost weight within two weeks with no visible pathology; 11% were partially resistant; and 70% experienced over 50% mortality. Among the fatally affected mice, common signs included liver inflammation, internal bleeding, enlarged spleens, abnormal liver color and texture, and delayed blood clotting — mirroring fatal cases in humans. Dr. Angela Rasmussen noted that the range of disease manifestations in the mice closely matched the clinical diversity seen during the 2014 outbreak. Dr. Michael Katze explained that fatal outcomes correlated with gene activity promoting inflammation and cell death, while survivors showed stronger activation of genes involved in blood vessel repair and immune cell production. The researchers believe this mouse model can accelerate the discovery of genetic markers and the testing of antiviral drugs and vaccines against all Ebola strains. Professor Andrew Easton of Warwick University stated that while host genetics influence Ebola outcomes — as with many viruses — human genetic diversity makes direct application of these findings complex. Professor Jonathan Ball of the University of Nottingham emphasized that the link between coagulation gene expression and disease severity is intriguing but still correlational; further research is needed to confirm causality in humans. The study was published in the journal Science. Experts agree that while genetics plays a critical role, environmental factors — such as nutrition, access to care, and underlying health conditions — also significantly affect survival rates.
translated_content: Znanstvenici su tvrdili da genetika može odrediti hoće li osoba zarazena ebolom preživjeti ili umrijeti. Novo istraživanje sugerira da bi DNK mogla biti ključ za razumijevanje različitih težina bolesti, koja je uništila Zapadnu Afriku. Svjetska zdravstvena organizacija izvještava da je gotovo 5.000 ljudi umrlo od ebole, uglavnom u Gvineji, Liberiji i Sijera Leoneu. Istraživači s Washingtonove univerziteta identificirali su genetske faktore koji stoji iza širokog raspona odgovora na infekciju ebolom — od potpune otpornosti do teških simptoma i smrti. Neke osobe koje su bile izložene virusu ostaju asimptomatske; druge iskušavaju umjerene simptome i oporave se; najosjetljivije osobe pati od krvarenja, oštećenja organa i šoka. Prethodna istraživanja pokazala su da ove razlike nisu posljedica varijacija samog virusa, već način na koji ljudsko tijelo reagira na infekciju. Istraživanje, provedeno u visokosigurnoj biokontrolnoj laboratoriji u Montani, koristilo je miševe inficirane mišjom adaptiranom verzijom virusa ebola odgovorne za izbijanje 2014. godine u Zapadnoj Africi. Dok su konvencionalni laboratorijski miševi umrli bez prikazivanja simptoma, novi model otkrio je spektar ishoda: 19% miševa potpuno se oporavilo, obnovivši izgubljenu težinu unutar dva tjedna bez vidljivih patoloških promjena; 11% bilo je djelomično otporno; a 70% imalo je više od 50% smrtnosti. Među smrtno zaraženim miševima, česti znakovi uključivali su upalu jetre, unutrašnje krvarenje, povećanu slezenu, anomalne promjene boje i teksture jetre te usporeno zgrušavanje krvi — što odražava smrtna slučajeva kod ljudi. Dr. Angela Rasmussen napomenula je da je raspon manifestacija bolesti kod miševa usko sličan kliničkoj raznolikosti vidjenoj tijekom izbijanja 2014. godine. Dr. Michael Katze objasnio je da su smrtni ishodi povezani s aktivnošću gena koji potiču upalu i smrt stanica, dok su oporavljeni miševi pokazivali jaču aktivnost gena uključenih u popravak krvnih žila i proizvodnju bijelih krvnih stanica. Istraživači vjeruju da ovaj mišji model može ubrzati otkrivanje genetskih markera i testiranje antivirusnih lijekova i cjepiva protiv svih vrsta ebole. Prof. Andrew Easton sa Warwickove univerziteta rekao je da, iako genetika domaćina utječe na ishode ebole — kao i kod mnogih virusa — genetska raznolikost ljudi čini direktnu primjenu ovih nalaza kompleksnom. Prof. Jonathan Ball sa Sveučilišta u Nottinghamu naglasio je da je povezanost između ekspresije gena za zgrušavanje i težine bolesti zanimljiva, ali još uvijek korelacijska; potrebna je daljnja istraživanja da bi se potvrdila uzročnost kod ljudi. Istraživanje je objavljeno u časopisu Science. Stručnjaci slažu se da iako genetika igra ključnu ulogu, okolišni faktori — kao što su prehrana, pristup brizi i osnovno zdravstveno stanje — također značajno utječu na stopu preživljavanja.

article_content: A man from Superior, Wisconsin, who gained international notoriety after being convicted in 2006 of sexually assaulting the carcass of a dead deer, was arrested this week for allegedly assaulting a female police officer. Bryan James Hathaway, 25, was arraigned Wednesday on four charges stemming from an incident at the Hermantown Walmart on Monday night. He is accused of assaulting Officer Kody Vedder, obstructing legal process, fleeing on foot, and receiving stolen property. He is being held in the St. Louis County Jail on $20,000 bail. According to the criminal complaint, Officer Vedder was off duty and shopping at Walmart with her 11-year-old daughter after her shift ended on Monday evening. She was wearing a black T-shirt with the word 'POLICE' printed boldly on the front and back. After finishing her shopping, Vedder noticed Hathaway sitting in the backseat of a parked Lincoln Town Car next to her vehicle. She observed him repeatedly ducking down and watching passersby — behavior she deemed suspicious. Vedder exited her car, knocked on Hathaway's window, and pointed to her shirt, identifying herself as a police officer and instructing him not to move. She immediately called 911 for backup. Before officers arrived, Hathaway attempted to flee. Vedder grabbed him by the shirt and tried to restrain him, but he twisted free and shoved her to the ground. She sustained scratches and bruising to her tailbone, requiring an X-ray. Officers from three nearby departments arrived and apprehended Hathaway near a Volkswagen dealership. Inside the car, they found a backpack containing two Android cell phones in their original packaging — one still bearing Walmart’s anti-theft security device. They also recovered a Virgin Mobile LG phone and a new power cord in a plastic bag, both believed to be stolen from the store. This incident comes less than six years after Hathaway’s 2006 conviction for sexual contact with a deer carcass. On October 11, 2006, then-18-year-old Hathaway discovered the animal’s body while biking along Stinson Avenue in Chicago. He admitted moving it into the woods and assaulting it, telling police: 'When I was done, I was upset with myself. I know having sex with animals is wrong, but I can’t help myself and I need help.' He pleaded no contest to sexual gratification with an animal and received probation and mandatory psychological treatment. In April 2005, Hathaway pleaded no contest to a felony charge of animal mistreatment related to shooting a 26-year-old Arabian gelding named Bambrick in Douglas County. He told investigators he intended to have sex with the horse but was scared off by a neighbor who heard the gunshot. Detective Sgt. Ed Anderson described Hathaway’s behavior as unprecedented: 'I’ve never run across a personality like this.' According to the Wisconsin Department of Corrections, Hathaway remains under probation supervision until August of next year. He also has a pending probation violation hearing in Chisago County stemming from a 2008 theft conviction.

Optužen je za napad na policajnicu Kody Vedder, ometanje zakonitog postupka, bijeg peške i primanje ukradenog imovine. Zadržan je u zatvoru St. Louis okruga uz novčanu jamčevinu od 20.000 dolara. Primijetila je kako se ponavljano sklanja i gleda prolaznike — ponašanje koje je smatrala sumnjivim. Pritom je doživjela ožiljke i modrice na repnoj kosti, što je zahtijevalo rendgenski snimak. Ovaj incident dogodio se manje od šest godina nakon Hathawayeve osude 2006. godine za seksualni kontakt s trupom jelena. 11. listopada 2006., tada 18-godišnji Hathaway pronašao je tijelo životinje dok je vozio biciklom uz Stinson Avenue u Chicagu. Priznao je krivnju za seksualno zadovoljstvo s životinjom i dobio je kaznu u obliku probacije i obvezu psihološkog liječenja. U travnju 2005. godine, Hathaway je priznao krivnju za kazneno djelo teškog zlostavljanja životinja vezano uz pucaj na 26-godišnjeg arapskog konja imena Bambrick u Douglas okrugu. Rekao je istražiteljima da je namjeravao imati seks s konjem, ali ga je uplašio susjed koji je čuo palju i krenuo u tom smjeru. article_content: Hanaa Ben Abdesslem, Tunisia’s first supermodel, has signed with French beauty giant Lancôme — a milestone in a region where modeling has long faced cultural resistance. Her success is part of a broader shift as Arab women increasingly claim space in global fashion. Moroccan model Hind Sahli has walked for top designers including Vera Wang and appeared in the Italian and Spanish editions of Vogue. Meanwhile, Arab-Israeli model Huda Naccache made headlines as the first woman to appear in a bikini on the cover of an Arabic magazine, Lilac. Naccache, 23, is currently studying archaeology at the University of Haifa and plans to return to modeling after graduation. Her cover sparked controversy, but she emphasizes respect for diverse beliefs while staying true to her path. Even more polarizing was German-Turkish model Sila Sahin, who became the first Muslim woman photographed topless for Playboy Germany. She was disowned by her conservative family but declared the shoot a personal liberation: 'I did it because I wanted to be free at last.' Despite pushback, many of these women report overwhelming support — especially from younger generations. Hind Sahli, 22, says young girls message her on Facebook asking how to begin modeling. 'I’m happy with what I’m doing,' she says. Hanaa Ben Abdesslem credits her brother’s early support and daily Skype calls with her parents, who initially didn’t understand modeling. 'They’ve had to create a new tick-box just for me,' she jokes. Male model Sertac Tasdelen, 29, notes that while modeling isn’t yet seen as prestigious in Turkey compared to careers like medicine or banking, attitudes are shifting with economic growth and rising demand for Arab representation in global advertising. Fashion analysts point to the growing purchasing power of Arab consumers as a key driver. 'Designers and brands have to go where the money is,' says Lauretta Roberts of WSGN. 'The haute couture market now caters overwhelmingly to wealthy Arab clients.' While economic forces are accelerating change, social acceptance lags. Shaista Gohir of the Muslim Women’s Network UK says, 'You always need that first person to break the boundary — to inspire others.' For Ben Abdesslem, whose next appearance is in the fully clothed but sensual 2013 Pirelli Calendar, this movement is about more than fashion. 'We’ve both created our own revolutions,' she says — referring to herself and her nation.

article_content: While the official Schoolies week in Queensland has concluded, celebrations continue across Australia, particularly in Victoria and New South Wales, where many teens have reached legal drinking age. Crowds are still pouring into popular destinations like the Gold Coast and Byron Bay, with the final phase of festivities now underway. Even though Queensland Police officially ended their dedicated Schoolies operation on November 29, officers remain visibly present — especially around Surfers Paradise — to manage the influx of older students from other states. Despite the end of the formal program, the energy hasn’t faded. Social media is buzzing with photos capturing the chaotic end-of-school vibe: teens passed out on beaches, half-naked on balconies, or sprawled in shopping trolleys after a long night. One young man in Fiji was photographed wearing a polka-dot bikini, turning heads abroad as part of his farewell celebration. A recurring theme? The selfie culture. Two girls grinned for the camera while their friend vomited into a toilet behind them. Another posed shirtless, but covered his private parts with a T-shirt — an awkwardly humorous contrast to his fully dressed friends. Meanwhile, someone was found buried up to their neck in sand, abandoned by their mates. In one case, a guy fell asleep mid-text to his partner — pants off, phone in hand. Another was spotted lounging in a garden bed after an accident. These moments, while outrageous, reflect a broader pattern: young people celebrating freedom with little restraint. Queensland Police reported 131 arrests across 152 charges during the official week (Nov 21–28), a decrease from prior years. Acting Chief Superintendent Des Lacy credited the improvement to smarter policing and partnerships with groups like Red Frogs, local councils, and event organizers. The focus now shifts to licensed venues, where most interstate attendees are legally allowed to drink. Authorities say the majority of students are behaving responsibly — and the drop in arrests shows progress.

article_content: Reports of a possible ceasefire in Gaza, brokered by Egypt, emerged Tuesday. However, without a long-term strategy to resolve the fractured state of Palestinian politics, any truce is likely to be as fleeting as past ones. This latest Israeli offensive is the sixth major military campaign in Gaza since Israel’s 2005 withdrawal of troops and settlers — and the first since the large-scale 'Cast Lead' operation four years ago. U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton arrived in the region to support Egypt’s mediation efforts. Egypt, uniquely positioned as the only country with direct ties to both Israel and Hamas, is the most credible mediator. But the conflict has worsened tensions between Cairo and Tel Aviv: Egyptian President Mohamed Morsy recalled his ambassador from Israel and sent his prime minister to Gaza to demonstrate solidarity with Hamas. Meanwhile, U.S.-Egyptian relations have suffered due to the Obama administration’s open alignment with Israel. While Israel insists its goal is to permanently halt rocket fire from Gaza, Hamas demands an end to the five-year blockade and full reopening of border crossings. Neither side appears to have a realistic endgame — and neither is likely to achieve its core objectives. Hamas cannot be eliminated militarily. Even if its rocket capabilities are degraded — a doubtful outcome — the war will only fuel its determination to rearm, as happened after Cast Lead. Without addressing root grievances, the cycle of violence will persist. Egypt shares Israel’s interest in curbing Hamas and stopping arms smuggling through the Sinai. Yet despite ideological links between Egypt’s Muslim Brotherhood government and Hamas, Cairo is frustrated by Hamas’s actions in both Gaza and Sinai. For any ceasefire to endure, it must involve Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas. While Hamas may emerge militarily weaker, it is likely to gain political strength, winning admiration across the Arab world. Abbas, by contrast, looks increasingly irrelevant: his leadership has delivered two decades of failed negotiations and a bankrupt, ineffective authority. Yet Egypt’s role as mediator in long-stalled Palestinian reconciliation talks offers a rare opportunity: to strengthen Abbas while containing Hamas. Though Hamas has a violent history, it has also proven capable of governance and pragmatic politics. Internal debates between hardliners and moderates within Hamas reflect the tension between resistance and rule. Egypt, Turkey, and Qatar aim to reduce Hamas’s dependence on Iran. But Israel’s offensive makes this harder, pushing Hamas toward more militant factions. Tying ceasefire terms to Palestinian unity could give Egypt leverage to pressure Hamas. Any lasting agreement must end rocket fire, strengthen border security, and ease the blockade — but only if Gazans receive tangible benefits. Because neither Israel nor Egypt trusts Hamas to secure the border, reopening crossings requires the return of Abbas’s Palestinian Authority. Yet this can only happen with Hamas’s consent — meaning genuine reconciliation is non-negotiable. In this model, every actor gains something — and thus has a stake in others’ success. It’s complex, but not impossible. The main obstacle? Israeli and U.S. resistance to any deal that legitimizes Hamas. This policy has backfired: Hamas now enjoys greater international legitimacy, the blockade is crumbling, and Abbas’s authority is collapsing — while Qatar pours hundreds of millions into Hamas. As Arab leaders visit Gaza, the message is clear: Palestinian unity is no longer optional. Fatah and Hamas don’t need to agree on everything — or even share a government. But they must agree on the rules of the political game. Excluding Hamas from diplomacy has killed the peace process. Without a unified, representative Palestinian voice, no deal with Israel can be negotiated — let alone implemented. A grand bargain is risky. But the risk of doing nothing is greater. Whether this becomes the last Gaza war — or merely a prelude to the next — depends on whether Israel, the Palestinians, and their allies finally confront reality.
translated_content: Izvještaji o mogućem primirju u Gazi, posredovanom Egipatom, pojavili su se utorka. Međutim, bez dugoročne strategije za rješavanje frakciranosti palestinske politike, bilo koje primirje vjerojatno će biti prolazno poput ranijih. Ova zadnja izraelska ofenziva je šesta velika vojna kampanja u Gazi otkad je Izrael povukao svoje vojnike i naseljenike 2005. godine — i prva od velike operacije 'Vodeni stub' prije četiri godine. Državni tajnik SAD Hilari Klinton stigla je u regiju kako bi podržala egipatske napore za posredovanje. Egipat, jedinstveno pozicioniran kao jedina zemlja s direktnim vezama i s Izraelom i s Hamasom, je najvjerojatniji posrednik. Ali sukob je pogoršao napete odnose između Kaira i Tel Aviva: egipatski predsjednik Mohamed Mursi povukao je svog ambasadora iz Izraela i poslao svojeg premijera u Gazu kako bi pokazao solidarnost s Hamasom. U međuvremenu, odnosi između SAD-a i Egipta trpe zbog otvorene podrške Obamaove administracije Izraelu. Iako Izrael tvrdi da je njegov cilj trajno zaustaviti rakete iz Gaze, Hamas traži kraj petogodišnje blokade i puno otvaranje graničnih prijelaza. Nijedna strana ne izgleda da ima realističan cilj — ni jedna nije vjerojatno da će postići svoje ključne ciljeve. Hamas se ne može ukloniti vojnim putem. Čak i ako bi njegove rakete bile smanjene — što je sumnjivo — rat će samo jačati njegovu želju za oporavkom, kao što se dogodilo nakon operacije 'Vodeni stub'. Bez rješavanja korijenskih žalbi, ciklus nasilja će nastaviti. Egipat dijeli Izraelov interes u ograničavanju Hamasa i zaustavljanju prevoza oružja kroz Sinaj. Međutim, unatoč ideološkim vezama između egipatske vlade Muslimanske bratstva i Hamasa, Kairo je razočaran Hamasovim akcijama u Gazi i Sinaju. Da bi primirje trajalo, mora uključivati predsjednika Palestinske vlasti Mahmuda Abbas. Iako Hamas može izaći iz ovog sukoba vojno oslabljen, vjerojatno će dobiti političku snagu i osvojiti simpatije širom arapskog svijeta. Abbas, s druge strane, izgleda sve manje važno: njegovo vođstvo je donijelo dvadeset godina neuspjelih pregovora i bankrotne, neefikasne vlasti. Međutim, uloga Egipta kao posrednika u dugo zaustavljenim palestinskim pregovorima o pomirenju nudi rijetku priliku: jačanje Abasa dok se Hamas drži pod kontrolom. Iako Hamas ima nasilnu prošlost, pokazao je da je sposoban za upravljanje i pragmatičnu politiku. Unutrašnji sporovi između radikalaca i pragmatičara unutar Hamasa odražavaju napon između otpora i vladanja. Egipat, Turska i Katar ciljaju smanjiti ovisnost Hamasa o Iranu. Ali izraelska ofenziva to čini težim, potiskujući Hamas prema više ratničkim frakcijama. Povezivanje uvjeta primirja s palestinskim pomirenjem moglo bi dati Egipatu dodatni pritisak na Hamas. Bilo koji trajan sporazum mora prestati s napadima raketa, pojačati sigurnost granica i olakšati blokadu — ali samo ako stanovnici Gaze dobiju vidljive koristi. Jer ni Izrael ni Egipat ne vjeruju Hamasu da osigura granicu, ponovno otvaranje graničnih prijelaza zahtijeva povratak Palestinske vlasti Abasa. Ali ovo može doći samo uz saglasnost Hamasa — što znači da je pravo pomirenje neizbježno. U ovom modelu, svaka strana dobiva nešto — i tako ima interesa u uspjehu drugih. To je složeno, ali ne nemoguće. Glavna prepreka? Izraelska i američka otpornost na bilo koji sporazum koji legitimiraju Hamas. Ova politika je imala obrnuti učinak: Hamas sada ima veću međunarodnu legitimnost, blokada se ruši, a Abasova vlast pada — dok Katar ulaže stotine milijuna dolara u Hamas. Dok arapski vođe posjećuju Gazu, poruka je jasna: palestinsko pomirenje više nije opcija. Fatah i Hamas ne moraju se složiti na sve — ili čak dijeliti vladu. Ali moraju se složiti na pravilima političke igre. Isključivanje Hamasa iz diplomacije je ubilo mirni proces. Bez jedinstvene, predstavničke palestinske vlasti, nikakav sporazum s Izraelom ne može biti pregovaran — niti proveden. Veliki sporazum je rizičan. Ali rizik od ništa činjenja je veći. Hoće li ovo postati posljednji rat u Gazi — ili samo uvod u sljedeći — ovisi o tome hoće li Izrael, Palestinci i njihovi saveznici konačno suočiti s stvarnošću.

article_content: The food fraud scandal escalated last night after Tesco admitted that the 'minced beef' in its frozen bolognese contained up to 100% horsemeat. The Everyday Value ready-meal was produced by Comigel, a French company also linked to contaminated products sold by Findus and Aldi. Horses slaughtered in Romania are believed to have been used by Comigel to produce meals distributed across Britain and Europe, raising fears the issue may be more widespread than initially thought. Tesco’s technical director, Tim Smith, apologized to customers, stating that while the company had withdrawn the product as a precaution after reports of horsemeat in Findus items from the same factory, subsequent tests confirmed the presence of horse DNA. UK Environment Secretary Owen Paterson informed ministers that while most positive test results showed trace levels of horse DNA (under 1%), three samples exceeded 60%. Tesco confirmed the horsemeat content ranged between 60% and 100%. Concerns persist that the horsemeat may have been contaminated with phenylbutazone ('bute'), a veterinary drug banned from the human food chain due to its link to aplastic anaemia. However, Tesco stated its tests for bute came back negative and that it would no longer source products from Comigel’s facility. The scandal originated four weeks ago with the discovery of horsemeat in burgers manufactured in Ireland. French authorities trace the horsemeat to two Romanian abattoirs, shipped via intermediaries in Cyprus and the Netherlands — a claim disputed by Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ponta, who insisted Romanian exports were correctly labeled as horsemeat. Six French supermarkets withdrew Findus and Comigel products following the UK recall. Paterson faced criticism from Labour MP Mary Creagh, who accused the government of incompetence, delayed testing, and unfairly blaming Eastern European nations. She noted that neither Romania nor Poland had found evidence of fraudulent practices in their abattoirs. The Food Standards Agency waited three weeks before ordering comprehensive testing of beef products sold in supermarkets, schools, hospitals, and prisons. Paterson suggested the contamination resulted from an international criminal conspiracy, with police in the UK and Europe now involved. Retailers have since removed large quantities of beef-related products from shelves. Investigations continue into the Spanghero depot in Castelnaudary, France, which supplied meat to Comigel.

Proizvod Everyday Value proizvela je Comigel, francuska tvrtka povezana s kontaminiranim proizvodima koje su prodavale i Findus i Aldi. Konji koji su ubijeni u Rumunjskoj vjerojatno su korišteni od strane Comigela za proizvodnju jela koja su distribuirana po Britaniji i Europi, što je probudilo brige da je problem širi nego što se na početku mislilo. Tehnički direktor Tesca, Tim Smith, izvinio se kupcima, navodeći da je kompanija uklonila proizvod kao opreznu mjeru nakon prijava o konjskom mesu u Findusovim proizvodima iz iste tvornice, ali kasnija ispitivanja potvrdila su prisutnost konjske DNK. Britanski ministar za okoliš, hranu i poljoprivredu, Owen Paterson, obavijestio je ministre da većina pozitivnih rezultata pokazuje tragove konjske DNK (manje od 1%), ali tri uzorka premašuju 60%. Tesco je potvrdio da sadržaj konjskog mesa varira između 60% i 100%. Postoje zabrinutosti da bi konjsko meso moglo biti kontaminirano fenilbutazonom ('bute'), veterinarskim lijekom zabranjenim u ljudskoj prehrani zbog povezanosti s aplastičnom anemijom. Međutim, Tesco je naveo da su njegovi testovi za bute bili negativni i da više neće kupovati proizvode s Comigelove tvornice. Skandal je počeo prije četiri tjedna otkrićem konjskog mesa u burgerima proizvedenim u Irskoj. Francuske vlasti tragaju konjsko meso do dvije rumunjske ubojnice, dostavljeno putem posrednika na Cipru i Nizozemskoj — tvrdnja koju osporava rumunjski premijer Victor Ponta, koji je insistirao da su rumunjski izvozi ispravno označeni kao konjsko meso. Šest francuskih trgovina uklonilo je Findusove i Comigelove proizvode nakon britanskog povlačenja. Paterson je suočen s kritikom od strane radničke zastupnice Mary Creagh, koja je optužila vladu za nekompetentnost, kašnjenje u testiranju i nepravedno optuživanje istočnoeuropskih zemalja. Ona je napomenula da ni Rumunjska ni Poljska nisu pronašle dokaze o prevari u svojim ubojnicama. Agencija za sigurnost hrane čekala je tri tjedna prije naručivanja sveobuhvatnog testiranja mesa proizvoda prodanih u supermarketima, školama, bolnicama, zatvorima i drugim javnim ustanovama. Paterson je predložio da je kontaminacija rezultat međunarodne kriminalne zavjere, a policija u UK-u i Europi sada je uključena u istragu. Trgovci su od tada uklonili velike količine proizvoda s govedinom sa policija. Istraga traje u depou Spanghero u Castelnaudaryju, Francuska, koji je isporučivao meso Comigelu.

article_content: In Brisbane’s inner-city suburb of New Farm, the Oxlade Drive House has been crowned the public’s favorite home at the 2014 Australian National Architecture Awards, winning the People’s Choice Award. Designed by architect James Russell, the home stands out not for grandeur, but for its thoughtful, climate-smart response to subtropical living. At its heart is a series of two-storey pavilions clad in durable Ironbark timber, arranged along the property’s length with open courtyards separating each section. These courtyards aren’t just aesthetic — they’re functional. A soft, breathable shade cloth screen wraps around them, filtering harsh sun, deterring mosquitoes and flies, and offering gentle privacy without walls. Architect James Russell describes the structure as a ‘beautiful shed’ — a humble term that belies its innovation. ‘We’re happy if people see it like an aviary or a butterfly enclosure,’ he told the Courier Mail. ‘In Brisbane, you deal with bugs. This screen becomes a quiet buffer — cooling the space naturally, and making indoor-outdoor living feel seamless.’ The design eliminates the need for air conditioning by channeling summer breezes and inviting winter sun through carefully positioned openings. The jury at the Queensland Architecture Awards called it ‘an intelligent, appropriate reinterpretation of inner-city living,’ praising how its robust material palette and spatial rhythm engage the senses and deepen the bond between interior and exterior. The home’s success lies in its simplicity: no flashy gimmicks, just smart, grounded architecture that listens to its environment. Winners of the national awards will be revealed at a ceremony in Darwin on November 6.
translated_content: U unutarnjem prijelazu Brisbanea, u New Farmu, kuća Oxlade Drive proglašena je najdražom kućom javnosti na Nacionalnim arhitektonskim nagradama Australije 2014., osvojivši nagradu izbora javnosti. Projektirana od strane arhitekte Jamesa Russella, kuća se ističe ne po veličini, već po pažljivom, klimatski prilagođenom rješenju za subtropski život. Na njenom srcu nalaze se serija dvospratnih paviljona obloženih trajnom drvenom šipkom Ironbark, raspoređenih duž zemljišta s otvorenim dvorištima koje ih razdvajaju. Ova dvorišta nisu samo estetska — ona su funkcionalna. Mekan, dišući zastor od sjene opkoljava ih, filtrira jaku sončevu svjetlost, odbija komarce i muhe i nudi blagu privatnost bez zidova. Arhitekt James Russell opisuje strukturu kao 'lijepi štednjak' — skroman izraz koji sakrije njenu inovaciju. 'Sretni smo ako ljudi vide to kao aviarijum ili okvir za leptire,' rekao je Courier Mailu. 'U Brisbanu imate s muhama i komarcima. Ovaj zastor postaje tihi filter — prirodno hladniji prostor i čini život unutar-i-van kuće jedinstvenim.' Projekt eliminira potrebu za klimatizacijom tako što usmjerava ljetne vjetrove i poziva zimsku sončevu svjetlost kroz pažljivo postavljene otvore. Žiri na Nagradama za arhitekturu Kraljevine Queensland nazvao ga je 'pametnom, odgovarajućom reinterpretacijom mogućnosti unutarnjeg gradskog života', cijeneći kako njegov čvrsti materijalni izbor i prostorna ritmičnost uključuju osjetila i jačaju vezu između unutrašnjosti i vanjskog prostora. Uspjeh kuće leži u njenoj jednostavnosti: nema neverovatnih trikova, samo pametna, temeljita arhitektura koja sluša svoje okruženje. Pobjednici nacionalnih nagrada bit će objavljeni na ceremoniji u Darwinu 6. studenoga.

article_content: Real Madrid star Gareth Bale is continuing to improve his Spanish skills. The 34-year-old, who previously revealed in November that he was fluent in Spanish swear words, shared a photo on Instagram showing a private lesson with his tutor, Michael, on Wednesday evening. Alongside the image, Bale wrote: 'I enjoyed the Spanish class with Michael this afternoon. More work!!' Bale’s dedication comes amid recent fan criticism after he chose not to pass to Cristiano Ronaldo during Real Madrid’s 3-0 victory over Espanyol — a decision that led to a missed opportunity and boos from parts of the Bernabéu crowd. However, Bale quickly silenced doubters with a spectacular free-kick that doubled Real Madrid’s lead before halftime. Cristiano Ronaldo has publicly urged fans to be more supportive of Bale, calling him a vital component of Carlo Ancelotti’s squad. With the second leg of Real Madrid’s Copa del Rey last-16 clash against arch-rivals Atlético Madrid looming on Thursday, the team must overcome a two-goal deficit to advance — making every player’s contribution crucial.

article_content: By Ted Thornhill. PUBLISHED: 09:06 EST, 13 November 2013. | UPDATED: 13:07 EST, 13 November 2013. Christie’s did not disclose the buyer of Francis Bacon’s three-panel painting, Three Studies of Lucian Freud, which sold for £89 million ($142.4 million) on Tuesday. However, speculation centered on Roman Abramovich, the Russian billionaire and owner of Chelsea Football Club, who previously paid £43 million ($86.3 million) in 2008 for Bacon’s Triptych, 1976 — then the highest price ever paid for a Bacon work. Bidding during the November 12 auction at Christie’s in New York was intense. The 1969 triptych, never before offered at auction, carried a pre-sale estimate of approximately $85 million. It ultimately far surpassed Edvard Munch’s The Scream, which sold for $119.9 million at Sotheby’s in May 2012. According to The New York Times, the painting was purchased by Manhattan art dealer William Acquavella, a specialist in 19th- and 20th-century art, on behalf of an unnamed client. A spokesperson for Abramovich declined to comment, leaving public speculation unresolved. The sale marked a new benchmark for the art market, surpassing the previous Bacon record set just months before the 2008 financial crisis, which briefly dampened prices. Since then, an influx of capital from global collectors — particularly from Asia, Russia, and the Middle East — has propelled auction prices to historic highs. Brett Gorvy, Christie’s head of postwar and contemporary art, noted that these collectors are aggressively building world-class collections featuring iconic masterpieces. Francis Outred, head of European postwar and contemporary art at Christie’s, described the triptych as 'a true masterpiece that marks Bacon and Freud’s relationship' and their 'creative and emotional kinship.' He emphasized the striking contrast between the radiant yellow background and the visceral, immediate brushwork, calling it 'a sudden and powerful conversation between two masters.' Three Studies of Lucian Freud is one of only two full-length triptychs of Freud, whose panels were separated for 15 years in the 1970s before being reunited. Christie’s also offered Andy Warhol’s Coca-Cola (estimated $40–60 million) and Jeff Koons’ Balloon Dog (Orange) (estimated $35–55 million). On Wednesday, Sotheby’s attempted to break the $71.7 million record for a Warhol with its offering of Silver Car Crash (Double Disaster), estimated at $60–80 million. Born in Dublin to English parents, Bacon moved to London in 1926. Though self-taught, he began exhibiting in the 1930s and gained international acclaim in the 1940s for his emotionally charged depictions of distorted human forms. He died of a heart attack in Madrid in 1992. Today, his work remains among the most sought-after of 20th-century art.

Christie’s nije otkrio kupca Francis Baconove trodjelne slike Three Studies of Lucian Freud, koja je prodana za 89 milijuna funti (142,4 milijuna dolara) u utorak. Međutim, spekulacije su se usmjerile na Romana Abramovića, ruskog milijardera i vlasnika fudbalskog kluba Chelsea, koji je ranije platio 43 milijuna funti (86,3 milijuna dolara) 2008. godine za Baconovu Triptych, 1976 — tada najvišu cijenu ikad plaćenu za Baconovo djelo. Natječaj tijekom aukcije 12. studenog u Christie’s-u u New Yorku bio je intenzivan. Trodjelna slika iz 1969., nikad ranije ponuđena na aukciji, imala je procijenjenu cijenu od otprilike 85 milijuna dolara. Konačno je daleko premašila Edvarda Muncha, The Scream, koji je prodan za 119,9 milijuna dolara na Sotheby’s-u u svibnju 2012. godine. Prema The New York Timesu, sliku je kupio menhetenski umjetnički trgovac William Acquavella, stručnjak za umjetnost 19. i 20. stoljeća, u ime nepoznatog klijenta. Predstavnik Abramovića je odbio komentirati, ostavljajući javne spekulacije nerešenima. Prodaja je označila novi rekord za tržište umjetnosti, premašivši prethodni Baconov rekord postavljen samo mjesec dana prije financijske krize 2008. godine, koja je privremeno smanjila cijene. Od tada je ulazak kapitala s globalnih tržišta — posebno iz Azije, Rusije i Bliskog istoka — potjerao cijene na povijesno visoke razine. Brett Gorvy, šef za poslijeratnu i savremenu umjetnost u Christie’s-u, naglasio je da ti kupci agresivno grade svjetski klase kolekcije koje sadrže ikonična djela. Francis Outred, šef za europsku poslijeratnu i savremenu umjetnost u Christie’s-u, opisao je trodjelnu sliku kao 'pravi vrhunac koji označava odnos Bacona i Freuda' i njihovu 'kreativnu i emocionalnu povezanost.' Naglasio je oštrinu kontrasta između zračnog žutog pozadinskog boja i vruće, neposredne četkice, nazivajući je 'naglim i moćnim razgovorom između dva majstora.' Three Studies of Lucian Freud je jedna od samo dvije puno-veličinske trodjelne slike Freuda, čiji su dijelovi bili odvojeni 15 godina u 1970-ima prije nego što su ponovno spojeni. Christie’s je također ponudio Andy Warholovu Coca-Colu (procijenjena cijena 40–60 milijuna dolara) i Jeff Koonsovu Balloon Dog (Orange) (procijenjena cijena 35–55 milijuna dolara). U srijedu, Sotheby’s je pokušao premašiti rekord od 71,7 milijuna dolara za Warhola ponuđajući monumentalnu Silver Car Crash (Double Disaster), procijenjenu na 60–80 milijuna dolara. Rođen u Dublinu od engleskih roditelja, Bacon se preselio u London 1926. godine. Iako samouki, počeo je izlagati radove 1930-ih godina i stekao međunarodno priznanje 1940-ih zbog emotivno opterećenih prikaza izobličenih ljudskih formi. Umro je od srčanog udara u Madridu 1992. godine. Danas njegova djela pripadaju među najtraženijima u 20. stoljeću.

article_content: Twelve A-10 Warthog fighter jets are being relocated from Afghanistan to Kuwait as part of a renewed effort to degrade ISIS operations across Iraq and Syria. Designed during the Cold War to take down Soviet tank columns, these rugged aircraft have become indispensable in modern asymmetric warfare thanks to their ability to fly low, slow, and stay airborne for hours—perfect for spotting and engaging mobile enemy units. Their signature weapon, a 30mm rotary cannon capable of unleashing nearly 4,000 rounds per minute, combined with guided missiles and bombs, makes them lethal against lightly armed fighters hiding among civilians or moving in small convoys. Alongside the A-10s, six MQ-9 Reaper drones will begin operations, providing persistent surveillance and precision strikes from above. Unlike faster jets that zip through target zones, both platforms can hover for extended periods, waiting for fleeting opportunities—a convoy appearing on a desert road, a commander stepping out of a vehicle. This patience is crucial: according to recent data, roughly 75% of sorties over the past three months did not result in weapons being fired. Instead, crews are trained to identify and track high-value, time-sensitive targets known as 'pop-up threats.' The decision to expand airpower came after a major multinational planning summit involving over 200 commanders from 33 countries. While the U.S. remains the dominant force, regional allies like Morocco are now contributing F-16s to the coalition. Still, the challenge isn’t lack of firepower—it’s finding reliable targets. ISIS blends into civilian populations, moves unpredictably, and often abandons positions before strikes arrive. Intelligence gathering relies on satellite imagery, high-altitude U-2 recon flights, and ground teams—including U.S. special operators and CIA assets—to pinpoint locations. To prevent civilian deaths that could fuel ISIS propaganda, every strike must be personally approved by General Lloyd Austin, head of U.S. Central Command. The A-10’s legendary resilience—shielded by 1,200 pounds of titanium armor, able to fly on one engine even after losing half a wing—makes it ideal for operating in hostile airspace where small arms and RPGs are common. Pilots have relied on these planes in Afghanistan to protect troops just yards away from danger, earning deep loyalty from ground forces. Despite repeated attempts by the Air Force to phase out the aging fleet, the Army and frontline units have consistently pushed back, insisting the Warthog’s unique capabilities are irreplaceable. As a result, these 'ugly but effective' jets are expected to remain in service well into the 2020s. Yet, even with enhanced airpower, success hinges on more than technology: it depends on accurate intelligence, disciplined rules of engagement, and the ability to adapt to an enemy that refuses to fight like a traditional army.
translated_content: Dvanaest A-10 Warthog borbenih aviona premješteno je iz Afganistana u Kuvajt kao dio obnove traganja za slabljenjem operacija ISIS-a u Iraku i Siriji. Projektirani tijekom Hladnog rata da uništavaju sovjetske tenkovske kolone, ovi čvrsti avioni postali su nezamjenjivi u modernoj asimetričnoj ratovanju zbog svoje sposobnosti leta nisko, sporo i ostajanja u zraku satima – savršeni za otkrivanje i napadanje pokretnih neprijateljskih jedinica. Njihov ključni oružje, 30 mm rotacijski top koji može ispaliti gotovo 4.000 metaka po minuti, uz vodene rakete i bombe, čini ih smrtonosnim protiv svjetlo naoružanih boraca koji se kriju među civilima ili kreću se u malim konvojima. Pored A-10 aviona, šest MQ-9 Reaper zmaja počet će s operacijama, pružajući trajnu nadzor i precizne udare s visine. U suprotnosti od bržih aviona koji prolaze kroz zone ciljeva, obje platforme mogu dugo lebdjeti, čekajući prolazne prilike – konvoj koji se pojavi na pustinjskom putu, zapovjednik koji izlazi iz vozila. Ova strpljivost je ključna: prema nedavnim podacima, otprilike 75% letova u posljednja tri mjeseca nije rezultiralo ispaljivanjem oružja. Umjesto toga, posade su obučene da identificiraju i prate visokovrijedne, vremenski ograničene ciljeve poznate kao 'pop-up ciljevi'. Odluka o proširenju zračne snage donesena je nakon velike višeodrasle planirajuće sastanke u kojem je sudjelovalo preko 200 zapovjednika iz 33 zemlje. Iako SAD ostaju dominirajuća sila, regionalni saveznici poput Maroka sada doprinose F-16 avionima koaliciji. Međutim, izazov nije u nedostatku vatrenog moći – već u pronalaženju pouzdanih ciljeva. ISIS se stopa s civilnim stanovništvom, kreće se nepredvidivo i često napušta pozicije prije nego što dolaze udari. Prikupljanje obavijesti temelji se na satelitskim slikama, visokoletnim letovima U-2 istraživačkih aviona i zemaljskim timovima – uključujući američke specijalne operativce i CIA – kako bi se precizno locirale lokacije. Da bi se spriječile građanske žrtve koje bi pogonule propagandu ISIS-a, svaki udar mora biti osobno odobren od strane generala Lloyd Austina, zapovjednika Središnjeg komanda. Legendarna otpornost A-10-a – zaštićen 1.200 funti titanskih oklopom, sposoban letjeti na jednom motoru čak i nakon gubitka polovice krila – čini ga idealnim za rad u neprijateljskom zraku gdje su malorazmjerna oružja i RPG-ovi česti. Piloti su se oslanjali na ove avione u Afganistanu da zaštitite vojnike na udaljenosti od nekoliko jardi, stječući duboku lojalnost od kopnene vojske. Unatoč ponovljenim pokušajima Zračne snage da ukloni staru flotu, vojska i borbeni jedinice konzistentno su se suprotstavljale, insistirajući da su Warthogove jedinstvene sposobnosti neprocjenjive. Stoga se ovi 'ružni ali učinkoviti' avioni očekuju da će ostati u službi do 2020-ih godina. Ipak, čak i s jačom zračnom snagom, uspjeh ovisi o više od tehnologije: ovisi o točnoj obavijesti, discipliniranim pravilima angažmana i sposobnosti prilagodbe neprijatelju koji se ne borí kao tradicionalna vojska.

article_content: Erica Hill, the newly appointed co-host of CBS’s 'The Early Show,' sees her new role not as a reward, but as a meaningful challenge. Speaking on CNN’s 'Reliable Sources' with Howard Kurtz, she dismissed lingering concerns about the show’s long-standing ratings slump. 'What’s done is done,' she said. 'My energy is all about what’s next.' Despite consistently finishing third behind NBC’s 'Today' and ABC’s 'Good Morning America,' Hill is undeterred, pledging her full commitment to reshaping the program’s direction. She’ll be stepping onto the set alongside Chris Wragge, her longtime weekend co-anchor since 2008. Meanwhile, longtime hosts Harry Smith and Maggie Rodriguez will stay on through early January, easing the handover. Hill admitted the transition isn’t easy — especially since she holds deep respect and affection for Smith and Rodriguez, both as journalists and close friends. 'It’s awkward, yes,' she added, 'but it’s also deeply human.' For his part, Smith, who spent 17 years anchoring morning shows at CBS, reflected on his time with warmth. On CBS Radio, he bid farewell to the daily grind, calling it 'one of the best seats in the house.' He reminisced about covering breaking news, interviewing celebrities, and even cooking with top chefs. 'I’m not leaving journalism — just this particular chair,' he said. Before joining CBS, Hill built her reputation on CNN, where she was a regular presence on 'AC360,' often sharing the desk with Anderson Cooper in lively, late-night news segments.

'Moj se energija usmjerava na ono što dolazi.' Iako se emisija dosad redovito nalazila na trećem mjestu iza NBC-ove 'Today' i ABC-ove 'Good Morning America,' Hill je neodlučna i obećala punu posvećenost promjeni smjera programa. Suradit će s Chrisom Wraggeom, svojim dugogodišnjim suradnikom na vikendnim emitiranjima od 2008. Međutim, dugo godina vodeći voditelji Harry Smith i Maggie Rodriguez ostajat će na čelu emisije do početka siječnja, olakšavajući prijelaz. Hill je priznala da je prijelaz težak — posebno jer duboko poštuje i cijeni Smitha i Rodriguez, ne samo kao kolege i novinare, već i kao prijatelje. 'Nije lako, to je istina,' dodala je, 'ali to je i duboko ljudski.' S druge strane, Smith, koji je 17 godina vodio jutarnje emisije na CBS-u, reflektirao je svoje vrijeme s toplinom. Na CBS radiju, oprostio se od svakodnevnog ritma, nazivajući ga 'jednim od najboljih mjesta u kući.' Sjećao se kako pokrivao važne vijesti, susretavao filmske zvijezde i čak kuvao s vrhunskim šefovima kuhinje. 'Ne napuštam novinarstvo — samo ovu stolicu,' rekao je. Prije nego što se pridružila CBS-u, Hill je izgradila svoju reputaciju na CNN-u, gdje je bila redovna prisutna na 'AC360', često dijeleći stol s Andersonom Cooperom u živahnim, kasnonoćnim vijestima.

article_content:
Joseph E. Stiglitz, Nobel laureate in Economics and former chief economist at the World Bank, argues that the 2008 financial crisis was not an accident — but the predictable result of systemic failures. While many were shocked by the depth of the collapse, Stiglitz and others had long warned of the dangers. The root cause? A dangerous mix of reckless deregulation, flawed monetary policy, and misaligned incentives within financial institutions. President Bush’s claim that the crisis stemmed simply from 'too many houses' ignores the deeper machinery behind the housing bubble. The Federal Reserve, under Alan Greenspan, flooded the economy with cheap credit while turning a blind eye to risky lending practices. This created a speculative frenzy fueled by excessive leverage — a classic financial trap disguised as innovation. New financial instruments didn’t solve problems — they obscured them. Complex derivatives hid the true extent of debt, making risks invisible until it was too late. The Fed, desperate to offset the fallout from the dot-com bust and sluggish growth after the 2001 tax cuts, replaced one bubble with another: housing. Household savings dropped to historic lows. Americans weren’t building wealth — they were borrowing against inflated home values. Meanwhile, the Iraq War drove up oil prices, siphoning billions from domestic spending. The economy was propped up on borrowed money and borrowed time. At the heart of the crisis were financial executives whose compensation rewarded short-term gains over long-term stability. They weren’t managing risk — they were manufacturing it. Their incentives encouraged gambling with other people’s money, and the system let them get away with it. This isn’t the first time Wall Street has crashed and then begged Washington for rescue. It’s a recurring pattern revealing deep flaws in our financial architecture. Stiglitz proposes six critical reforms: 1. Realign executive pay: Bonuses should be tied to five-year performance, not annual results, to discourage reckless behavior.
2. Create a Financial Product Safety Commission to vet financial instruments — just as we do with food and drugs — to protect consumers and institutions alike.
3. Establish a Financial Systems Stability Commission to monitor systemic risk across the entire financial network.
4. Introduce 'speed bumps' — limits on rapid credit expansion — to prevent lending booms that inevitably lead to busts.
5. Strengthen consumer protection laws to ban predatory lending and abusive credit card practices.
6. Enforce antitrust measures to break up institutions that are 'too big to fail.' If a firm’s collapse threatens the economy, it’s too big to exist. Stiglitz acknowledges that financial innovators will always find ways to evade rules. But these reforms won’t eliminate risk — they’ll make the next crisis less likely and far less devastating. The goal isn’t to stop progress — it’s to ensure progress serves society, not just shareholders.

article_content: Despite individual accolades and past triumphs with England, this may well be one of the most memorable days of Stuart Pearce’s managerial career. With Ben Osborn’s stunning injury-time winner, the ecstatic Nottingham Forest manager sprinted onto the pitch — a scene echoing his legendary penalty celebration against Spain at Euro ’96. ‘Psycho is back!’ roared Forest fans in one corner of the iPro Stadium. Pearce thrust his chest forward, arm raised high — a gesture of unity with the supporters who stood by him through a fortnight of turmoil. The 2-1 comeback victory over rivals Derby County wasn’t just three points — it was a lifeline. After slipping to 13th in the Championship, Pearce faced mounting pressure. Yet, with 15 minutes left and trailing, few expected Forest to turn things around — especially on Derby’s home turf, where they’d conceded just two goals since early November. Britt Assombalonga’s fierce finish from close range leveled the score, triggering Pearce’s trademark fist-pump celebration. Then came Osborn — a 20-year-old academy graduate — who netted his first professional goal in the most dramatic fashion possible. ‘All my mates are Derby fans,’ he grinned. ‘They were texting me last night: don’t score the winner.’ Derby had taken an early lead through an unchallenged own goal by Henri Lansbury, and for much of the first half, Forest looked rattled. Pearce paced the touchline, frustrated by a missed penalty appeal when Jake Buxton pulled Michail Antonio’s shirt. But as so often in the Championship, momentum shifted in an instant. Assombalonga’s equalizer sparked pandemonium, and Osborn’s winner sent the stadium into raptures. Pearce, visibly moved, declared: ‘I’m entrenched in Nottingham. This is more than just a job. I thrive at the all-or-nothing end of football.’ His words resonated — not just as manager, but as a man who feels every heartbeat of this club. Derby manager Steve McClaren lamented his team’s collapse: ‘We showed our total immaturity — we got overexcited and lost our shape.’ A Derby fan even rushed the pitch at full time, attempting to attack Kelvin Wilson before being tackled by steward Jamaal Lascelles — a chaotic footnote to a historic day. Amidst the chaos, one truth emerged: this result didn’t just lift Forest off the bottom half — it reignited belief. For Pearce, it may have been the turning point he needed.

article_content: Greece’s Roma community is demanding justice after the death of 17-year-old Christos Michalopoulos, who was fatally shot during a police chase on November 11 near Thebes. At his funeral, dozens of grieving teenagers — classmates and friends — stood in silence, some fainting from shock, as mourners chanted his name like roll call: 'Christos Michalopoulos! Present!' This marks the third time in under three years that a Roma teenager has died in a police incident in Greece. The Hellenic Police claim Michalopoulos was driving recklessly, ignored commands to stop, and attempted to seize an officer’s firearm during a high-risk stop. But family and witnesses offer a starkly different account: that officers violently pulled him from the car, struck him, and shot him at close range. A leaked CCTV recording captures the moments before the shooting: police shouting 'Stop!' followed by rapid knocks on the car window, then gunfire and screams — including Christos’s brother crying, 'What did the child do for you to shoot him?' Forensic findings contradict the police version: no trace of Michalopoulos’s DNA was found on the weapon, and the bullet entered his clavicle at close range. His family’s lawyer alleges evidence was deliberately destroyed — the crime scene washed, the car cleaned, and the victim’s hands wiped. Roma youth across Greece describe daily harassment: random stops, public body searches, and threats. 'The cops are all racist,' said 18-year-old Panagiotis Chatzidiakos, a friend. 'We’re afraid to move around.' Amnesty International has called for a prompt, transparent, and independent investigation — including into whether racism motivated the killing. The accused officer, temporarily suspended, was released after giving testimony and has denied wrongdoing, claiming self-defense. This tragedy echoes the 2021 killing of Nikos Sampanis and the 2022 killing of Kostas Frangoulis — both Roma teens killed in similar police pursuits. Advocates warn: 'A sin... became a sin... and is becoming a sin again. Always for Roma.' As investigations continue amid widespread protests, the Roma community asks: How many more deaths must occur before Greece confronts its systemic racism?

article_content: If you've thrown a birthday party recently, you might have experienced the shortages or price hikes affecting the helium market. But balloon customers aren’t the only ones impacted. Scientists, manufacturers, and industries relying on helium are also feeling the strain. Without a long-term strategy to manage this vital, non-renewable resource, conditions could worsen. Liquid helium has enabled countless innovations — from cell phones and laptops to medical breakthroughs like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). These devices depend on superconducting magnets cooled by liquid helium to generate strong, stable magnetic fields. Fiber optic cable and semiconductor manufacturers also rely heavily on helium. For researchers, helium isn’t a luxury — it’s essential. Interruptions in supply can render weeks or months of work useless. Rising prices have consumed significant portions of research budgets, creating severe financial pressure. One major cause of the shortage is helium’s nature as a trace byproduct of natural gas extraction. Only 14 of thousands of natural gas sites worldwide contain enough helium to make separation economically viable. When even a few of these sites shut down for maintenance, global supply dips sharply. Decades ago, the U.S. established the Federal Helium Reserve in the Texas panhandle to secure supply for defense, space, and scientific research. In the 1960s and '70s, the government amassed large quantities. But in 1996, Congress mandated the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to sell off the reserve to recover costs, with all sales required to end by 2015. Today, BLM’s sales account for over 30% of global helium supply. Once they stop, experts predict dramatic price increases and supply shortages. At BLM’s request, the National Research Council recommended long-term management strategies — including protecting critical users and developing sustainable sourcing plans. It’s time to update U.S. helium policy. Done right, we can ensure future generations enjoy birthday balloons — and continue developing life-changing technologies.

article_content: Call it a false memory. A trick of the mind. Or a 'misremembrance.' Television anchor Brian Williams is not the first person to be embarrassed by claiming a recollection that never actually happened. Recent history reveals how several prominent figures have experienced what experts label false 'flashbulb' memories. Astrophysicist and television host Neil deGrasse Tyson, a protégé of the late Carl Sagan, once claimed he heard President George W. Bush make a remark intended to distinguish Judeo-Christian Americans from fundamentalist Muslims. Tyson’s assertion was long published on the Hayden Planetarium’s website, which he leads. 'After the 9/11 attacks, when President George W. Bush, in a speech aimed at distinguishing the U.S. from Muslim fundamentalists, said, 'Our God is the God who named the stars,' Tyson remarked. 'The problem is, two-thirds of all named stars have Arabic names. I don’t think he knew this—it would undermine his point.' Fact-checkers found Tyson’s recollection incorrect. The New York Times later published an opinion piece in December 2014 by psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel Simons examining the Tyson incident and 'Why Our Memory Fails Us.' 'In his post-9/11 speech, Mr. Bush actually said, 'The enemy of America is not our many Muslim friends,' and said nothing about stars,' wrote the professors. 'Mr. Bush had, however, once made a similar statement—in 2003, during a tribute to the astronauts lost in the Columbia space shuttle disaster: 'The same creator who names the stars also knows the names of the seven souls we mourn today.' Tyson later posted an apology on Facebook. 'Blogosphere headlines accused me of being a compulsive liar and a fabricator,' he wrote. 'I here publicly apologize to the President for casting his quote in the context of contrasting religions rather than as a poetic reference to the lost souls of Columbia. I have no excuse, other than both events—so close together—deeply upset me. In retrospect, I’m surprised I remembered any details from either.' Interestingly, as Chabris and Simons noted, even President Bush himself suffered a false memory. He repeatedly recalled watching the first plane strike the North Tower of the World Trade Center on live television before entering a Florida classroom on September 11, 2001. In reality, no live footage existed at that time—he was informed of the impact, but did not witness it visually. This misrecollection was analyzed in a 2004 scholarly essay by then-graduate student Daniel Greenberg of Duke University, now a memory expert and professor at the College of Charleston. In 'President Bush’s False 'Flashbulb' Memory of 9/11/01,' Greenberg found two of Bush’s accounts impossible due to timing constraints. 'How can we explain these inconsistencies?' Greenberg asked. 'Over the past century, numerous studies have shown that people frequently suffer from false memories—fictitious recollections of events that never occurred.' Despite access to advisors, Bush’s case resembled a near-textbook example of false recall. During his 2012 presidential campaign in Michigan, Mitt Romney claimed to have witnessed the golden jubilee of the automobile in Detroit on June 1, 1946, stating his father served as master of ceremonies. 'I think my dad had a job… being the grandmaster or whatever of the 50th celebration of the automobile in Detroit,' Romney told a rally. 'They painted Woodward Avenue with gold paint. My memory’s a little foggy… but yeah, I was probably four or something like that.' But Romney was born on March 12, 1947—the event occurred nine months before his birth. The Toronto Star exposed the discrepancy. 'The timelines suggest Romney could well have been conceived that day. But it is inconceivable he was actually there,' the paper noted. A Romney aide clarified: 'Mitt doesn’t say he was there. In fact, he says his memory was foggy. He was simply telling the story about his dad.' In her 2008 presidential campaign, Hillary Clinton described arriving in Bosnia in 1996 under sniper fire. 'I remember landing under sniper fire… we just ran with our heads down to get into the vehicles,' she said. Video footage from Tuzla Airport, however, showed Clinton calmly exiting the aircraft with her daughter Chelsea, smiling and conversing with locals—including an 8-year-old girl who gave her a poem—and greeting troops. The Philadelphia Daily News confronted her with the footage. Clinton responded: 'I misspoke. That was a minor blip.' In a radio interview, she added: 'I’ve been in the public eye for many years. This happens to anyone.' James Frey’s memoir, 'A Million Little Pieces,' became a bestseller after being selected by Oprah Winfrey’s book club. The book, detailing his struggles with addiction and recovery, moved millions. But in 2006, The Smoking Gun revealed extensive fabrications: Frey was jailed for hours, not 87 days; key events were invented; characters were composites. Frey later confessed to Oprah: 'I made a mistake. I made a lot of mistakes.' When pressed, he said: 'I think probably both—I lied, and I made mistakes.' He defended the book as a memoir based on memory, asserting: 'I did the best I could to recreate my life according to my memory.' Winfrey retracted her endorsement, saying she felt 'conned.'

Brian Williams, voditelj televizijske emisije, nije prva osoba koja je bila u sramoti zbog tvrdnje o sjećanju koje nikada nije stvarno dogodilo. Nedavna povijest pokazuje kako su nekoliko poznatih ličnosti doživjelo ono što stručnjaci nazivaju lažnim 'flashbulb' sjećanjem. Astrofizikar i televizijski voditelj Neil deGrasse Tyson, učenik kasnog Carla Sagana, jednom je tvrdio da je čuo predsjednika Georgea W. Bushea kako kaže napomenu namijenjenu razdvajanju Judeo-kristianskih Amerikanaca od fundamentalističkih muslimana. Tysonova tvrdnja dugo je objavljivana na web-stranici Haydenove planetarije koju on vodi. 'Nakon napada 9/11, kad je predsjednik George W. Bush, u govoru namijenjenom razdvajanju SAD-a od fundamentalističkih muslimana, rekao: 'Naš Bog je Bog koji je imenovao zvijezde,' rekao je Tyson. 'Problem je u tome što dvije trećine svih imenovanih zvijezda imaju arapska imena. Mislim da on to nije znao—to bi oslabilo njegovu točku.' Provjeritelji činjenica otkrili su da je Tysonovo sjećanje pogrešno. The New York Times kasnije je objavio mišljenje u prosincu 2014. od psihologa Christophera Chabrisa i Daniela Simonsa koji su istraživali Tysonov slučaj i 'Zašto naše sjećanje ne uspijeva.' 'U svom govoru nakon 9/11, g. Bush je zapravo rekao: 'Neprijatelj Amerike nisu naši mnogi muslimanski prijatelji,' i ništa nije rekao o zvijezdama,' napisali su profesori. 'G. Bush je, međutim, jednom rekao sličnu izjavu—2003. godine, u čast astronautima koji su poginuli u nesreći svemirskog broda Columbia: 'Isti stvoritelj koji je imenovao zvijezde također zna imena sedam duša koje žalimo.' Tyson je kasnije objavio izvinjenje na Facebooku. 'Blogovi su me optuživali da sam kompulzivni lažac i izmišljač,' napisao je. 'Ovdje javno izvinjavam predsjedniku jer sam njegov citat stavio u kontekst suprotstavljanja religija umjesto kao poetski refren za izgubljene duše Columbia. Nemam opravdanje, osim što su oba događaja—toliko bliska jedan drugome—duboko me uzrujala. U povratnoj perspektivi, iznenađen sam što sam se sjetio bilo kakvih detalja iz bilo kojeg od njih.' Zanimljivo, kako su Chabris i Simons primijetili, čak je i sam predsjednik Bush doživio lažno sjećanje. On je ponavljao kako je video kako prvi avion udara u sjevernu kulu Svjetskog trgovinskog centra na živoj emisiji prije nego što je ušao u učionicu u Floridi 11. rujna 2001. Stvarnost je bila da nije postojala nikakva živa snimka u tom trenutku—bio je obaviješten da je avion udario, ali nije video to. Ovo pogrešno sjećanje analizirano je u 2004. godini u znanstvenom eseju tadašnjeg studenta diplomca Daniela Greenberga sa Sveučilišta Duke, danas stručnjaka za ljudsku memoriju i profesora na Sveučilištu College of Charleston u Južnoj Karolini. U radu pod naslovom 'Lažno 'flashbulb' sjećanje predsjednika Bushea o 9/11/01,' Greenberg je otkrio da su dvije od Bushevih verzija nemoguće zbog vremenskih ograničenja. 'Kako možemo objasniti ove neslaganja?' pitao je Greenberg. 'Tijekom posljednjeg stoljeća, brojne studije pokazale su da ljudi često pate od lažnih sjećanja—fiktivnih sjećanja na događaje koji se nikada nisu dogodili.' Unatoč pristupu savjetnicima, Bushov slučaj podsjećao je na gotovo tekstualni primjer lažnog općeg sjećanja. Tijekom svoje kampanje za predsjedništvo 2012. godine u Michiganu, Mitt Romney tvrdio je da je bio svjedok zlatnog jubileja automobila u Detroitu 1. lipnja 1946., navodeći da je njegov otac bio voditelj događaja. 'Mislim da je moj otac imao posao… bio veliki voditelj ili što već 50. obljetnice automobila u Detroitu,' rekao je Romney na mitingu. 'Pozlaćeni su Woodward Avenue. Moje sjećanje je malo mutno… ali da, vjerojatno sam bio četiri ili nešto slično.' Ali Romney je rođen 12. ožujka 1947.—dogadaj se dogodio devet mjeseci prije njegova rođenja. The Toronto Star je otkrila nesuglasicu. 'Vremenski rasporedi sugeriraju da bi Romney mogao biti zatrudnjen tog dana. Ali je nemoguće da je bio stvarno tu,' navela je novina. Pomoćnik Romneysa pojasnio je: 'Mitt ne kaže da je bio tu. Zapravo kaže da mu je sjećanje mutno. Jednostavno je pričao priču o svom ocu.' U svojoj kampanji za predsjedništvo 2008. godine, Hillary Clinton opisala je kako je pristajala na Bosni pod vatrom snajperista. 'Sjećam se da sam pristajala pod snajperiskom vatrom… samo smo trčali s glavama niz da bismo ušli u vozila,' rekla je. Snimke s aerodroma Tuzla, međutim, pokazale su kako je Clinton mirno izašla iz aviona uz svoju kćer Chelsea, osmijehom i razgovarala s lokalnim stanovnicima—uključujući 8-godišnju djevojčicu koja joj je dala pjesmu—i pozdravljala američke vojnike. Philadelphia Daily News je suočila ju s tim snimkama. Clinton je odgovorila: 'Pogriješila sam. To je bio mali propust.' U radio intervjuu dodala je: 'Bila sam u javnom životu godinama. Ovo se događa svima.' James Freyjeva autobiografija, 'A Million Little Pieces,' postala je bestseler nakon što ju je Oprah Winfrey odabrala za svoju književnu klub. Knjiga, koja detaljno opisuje njegove borbe s ovisnošću i oporavkom, dirnula je milione. Ali 2006. godine The Smoking Gun otkrio je ekstenzivne izmišljotine: Frey je proveo samo nekoliko sati u zatvoru, a ne 87 dana; ključni događaji su izmišljeni; likovi su kompoziti. Frey je kasnije priznao Oprah: 'Pogriješio sam. Napravio sam puno grešaka.' Kad su ga pritisnuli, rekao je: 'Mislim da su oboje—lažio sam i pogriješio sam.' Obranio je knjigu kao autobiografiju temeljenu na sjećanju, tvrdeći: 'Učinio sam sve što sam mogao da ponovno stvorim svoj život prema svom sjećanju.' Winfrey je povukla podršku, rekavši da se osjećala 'prevarena.'

article_content: On Saturday afternoon, Darrius Kennedy, a 51-year-old man from Hempstead, Long Island, was fatally shot by New York City police officers near Times Square following a prolonged encounter. Authorities say the incident began when officers approached Kennedy after observing what appeared to be a marijuana cigarette. He became agitated, concealed the cigarette, and drew an 11-inch knife, raising it above his head while putting on a blue bandana. As officers attempted to arrest him, Kennedy walked south along 7th Avenue, ignoring repeated commands to drop the weapon. Despite being sprayed with pepper spray six times, he continued moving forward. Near the intersection of 7th Avenue and 37th Street, he advanced toward uniformed officers, prompting two of them to fire, striking him in the torso. Kennedy was transported to Bellevue Hospital and pronounced dead at 3:42 p.m. Two officers involved were treated for tinnitus, likely from the gunfire; a third officer received treatment for eye irritation due to pepper spray exposure. All three officers have been placed on administrative leave pending a full review by the NYPD. Video footage recorded by CNN iReporter David Fowler captured bystanders reacting loudly as the pursuit unfolded through a busy pedestrian zone.

Prema vlastima, incident se počeo kada su policajci pristupili Kennediju nakon što su primijetili što je izgledalo kao cigareta marihuane. Postao je uzbuđen, sakrio cigaretu i izvukao 11-inch nož, podigao ga iznad glave dok je stavljao plavi bandanu na glavu. Dok su policajci pokušavali arrestirati ga, Kennedy je hodao prema jugu uz 7. aveniju, ignorirajući ponovljene naredbe da spusti oružje.
