article_content: On Wednesday, Israeli warplanes carried out an airstrike inside Syria, targeting what U.S. officials described as a convoy suspected of transporting Russian-made surface-to-air missile parts—possibly headed for Hezbollah in Lebanon. While Syria and its allies called the attack barbaric and a flagrant breach of international law, Washington insisted the strike was limited and unrelated to concerns over Syria’s chemical weapons arsenal. Syrian state media claimed the strike hit a defense research center near Damascus, killing two employees and wounding five, linking it to efforts by rebel groups to seize the facility. But a senior U.S. official countered that no such facility was damaged—only a moving convoy. The weapons, they said, were intended to bolster Hezbollah, which both Iran and Syria support, and which Israel views as a major security threat. Regional powers reacted swiftly: Iran’s deputy foreign minister warned of 'dire consequences' for Israel, echoing earlier threats that any strike on Syria would be treated as an attack on Iran itself. Russia, a staunch ally of Damascus, labeled the action an 'unprovoked violation' of the U.N. Charter. Meanwhile, Syria formally lodged a complaint with the U.N. peacekeeping force stationed in the Golan Heights, demanding accountability under the 1974 disengagement agreement. Analysts believe Hezbollah is racing to stockpile advanced arms before Syria’s weakened regime loses control. Past transfers of Scud missiles capable of carrying chemical warheads have raised alarms in Israel. Yet U.S. officials stressed this operation wasn’t prompted by fears of chemical weapons proliferation. Though Israel hasn’t officially commented, experts like Michael O’Hanlon of the Brookings Institution said the strike, while significant, doesn’t yet signal a major escalation—but retaliation remains a real risk. The U.N. expressed deep concern but admitted it lacked clarity on the details. As tensions simmer, Syria’s ambassador to Lebanon hinted at a possible 'surprise retaliation,' leaving the region on edge.

article_content: Remember those carefree days when a gallon of gas was only $5? Or when you could mail a letter for a mere 50 cents? Saying those words out loud now feels surreal — trying to imagine how young Americans today will look back on the early 2020s and recall when gas cost five dollars a gallon and a postage stamp was half a dollar. Back before prices began to surge. Will it happen? Will the prices we’re heading toward — $20-a-gallon gas, $6 for a first-class stamp — one day seem like unbelievable bargains? It feels both impossible and inevitable. If, as some experts predict, gas hits $5 this summer, it could influence the presidential campaign. CNN’s Jack Cafferty noted on 'The Situation Room' that regardless of the causes — Middle East tensions, refinery closures, or summer travel demand — 'the American public has always tended to blame the person in the White House for high gas prices.' Beyond politics, we stand on the edge of a symbolic threshold: $5 gas and 50-cent stamps — both recommended by the U.S. Postal Service. It’s sticker shock on a national scale. Will people accept this double hit as unavoidable, or will they feel: Enough is enough? Economists cite inflation and cost adjustments, but nostalgia isn’t about numbers — it’s about freedom. The song 'See the U.S.A. in Your Chevrolet' wasn’t sung by a nation worried about fuel costs. In 1950, gas cost roughly 27 cents; by 1970, it had climbed to just 35 cents. Roads stretched wide open. As Dan Seals sang in 'My Old Yellow Car': 'There was no road too winding and nowhere too far / With two bucks of gas and my old yellow car.' We mark our lives by milestones — the first time you bought gas, the first stamp you ever used. From 1932 to 1958, the postage stamp stayed at 3 cents. When it rose to 4 cents in '58, it made headlines. By the time it hits 50 cents, no one will need to ask why. Operating the Postal Service has fixed costs — mostly labor — and revenue is collapsing amid email and declining mail volume. Last quarter, the Postal Service lost $3.3 billion while mail volume dropped 6%. Holiday card sales fell from 2.7 billion in 1995 to 1.5 billion recently. Understanding the reasons doesn’t soften the blow. $5 gas and 50-cent stamps aren’t luxuries — they’re necessities. That’s why the frustration runs deep. Their symbolism lies in their ubiquity. And if one day Americans look back on $5 gas and 50-cent stamps with the same wistfulness older generations feel for 31-cent gas and 3-cent stamps… well, that seems unthinkable. Yet so did this.
translated_content: Sjetite li se tih slobodnih dana kada je litar goriva koštao samo 5 dolara? Ili kada ste mogli poslati pismo za samo 50 centi? Govoriti te riječi na glas danas osjeća se nerealno — pokušavate zamisliti kako će današnji mladi Amerikanci gledati natrag na početak 2020-ih i sjećati se kad je gorivo koštalo pet dolara po litru, a poštna marka pola dolara. Prije nego što su cijene počele rasti. Da li će se to dogoditi? Da li će cijene ka koje se mi približavamo — 20 dolara po litru goriva, 6 dolara za prvu klasu — jednog dana izgledati kao nevjerojatni uštedi? Čini se nemoguće i neizbježno istovremeno. Ako, kao što neki stručnjaci predviđaju, gorivo dostigne 5 dolara ovog ljeta, to bi moglo utjecati na predsjedničku kampanju. CNN-ov Jack Cafferty je napomenuo na 'The Situation Room' da bez obzira na uzroke — napon u Bliskom istoku, zatvaranje rafinerija ili povećana potražnja tijekom ljetnih odmora — 'američka javnost uvijek je tendirala kriviti osobu u Bijeloj kući za visoke cijene goriva.' Izvan politike, nalazimo se na rubu simboličke granice: 5 dolara za gorivo i 50-centne poštanske marke — obje preporučene od strane U.S. pošte. To je šok od cijena na nacionalnoj razini. Hoće li ljudi prihvatiti ovaj dvostruki udar kao neizbježan, ili će osjetiti: Dovoljno je dovoljno? Ekonomisti navode inflaciju i prilagodbe, ali nostalgija nije o brojkama — već o slobodi. Pjesma 'See the U.S.A. in Your Chevrolet' nije pjevana od strane nacije koja se brine o troškovima punjenja rezervoara. Godine 1950. gorivo je koštalo otprilike 27 centi; 1970. je poraslo na samo 35 centi. Ceste su čekale. Kako je Dan Seals pjevao u svojoj divnoj, ali zanemarivanoj pjesmi o radosti vožnje, 'My Old Yellow Car': 'Nije bilo puta predivnog ni mjesta predalekog / Sa dva dolara goriva i mojom starom žutom kolom.' Označujemo svoj život preko kilometarskih znakova — trenutak kad ste prvi put kupili gorivo, prva marka koju ste ikada primijetili. Od 1932. do 1958. godine, cijena poštanske marke nije se mijenjala. Tijekom tih 26 godina, ostala je na 3 centa. Kad je konačno porasla na 4 centa 1958., to je bilo velika vijest. Kad god dostigne 50 centi, nitko više neće morati pitati zašto. Funkcioniranje Pošte ima fiksne troškove — uglavnom povezane s radnom snagom — a prihodi nestaju u doba e-pošte i padanja količine pošte. U zadnjem financijskom kvartalu, Pošta je izgubila 3,3 milijarde dolara, dok je količina pošte pala za 6%. Prodaja božićnih kartica pala je s 2,7 milijarde 1995. na 1,5 milijarde nedavno. Razumijevanje razloga ne uklanja bol. 5 dolara goriva i 50-centne marke nisu luksuzi — to su nužnosti. Zato frustracija duboko prolazi. Njihova simbolika leži u njihovoj sveprisutnosti. I ako jednog dana Amerikanci gledaju natrag na 5 dolara goriva i 50-centne marke s istom tužnom željom koju stariji generacije osjećaju za 31-centno gorivo i 3-centnu marku… pa, to se čini nemogućim. Ali i ovo se činilo nemogućim.

article_content: Andy Murray’s struggles on the clay continued in Rome, where he fell to Richard Gasquet in the third round. Despite fighting hard to win the first set in a tense tiebreak, Murray couldn’t maintain momentum, losing the next two sets 6-3, 6-2. He openly admitted to battling a persistent back issue throughout the season, revealing he hasn’t taken a break from competition — even as his muscles grew increasingly fatigued. With the French Open looming, Murray expressed concern about whether he’ll be fit to compete, saying he’s trying to manage the pain without worsening it. 'I’ve felt this for months,' he told AFP. 'There’s just no time to rest.' Novak Djokovic faced an unexpected scare against Argentina’s Juan Monaco, dropping the first set amid gusty winds that disrupted his rhythm. Frustrated, he smashed his racket — but quickly regained control, storming back to win the next two sets 6-2, 6-3. He acknowledged the conditions affected both players equally, setting up a quarterfinal clash with Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who dispatched Juan Martin del Potro in straight sets. Rafael Nadal bounced back from his Madrid disappointment with a commanding 6-1, 6-1 win over compatriot Marcel Granollers. Though the weather remained tricky, Nadal found his groove after the third game, delivering a clinical performance. His next opponent will be Tomas Berdych. Roger Federer, the defending Rome champion, dug deep to overcome former world No. 1 Juan Carlos Ferrero in three sets: 6-2, 5-7, 6-1. He now faces Andreas Seppi, who pulled off a thrilling three-set upset over Stanislas Wawrinka, winning the deciding tiebreak 8-6 after saving multiple match points. The women’s side saw a major shake-up when world No. 1 Victoria Azarenka withdrew due to a right shoulder injury. Second seed Maria Sharapova advanced with a 7-6(4), 6-3 win over Ana Ivanovic, setting up a highly anticipated quarterfinal against Venus Williams — their first-ever meeting on clay. Meanwhile, Serena Williams extended her flawless clay record this season, defeating Anabel Medina Garrigues 6-3, 6-1, and will next face Flavia Pennetta. Reflecting on her history at the venue, Serena said, 'This court holds so many memories.' Petra Kvitova, the fourth seed, edged out Sorana Cirstea in three sets to reach the quarterfinals, where she’ll battle Germany’s Angelique Kerber — another left-handed threat — in what promises to be a tactical showdown.

Iako se borio da osvoji prvi set u napetom tiebreaku, Murray nije mogao održati impetus i izgubio sljedeća dva seta 6-3, 6-2. Otkrio je da mu je bol u leđima trajala cijelu sezonu i da nije imao pauzu od natjecanja — čak ni kada su mu mišići postajali sve umorniji. S obzirom na Francuski otvoreni, Murray je izrazio zabrinutost oko svog učešća, rekavši da pokušava upravljati bolom kako ne bi pogoršao stanje. 'Osećam ovo već mjesecima,' rekao je AFP-u. 'Nema vremena za odmor.' Novak Đoković suočio se s neočekivanim izazovom protiv Argentineša Juana Monaca, izgubivši prvi set uz bujne vjetrove koji su ometali njegov ritam. Razočaran, razbio je raketu — ali brzo se oporavio i osvojio sljedeća dva seta 6-2, 6-3. Priznao je da su uvjeti utjecali na oba igrača jednako, što ga je dovelo do četvrtfinalne utakmice protiv Jo-Wilfrida Tsonge, koji je porazio Juana Martina del Portoa u dva seta. Rafael Nadal oporavio se od neuspjeha u Madriju dominirajućim rezultatom 6-1, 6-1 protiv španjolskog kolege Marcele Granollersa. Iako su vremenski uvjeti ostali teški, Nadal je pronašao ritam nakon trećeg igre i izveo klasičan nastup. Njegov sljedeći protivnik bit će Tomáš Berdych. Roger Federer, branitelj naslova u Rimu, duboko se potrudio da pobijedi bivšeg svjetskog broja 1, Juana Karlosa Ferrera, u tri seta: 6-2, 5-7, 6-1. Sada će se suočiti s Andreasom Seppijem, koji je izveo uzbudljiv trosetni preokret protiv Stanislava Vavrinke, osvojivši odlučujući tiebreak 8-6 nakon spašavanja više bodova za pobjedu. Ženski dio turnira bio je pretresen kada je svjetska broj jedan Viktorija Azarenka povukla svoje prijave zbog ozljede desnog ramena. Druga po rejtingu Maria Šarapova prošla je dalje rezultatom 7-6(4), 6-3 nad Anom Ivanović, postavši protivnicom Venus Williams u četvrtfinalu — njihov prvi susret na travi. U međuvremenu, Serena Williams produžila je svoj savršen zapis na travi ove sezone, pobjedom nad Anabel Medinom Garrigues 6-3, 6-1, a sljedeći protivnik joj je Flavija Pennetta. Reflektirajući na svoju povijest na ovom terenu, Serena je rekla: 'Ovaj teren ima toliko sjećanja.' Četvrta po rejtingu Petra Kvitova izborila se protiv Sorane Cirstea u tri seta da bi stigla do četvrtfinala, gdje će se suočiti sa Njemcom Angelique Kerber — još jednom lijevorukom prijetnjom — u utakmici koja obećava biti taktički izazovna.

article_content: A woman reported missing after a mudslide and flash flood — which killed a 53-year-old driver and destroyed homes — has been found safe, authorities confirmed today. Six homes were destroyed and approximately 30 others damaged when mudslides and flash flooding struck Manitou Springs, Colorado, following heavy rainfall in an area still recovering from last year’s wildfires. Many residents were forced to cling to trees and scramble up cliffside roads to escape torrents of mud and silt. Trail of destruction: A pickup truck was crushed beneath boulders and uprooted trees. Tide of debris: Rubble and branches were swept into yards and homes. As heavy rain continued to fall, residents and business owners worked to salvage belongings and clear debris, while tow trucks removed wrecked vehicles from streets and highways. Victim: John Collins, 53, was found buried under mud and debris next to his car on Highway 24, according to El Paso County police. The region has become significantly more vulnerable to flash floods since last year’s wildfires left scorched soil unable to absorb water effectively. 'This is the first year of the burn scar. We’ve got nine more years of this,' said Colorado Springs Fire Lieutenant Steve Schopper. When the storm hit Friday, it sent mud, boulders, and debris surging into Manitou Springs, a town of roughly 5,000 residents. Initial reports indicated two fatalities, but one woman — who requested anonymity — was later confirmed safe. Laura Hunter, 49, described her harrowing escape after her rental home was obliterated by a four-foot wall of mud and floodwater. 'I lost everything, but I survived. I’m so grateful to be alive,' Hunter said. She was at home when water began seeping through her living room window. Believing she could reach higher ground, she opened the front door — and was immediately swept away. Despite breaking her leg, Hunter managed to grab a tree and crawl to a ridge, where neighbors rescued her. Forceful surge: The four-foot wall of mud and water demolished cars and homes upon impact. Rescued: Laura Hunter was pulled to safety after the flood swept away her home. Clean-up: Volunteers helped remove mud from a local café. Her rental home was destroyed, but a firefighter returned her ID and bank cards, and a friend recovered her bicycle. 'My long-term goals are simple: to be deeply grateful for my life and to build healthy relationships. That’s what matters most now,' Hunter told reporters at Penrose Hospital in Colorado Springs. John Collins, of Teller County, was the only confirmed fatality. Friends remembered him as a gentle man who loved gardening and dressed as Santa for children during the holidays. 'It was always the highlight of my children’s Christmas to sit on his lap,' said family friend Jessica Russ-Medovich. 'They’ll never forget that.' As additional rain fell, residents struggled to secure their homes and recover belongings. Some said they doubted they could endure rebuilding again, having done so after prior disasters. Swarms of volunteers arrived to help clear silt from homes and businesses. However, a resident near Timberline Baptist Church reported looters rummaging through items volunteers had salvaged and placed in the parking lot. 'They were going through everything, just taking whatever they could,' the woman told CBS Denver. At least 20 vehicles were swept away on Friday. Kathryn Presnal, of Cascade, recounted how she fled her car and climbed a cliffside, pulling another driver to safety as the flood surged. 'I grabbed her hand and pulled her up,' said the Colorado Springs school principal. 'We stood there and watched our cars float away.' City officials are constructing 11 catch basins to mitigate future flooding. 'Given the volume of rain we received Friday, nothing we could have done would have prevented this level of flooding,' said city spokesperson Dave Hunting. 'It was just Mother Nature doing her thing.'
translated_content: Žena koja je prijavljena kao nestala nakon klizanja zemlje i poplave prouzrokovane olujom — koja je ubila vozača od 53 godine i uništila kuće — pronađena je živa, potvrdili su vlasti danas. Šest kuća je uništeno, a otprilike trideset drugih oštećeno kada su klizanje zemlje i poplave pogodile Manitou Springs u Koloradu nakon jakih kiša u regiji koja se još uvijek oporavlja od požara prošle godine. Mnogi su stanovnici morali držati se stabala i penjati se uz stjenice uz ceste kako bi pobjegli od struja blata i mulja. Trag uništenja: Pickup kamion bio je srušen pod kamenjem i iskorenjenim stablima. Val šljunka: Odlomci i grane bili su uneseni u dvorišta i kuće. Dok su jake kiše nastavile padati, stanovnici i vlasnici poslova pokušavali su spašavati svoje stvari i čistiti štetu, dok su kola s ruševinama bila vučena s ulica i autoceste. Žrtva: John Collins, 53, pronađen je zakopan pod blatom i ruševinama pored svog automobila na cesti Highway 24, prema policiji okruga El Paso. Regija je postala značajno ranjivija za poplave jer su požari prošle godine ostavili spaljenu zemlju koja više ne može apsorbirati vodu. 'Ovo je prva godina zone izgorjelog tla. Imamo još devet godina ovakvih rizika,' rekao je pomoćnik zapovjednika vatrogasaca iz Colorado Springsa Steve Schopper. Kada je oluja pogodila petkom, ona je navela blato, kamenje i druge šljunkove u Manitou Springs, grad od oko 5.000 stanovnika. Početne izvještaje su navodile dvije smrti, ali jedna žena — koja je tražila anonimnost — kasnije je potvrđena kao živa. Laura Hunter, 49, opisala je svoj strahotni bijeg nakon što joj je najamna kuća potpuno uništena četverofetnim zidom blata i poplavnih voda. 'Izgubila sam sve, ali preživjela sam. Veoma sam zahvalna što sam preživjela,' rekla je Hunter. Bila je kod kuće kada je voda počela ulaziti kroz prozor u dnevnoj sobi. Mislila je da će moći doći na više tlo, pa je otvorila vrata — i odmah je odnijeta. Unatoč slomljenoj nozi, Hunter je uspjela uhvatiti se za drvo i puzati na greben, gdje su je spasili susjedi. Snaga vala: Četverofetni zid blata i vode uništio je automobile i kuće prilikom udara. Spasena: Laura Hunter je izvučena na sigurno nakon što je poplava odnijela njenu kuću. Čišćenje: Dobrovoljci su pomagali u uklanjanju blata iz kafe. Njena najamna kuća je bila otklonjena, ali vatrogasac joj je vratio ličnu kartu i bankovne kartice, a prijatelj je spašavao njen bicikl. 'Moji dugoročni ciljevi su jednostavni: biti duboko zahvalna za svoj život i graditi zdrave odnose. To je sada najvažnije za mene,' rekla je Hunter novinarima u bolnici Penrose u Colorado Springsu. John Collins iz Teller Countya bio je jedina potvrđena žrtva. Prijatelji su ga sjećali kao mekog čovjeka koji je volio vrtlarstvo i oblačio se kao Djed Mraz za djecu tijekom Božića. 'To je uvijek bio najveći radost za moju djecu da sjednu na njegovim koljenima,' rekla je porodična prijateljica Jessica Russ-Medovich. 'To će nikad ne zaboraviti.' Dok su dodatne kiše padale, stanovnici su se borili da osiguraju svoje kuće i spašavaju stvari. Neki su rekli da sumnjaju da mogu podnijeti ponovno građenje, budući da su već to učinili nakon prethodnih katastrofa. Veliki broj dobrovoljaca stigao je da pomogne u uklanjanju mulja iz kuća i poslova. Međutim, jedna stanovnica blizu Crkve Timberline Baptist prijavila je da su ljudi pljačkali stvari koje su dobrotvornici spašavali i stavili na parking. 'Hodali su kroz sve, samo tražeći što mogu uzeti,' rekla je žena CBS Denveru. Na petak je bilo najmanje 20 automobila odnijeto. Kathryn Presnal iz Cascadea opisala je kako je pobjegla iz svog automobila i penjala se uz stijenu, povlačeći drugog vozača sa sobom dok je poplava stizala. 'Uhvatila sam je za ruku i povukla je gore,' rekla je direktorica škole iz Colorado Springsa. 'Stajali smo tamo i gledali kako naši automobili plutaju.' Gradski zvaničnici grade 11 kanala za prikupljanje vode kako bi smanjili rizik od budućih poplava. 'S obzirom na količinu kiše koju smo imali petkom, ništa što smo mogli učiniti ne bi spriječilo takav nivo poplave,' rekao je gradski govornik Dave Hunting. 'To je samo priroda činila svoj posao.'

article_content: Loretta Fuddy, the Hawaii health official who verified the authenticity of President Obama’s long-form birth certificate, died Wednesday night in a small-plane crash. The aircraft, carrying nine people, went down about a mile off Kalaupapa on the island of Molokai, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. Eight passengers survived; one swam ashore, four were rescued by a Maui Fire Department helicopter, and three were saved by a Coast Guard helicopter. As director of Hawaii’s Department of Health, Fuddy played a pivotal role in publicly confirming Obama’s birth records in April 2011, helping to dispel baseless claims questioning his U.S. citizenship. 'I have seen the original records filed at the Department of Health and attest to the authenticity of the certified copies the department provided to the President,' she said at the time. Governor Neil Abercrombie called her death devastating, describing Fuddy as deeply loved and respected — selfless, devoted, and guided by both expertise and compassion. 'Her knowledge was vast; her counsel and advice always given from her heart as much as from her storehouse of experience,' he stated. A biography on hawaiihealthconnector.com highlighted her leadership in public health and numerous accolades. Outside of work, she enjoyed singing in her church choir, spending time with her cat Flint, and bonding with her grand nieces and nephews.

Zrakoplov s devet putnika srušio se otprilike jednu milju od Kalaupape na otoku Molokai, prema U.S. obalnoj straži. Osmorica putnika preživjela; jedan je plivao na obalu, četvoro je spašeno helikopterom vatrogasne službe s Mauija, a troje je spašeno helikopterom obalne straže. Kao direktorica Zavoda za zdravstvo Havaja, Fuddy je igrala ključnu ulogu u javnoj potvrdi Obama-ovih rodnih dokumenata u travnju 2011., pomažući u ukidanju besnovitih tvrdnji o njegovoj američkoj državljanstvu. 'Vidjela sam izvorne dokumente predane u Zavodu za zdravstvo i potvrđujem autentičnost certificiranih kopija koje je zavod pružio predsjedniku,' rekla je tada. Guverner Neil Abercrombie nazvao je njenu smrt katastrofalnom, opisujući Fuddy kao duboko voljenu i poštovanu osobu — bezinteresnu, posvećenu i vodjenu istovremeno stručnošću i saživljavanjem. 'Njeno znanje je bilo ogromno; savjeti i smjernice su uvijek dolazili iz srca, ne samo iz njenog zaliha iskustva,' rekao je on. Biografija na hawaiihealthconnector.com istakla je njezinu vodeću ulogu u javnom zdravstvu i brojna priznanja. Izvan posla, ona je uživala u pjevanju u crkvenom zboru, provođenju vremena s mačkom Flint i druženju s svojim unucima i unukama.

article_content: Can a movie capture lightning twice? Stephenie Meyer’s 'Twilight' series proved that even critically panned stories can dominate box offices — but 'The Host' might only manage the hype, not the heart. While it draws from decades of alien possession tales — from 'Invasion of the Body Snatchers' to the Wachowskis’ overlooked 'The Invasion' — this version flips the script: the invaders aren’t monsters. They’re the 'Souls,' calm, truthful, nonviolent beings who’ve already won Earth. Only scattered human survivors remain, hiding in deserts and caves. At the center is Melanie (Saoirse Ronan), whose body is taken over by a Soul named Wanda. But Melanie refuses to disappear. What follows isn’t a battle for control — it’s a quiet, internal dialogue between two consciousnesses sharing one skin. Ronan, one of cinema’s most gifted young performers, tries to carry the weight of this psychological tug-of-war, though some compare her performance to a puppet pulled by invisible strings — poignant, but rigid. The story leans into romance: Melanie’s ex-boyfriend Jared still loves her, while another survivor, Ian, finds himself drawn to Wanda’s gentle nature. 'You wouldn’t love me if you saw my real face,' Wanda says — but love, as the film suggests, doesn’t always need a face. Meanwhile, the Souls’ overwhelming technological superiority raises questions: Why can’t they find hidden humans? Why do sunglasses become a dead giveaway? The film doesn’t answer — and neither does it offer suspense. Visually, the desert cave hideout stands out — a striking, almost poetic refuge. William Hurt’s eccentric farmer Jeb, powered by hand-cranked solar panels, brings rare charm to an otherwise somber tone. But the male leads lack depth, and Diane Kruger’s intense alien hunter, The Seeker, is wasted. The result? A film that wants to be profound but feels stuck in its own seriousness — a 'Twilight' cousin that forgot to smile, laugh, or even blink.
translated_content: Može li se grom udariti dva puta? Serija 'Twilight' od Stephenie Meyer je dokazala da čak i kritički zanemariva priča može dominirati na blagajnama — ali 'The Host' možda će uspjeti samo u stvaranju haosa, a ne srca. Iako se oslanja na decenije priča o vanzemaljskom zauzimanju — od 'Invasion of the Body Snatchers' do zanemarenog 'The Invasion' Wachowskijevih — ova verzija okreće scenu: invazija nisu zličari. Oni su 'Duše', mirni, iskreni, nenasilni bića koja su već osvojila Zemlju. Samo nekoliko preživjelih ljudi ostaje, skrivenih u pustinjama i pećinama. Na središtu je Melanija (Saoirse Ronan), čije tijelo je zauzeto od strane Duše koja se zove Vanda. Ali Melanija se ne želi otkazati. Ono što slijedi nije borba za kontrolu — već tiha, unutrašnja razmjena između dvije svijesti koje dijele jedno tijelo. Ronan, jedna od najtalentiranijih mladih glumica u kinematografiji, pokušava nositi težinu ovog psihološkog tugovanja, iako neki uspoređuju njenu performansu sa lutkom vučenom nevidljivim niti — emotivnom, ali krutom. Priča se oslanja na roman: Melanijin bivši dečko Jared joj još uvijek voli, dok drugi preživjeli, Ian, osjeća privlačnost prema Vandinom mekom naravu. 'Ne bi volio mene ako bi video kako ja zapravo izgledam,' kaže Vanda — ali ljubav, kao što film sugerira, ne mora uvijek imati lice. U međuvremenu, nadmoćna vanzemaljska tehnologija Duša postavlja pitanja: Zašto ne mogu pronaći skrivene ljude? Zašto su naočale pokazatelj? Film ne odgovara — niti nudi uzbuđenje. Vizualno, pećinska skloništa izvanredno ističu — zapanjujući, gotovo poetski utočište. William Hurtov čudnovati farmer Jeb, napajan ručnim solarnim panelima, donosi rijetku simpatiju u inače sumorn ton. Ali muški likovi nemaju dubinu, a Diane Krugerova intenzivna vanzemaljska lovacica, Tražiteljka, je potpuno izgubljena. Rezultat? Film koji želi biti dubok, ali se osjeća zarobljen u vlastitoj ozbiljnosti — rođak 'Twilighta' koji je zaboravio osmijeh, smijeh ili čak treptati.

article_content: After a lighthearted chat with her Canadian husband, Sabriena Abrre took to TikTok to share how shocked she was by the gaps in her own geography knowledge — despite being a solid student who graduated with strong grades. In her viral October 26 video, she revealed that she once believed Alaska was an island, thought Texas was larger than Alaska, and didn’t realize Maine connected to Canadian provinces like Quebec and New Brunswick. These weren’t random guesses; they stemmed directly from how U.S. schools typically teach geography: in isolation, using flattened maps that shrink Alaska and obscure cross-border relationships. She shared that even her uncle, living in Utah, confused Vancouver as a country instead of a city in British Columbia — a mistake she likens to asking if someone’s been to California from Los Angeles. While she jokes about knowing the periodic table, dinosaur diets, and how to drop an egg without breaking it, she stresses that these aren’t substitutes for basic civic knowledge. Her core argument? Teach North America as a connected region, not two disconnected countries. ‘I didn’t think I needed a globe to check if my school was right,’ she said. The video, viewed over 828,000 times, resonated with thousands who admitted similar blind spots — while others blamed her for not seeking out maps herself. But Sabriena’s point remains: if foundational geography isn’t taught accurately in classrooms, expecting students to self-correct is unfair.
translated_content: Nakon lagane razmjene s kanadskim mužem, Sabriena Abrre je otišla na TikToka da podijeli kako je bila šokirana prazninama u svom znanju o geografiji — iako je bila dobra učenica koja je završila s odličnim ocjenama. U svom viralnom videu objavljenom 26. listopada, otkrila je da je jednom vjerovala da je Aljaska otok, da je mislila da je Teksas veći od Aljaskе i da nije znala da Maine graniči s kanadskim pokrajinama Kvebek i Novi Brunswick. Ovo nisu bile nasumične pretpostavke; izvor im je bio način na koji se geografija obično predaje u američkim školama: izolirano, koristeći ravnine karte koje smanjuju Aljasku i skrivaju granice između zemalja. Podijelila je da je čak i njezin stric, koji živi u Utahu, pogriješio i smatrao da je Vancouver država umjesto grada u pokrajini Britanska Kolumbija — grešku koju uspoređuje s pitanjem je li netko posjetio Kaliforniju iz Los Angelesa. Iako se šali o tome da zna periodni sustav elemenata, prehranu dinozaura i kako spustiti jaje bez da se razbije, naglašava da ovo ne mogu zamijeniti osnovno građansko znanje. Njezin ključni argument? Naučite Sjevernu Ameriku kao povezanu regiju, ne kao dvije odvojene zemlje. 'Ne mislila sam da trebam globus da provjerim je li moja škola u pravu,' rekla je. Video, koji je pregledan više od 828.000 puta, pronašao je odjek kod tisuća ljudi koji su priznali slične praznine — dok su drugi optuživali ju da nije tražila karte sama. Ali Sabrienin poučak ostaje: ako osnovna geografija nije poučavana točno u školama, očekivati da će učenici sami popraviti svoje znanje nije pravedno.

article_content: Alexandra Traycoff, a 24-year-old heart patient who has received care at Riley Hospital for Children since infancy, was moved after seeing a news story about 8-year-old Katelyn Newell — another young girl awaiting a heart transplant at the same hospital. What struck Alexandra was not only Katelyn’s medical journey but also their shared love for pop star Justin Bieber. Having received three heart surgeries herself and now attending outpatient care, Alexandra felt a deep connection. She decided to give Katelyn two unused tickets to Bieber’s upcoming July 10 concert at Bankers Life Fieldhouse. With the help of her parents, Lori and Sergei, Alexandra arranged a surprise visit to Katelyn’s hospital room. The surprise was coordinated with WRTV 6, whose crew documented the emotional moment. Katelyn, seated in a red hospital wagon, first discovered a Bieber book and temporary tattoos before finding the tickets tucked under layers of tissue paper. 'Do you know what those are?' her mother asked. 'Tickets,' Katelyn replied. 'To?' 'A concert.' 'Who are you going to see?' 'Justin!' Overwhelmed, Katelyn clutched the tickets as applause filled the room. Alexandra’s mother, Lori, described the gesture as 'hope for the future — something for Katelyn to look forward to.' The Traycoffs had originally planned to sell the extra tickets but changed their minds after learning of Katelyn’s story. They also released a bouquet of balloons outside the hospital — wishing for Katelyn’s phone call announcing a matching donor heart. Alexandra is now working through social media to connect Katelyn with Justin Bieber, having reached out to Ellen DeGeneres and tweeting directly to the singer — though she has not yet received a response. She plans to return to visit Katelyn and stay in touch with her family. 'Moms need support, too,' Lori Traycoff said. 'We’re here for each other.'

article_content: Far-right politician Marine Le Pen has suffered a spinal fracture after falling into an empty pool in France, according to reports. The 44-year-old’s 'rather serious' accident has sent shockwaves through nationalist circles across Europe. As leader of the National Front (FN), Le Pen is one of the most prominent right-wing figures on the continent, known for her hardline stance on immigration and criticism of Islam. Her policies have consistently drawn significant electoral support. Le Pen succeeded her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, as head of the party in January 2011. A May poll indicated she would defeat incumbent President François Hollande in a hypothetical election. She has capitalized on public dissatisfaction fueled by economic stagnation, record unemployment, and Hollande’s low approval ratings. The accident was first disclosed by her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen — a convicted racist and anti-Semite who was a finalist in the 2002 French presidential election. He explained her absence from an FN meeting in Limoges: 'Marine could not attend because she was the victim of a rather serious accident that left her immobile. She fell into an empty pool and sustained a spinal fracture.' The FN confirmed the injury as a sacral fracture — a painful condition affecting the triangular bone at the base of the spine, often requiring surgery and significantly limiting mobility. Though the incident occurred a week ago, the party stated Le Pen remains committed to her political duties. Under her leadership, the FN has sought to distance itself from its extremist past, including overt racism and intimidation targeting Jews, Muslims, and minority communities. Today, the FN is France’s third-largest political force. In recent months, Le Pen has led opposition to same-sex marriage in France and fiercely criticized Hollande’s Socialist government. She advocates for drastic immigration reductions, reinstating the death penalty, and withdrawing from the European Union. Like her father, Le Pen’s charisma has become synonymous with the FN — a presence now potentially jeopardized by her injury.

article_content: Chris Berkey navigates the rough waters of the Great Lakes, delivering essential goods like cement to remote industrial towns — a gritty but vital job that keeps the U.S. economy moving. But these waters are changing. In December, Lake Michigan and Lake Huron hit record-low water levels, and experts predict even lower readings within months. Ships like Berkey’s are now carrying lighter loads to avoid running aground, some harbors have shut down entirely, and coastal tourism is bracing for a tough season. ‘There used to be a safety margin,’ Berkey says. ‘Now it’s gone.’ This isn’t new — water levels have been below average for over a decade, according to Keith Kompoltowicz of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. But the situation is worsening. Coal shipments have fallen 8.2% since 2012 and are a quarter below their five-year average, largely because silt has clogged harbors and dredging hasn’t kept pace. A $200 million backlog in maintenance work means 17 million tons of sediment now block critical channels. Fishing communities are suffering too. In Frankfort, Michigan, the famed Betsie River salmon run — a magnet for anglers from Texas, Ohio, and beyond — dried up last year. Fish stranded in mud led state officials to close the run to protect the species. If spring rains don’t restore water levels, the narrow passage could vanish again, driving tourists away. Local businesses, like Steve Christian’s Dinghy’s restaurant, rely on summer visitors. ‘No boats in the harbor? No customers in my dining room,’ he says. Meanwhile, private marinas worry about access, and charter operators fear losing peak-season revenue. Even Chicago’s water district had to clarify that fears of sewage flowing backward into Lake Michigan are unfounded — though low water could still restrict river traffic. The root cause? A combination of dry winters, hot summers, and insufficient snowmelt. Though similar lows occurred in 1964, and history suggests recovery is possible, the real bottleneck may be political: Congress has left nearly $7 billion untouched in a dedicated harbor fund, spending only half of what comes in annually. ‘The money’s there,’ says Glen Nekvasil of the Lake Carriers’ Association. ‘They just need to use it.’ For now, businesses adapt — shifting to trucks and trains, cutting capacity, hoping for rain. But as Berkey puts it: ‘If there’s no water, we’re going to miss out on a lot of activity.’ And while locals believe this is cyclical — and history says they’re right — waiting for nature to fix it isn’t enough. Infrastructure, funding, and foresight are needed now.

Ali ove vode se mijenjaju. Prošlog prosinca jezera Michigan i Huron postigle su rekordno niske razine vode, a stručnjaci predviđaju još niže razine u sljedećim mjesecima. Brodovi poput Berkeyevog sada nose manje tereta kako bi se izbjeglo zaglavljivanje, neki pristaništa su potpuno zatvorena, a obalni turizam se priprema za tešku sezonu. ‘Postojala je sigurnosna margina,’ kaže Berkey. ‘Sada je nestala.’ Ovo nije novo — razine vode su više od deset godina ispod prosjeka, prema Keithu Kompoltowiczu iz U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Ali situacija se pogoršava. Pošiljke uglja opale su za 8,2% od 2012. i za četvrtinu ispod petogodišnjeg prosjeka, uglavnom jer mulj zagušuje pristaništa, a kanalizacija nije uslijedila. Zaliha od 200 milijuna dolara u održavanju znači da je 17 milijuna tona mulja sada blokirala ključne prolaze. Zahvaćeni su i ribarski zajednice. U Frankfortu, Michigan, poznati ribolov lososa na rijeci Betsie — magnet za ribolovce iz Teksasa, Ohia i drugdje — prošle je godine osušio. Ribice su ostale zarobljene u blatu, što je natjeralo državne službe da zatvore ribolov kako bi se zaštitila populacija. Ako proljetne kiše ne vrate razine vode, uski prolaz bi mogao ponovo nestati, odvodeći turiste. Lokalne tvrtke, poput Stevea Christiana iz restorana Dinghy’s, ovise o ljetnim posjetiteljima. ‘Nema brodova u luci? Nema kupaca u mom restoranu,’ kaže on. Međutim, privatni marini brinu o pristupu, a operateri čartera boje se gubitka prihoda u vršnoj sezoni. Čak je i vodna agencija u Chicagu morala objasniti da su strahovi od preliva otpadnih voda u jezero Michigan nemogući — iako niske razine mogu ograničiti promet na rijeci. Glavni uzrok? Kombinacija suhih zima, vrućih ljeta i nedostatka taloga snijega. Iako su slično niske bile i 1964., a povijest sugerira da će se situacija poboljšati, pravi blokada može biti politička: Kongres je ostavio gotovo 7 milijardi dolara nepotrošenih u posebnom fondu za pristaništa, trošeći samo polovicu onoga što se prikupi. ‘Novac je tu,’ kaže Glen Nekvasil iz Lake Carriers’ Association. ‘Samо trebaju ga koristiti.’ Za sada, tvrtke se prilagođavaju — prelaze na kamione i vlakove, smanjuju kapacitet, nadajući se kiši. Ali kao što Berkey kaže: ‘Ako nema vode, izgubit ćemo puno aktivnosti.’ I dok lokalni stanovnici vjeruju da je ovo ciklično — a povijest kaže da imaju pravo — čekanje da priroda riješi problem nije dovoljno. Potrebna su infrastruktura, financiranje i predvidljivost sada.

article_content: On Constitution Day, President Droupadi Murmu called for a bold overhaul of India’s judicial recruitment system, proposing a nationwide judicial service designed to identify bright young minds early and guide them upward through the courts — from district benches to the Supreme Court. Speaking at the Supreme Court’s annual celebration, she pointed out that too many Indians are shut out of justice not because they lack merit, but because they can’t afford lawyers or don’t understand court procedures conducted in unfamiliar languages. Her vision? A system where justice isn't a privilege for the few, but a right accessible to all — regardless of income, region, or mother tongue. Murmu noted that India’s judiciary has always been open to diversity, and she believes the bench and bar should mirror the country’s rich cultural mosaic. One powerful way to do that, she suggested, is through a transparent, merit-based national exam to bring in talent from every corner of the country — including underrepresented communities. 'Let’s give every ambitious student from a small town or village the same shot as someone from Delhi or Mumbai,' she urged. Drawing from childhood memories of folk tales about kings who hung a bell for anyone to ring when seeking justice, Murmu reflected that true justice isn’t about constant noise — it’s about building a system so efficient that people rarely need to cry out for help. 'We shouldn’t make citizens beg for justice,' she said. 'We should make justice come to them.' She shared how visiting top universities — IITs, IIMs, and state colleges — has shown her how many brilliant students dream of serving in the judiciary, not just as bureaucrats or engineers. Yet, the path remains unclear and intimidating. 'We need to remove the walls between classrooms and courtrooms,' she said, urging legal educators and policymakers to design smoother entry points. Murmu commended recent moves by the Supreme Court — like releasing judgments in regional languages and streaming hearings live — as vital steps toward transparency and inclusion. But she stressed that these are only beginnings. The real work lies in dismantling colonial-era mindsets still embedded in legal culture, and empowering the younger generation to reimagine justice through the lens of the Constitution — not as a dusty document, but as a living, breathing promise. She ended with optimism: India has proven it can uplift women, Dalits, Adivasis, and others into leadership roles across sectors. Now, she believes, it’s time for the judiciary to lead the way — not just in interpreting the law, but in embodying the democracy it serves.

U svom govoru na godišnjoj proslavi Vrhovnog suda, istaknula je da su previše Indijanaca isključeno iz pravde ne zato što imaju manje kvalifikacija, već zato što ne mogu priuštiti odvjetnike ili ne razumiju postupke koji se vode na nepoznatim jezicima. Njena vizija? Sustav u kojem pravda nije privilegija malih, već pravo dostupno svima — bez obzira na prihod, regiju ili maternji jezik. Murmu je napomenula da je indijski sudbeni sustav uvijek bio otvoren raznolikosti i da smatra da su sudovi i odvjetnici trebali reflektirati bogatstvo kulturne raznolikosti zemlje. Jedan moćan način da se to ostvari, predložila je, jest transparentan i meritokratski nacionalni ispit koji bi privukao talente iz svih dijelova zemlje — uključujući i zanemarivane zajednice. 'Neka svaki ambiciozan student iz malog grada ili sela ima iste šanse kao i netko iz Delhija ili Mumbaija,' pozvala je. Povezujući s djetinjstvom pričama o kraljevima koji su objesili zvono koje je svatko mogao zazvoniti kad bi tražio pravdu, Murmu je razmišljala kako prava pravda nije o stalnoj buci — već o stvaranju sustava toliko učinkovitog da ljudi rijetko moraju vrištati za pomoć. 'Ne bismo trebali natjerati građane da molje za pravdu,' rekla je. 'Treba nam pravdu donijeti njima.' Podijelila je kako su joj posjete najboljim sveučilištima — IIT-ima, IIM-ima i državnim kolegijima — pokazale koliko mnogo talentiranih studenata sanja o službi u sudstvu, a ne samo kao birokrati ili inženjeri. Međutim, put je još uvijek nejasan i zastrašujući. 'Moramo ukloniti zidove između učionica i sudnica,' rekla je, pozivajući obrazovne institucije i zakonodavce da dizajniraju glatke ulaze. Murmu je cijenila nedavne korake Vrhovnog suda — poput objave presuda na regionalnim jezicima i emitiranja sjednica uživo — kao ključne korake prema transparentnosti i uključivanju. Ali naglasila je da su to samo počeci. Stvarni rad leži u uklanjanju kolonijalnih mentaliteta koji su još uvijek ugrađeni u pravnu kulturu i omogućavanju mlađoj generaciji da ponovo zamisli pravdu kroz prizmu Ustava — ne kao zaboravljen dokument, već kao živi, dišući obećanje. Završila je optimizmom: Indija je dokazala da može podići žene, Dalite, Adivase i druge u vodeće uloge u svim sektorima. Sada, vjeruje ona, vrijeme je da sudstvo vodi put — ne samo tumačeći zakon, nego i otkrivajući demokraciju koju služi.

article_content: Eoin Morgan is stepping up as England’s new captain for Sunday’s fourth ODI against Sri Lanka, following Alastair Cook’s suspension for a sluggish over-rate in Hambantota. Though Morgan hasn’t reached a half-century in his past 15 one-day innings, he remains confident his natural, aggressive style will spark a turnaround. He credits his recent struggles not to lack of talent, but to distractions—namely, adjusting to coaching changes early in the summer and spending too much mental energy off the field. Morgan says he never dwells on form, because his game is built on risk-taking: 'I’ve always played like this since I was a kid, and it works for me.' His track record as captain tells a different story: in seven matches leading England, he’s averaged 73 with the bat—nearly double his career average. That’s why he believes taking the reins might actually help him score again. Meanwhile, England’s lineup is in flux. James Taylor, the only squad member yet to play, could debut, and off-spinner James Tredwell is expected back. Ben Stokes, struggling for rhythm, may be dropped. There’s buzz around promoting Moeen Ali to open alongside Alex Hales—a move that could electrify the team. After a narrow win on Wednesday, the mood in camp has shifted from doubt to belief. As Morgan puts it: 'You can see it in their eyes.' The match, set for 4:30 AM GMT at Colombo’s R. Premadasa Stadium, offers a fresh chapter for England—and a chance for Morgan to prove his leadership isn’t just symbolic.

article_content: A fish and chip shop owner in Padiham, Lancashire, has sparked controversy by displaying a banner declaring 'Under new management with English owners.' Paul Bradbury, who took over the Chippy On The Green with his wife Rachel less than two weeks ago, insists he is not racist. He claims customers prefer being served by English staff and say the sign made them more likely to visit — despite the shop having previously been owned by individuals of East Asian and Greek descent. The banner has drawn sharp criticism from local leaders, including Burnley’s Liberal Democrat MP Gordon Birtwistle and Padiham’s mayor, Coun Vincent Pridden, who called the message divisive and damaging to community cohesion. Local residents, such as teacher Gary Curson, expressed disgust, saying the sign promotes exclusion and sends a harmful message to children and the wider community. Bradbury defended the sign, stating, 'We’re advertising that we are English. You wouldn’t want your fish and chips served by someone Turkish or from elsewhere — it wouldn’t be as good.' He added that the shop welcomes everyone, regardless of background, and pointed out that it serves Chinese food, kebabs, and pizza — implying this contradicts any accusation of racism. Meanwhile, a separate issue emerged in Preston, where ex-soldier Steven Rolfe was asked to remove a painted English flag from his front door — a symbol he had displayed since 2003. While some saw it as harmless patriotism, others deemed it offensive. Muslim community leader Ali Anwar criticized what he called 'political correctness gone mad,' arguing that the English flag should not be monopolized by far-right groups and that pride in English identity need not be exclusionary. Lancashire Police confirmed they have not yet received official complaints about the banner. Yet, the incident has ignited broader conversations about national identity, inclusivity, and how expressions of cultural pride can unintentionally marginalize others.

article_content: The FDA has approved a new pain medication called Targiniq ER — a combination of oxycodone, a powerful opioid painkiller, and naloxone, a drug normally used to reverse overdoses. At first, this pairing seems odd. But the design is intentional: when swallowed whole, naloxone remains inactive, allowing oxycodone to relieve severe pain. If someone tries to crush, dissolve, or inject the pill, naloxone activates and blocks oxycodone’s euphoric effects, making abuse much less rewarding. Purdue Pharma has tried this before. When they reformulated OxyContin in 2010 to resist crushing, abuse dropped dramatically — from 36% of users misusing it before the change to just 13% afterward, according to the New England Journal of Medicine. That success fueled hope that similar strategies could work with Targiniq ER. But experts stress it’s not a silver bullet. Naloxone only works if the drug is tampered with and enters the bloodstream directly — meaning chewing or swallowing Targiniq ER delivers the full, unblocked dose of oxycodone. For someone struggling with addiction, it’s just as risky as taking plain oxycodone. Emergency physicians like Dr. Stephen Anderson see value in the built-in deterrents, calling them a ‘well-designed pharmacological barrier.’ Yet addiction researchers like Andrew Kolodny and Caleb Banta-Green remind us: if one opioid becomes harder to misuse, people will turn to another. This isn’t solving addiction — it’s just shifting the game. The U.S. accounts for 83% of global oxycodone use and 99% of hydrocodone consumption, with 46 lives lost every day to prescription opioid overdoses. The FDA says Targiniq ER should be prescribed only as a last resort — for patients who’ve exhausted all other pain management options. While this is a cautious step forward, it doesn’t address the systemic roots of the crisis.

Purdue Pharma već je pokušao ovaj pristup. Kada su reformirali OxyContin 2010. godine tako da je teže drobiti, zloupotreba je dramatično opala — s 36% korisnika koji su zloupotrebljavali lijek prije promjene na samo 13% nakon nje, prema New England Journal of Medicine. Iako je ovo oprezan korak naprijed, ne rješava sistemske korijene krize.

article_content: A 1,700-year-old Roman lead coffin, unearthed in a field in Leicestershire, has revealed a rare and poignant discovery: two jet bracelets, believed to have belonged to a young girl buried within. The coffin, sealed and remarkably preserved, was found last month by metal detectorist Chris Wright and has since been carefully excavated by experts from Archaeology Warwickshire and the University of York. The presence of the delicate bracelets — typically associated with Roman women — strongly suggests the child was female, though DNA analysis of bone fragments will confirm this. The child’s identity remains unknown, but researchers are inviting the public to help choose a Roman name for her from six meaningful options: Oriens (‘rise like the sun’), Loquor (‘I speak’), Aperio (‘reveal’), Addo (‘inspire’), Accendo (‘illuminate’), and Parvulus (‘infant’). Project spokesman Stuart Palmer described the find as 'very unusual,' noting that intact child burials from this era rarely survive. The lead coffin’s sealed environment has preserved not only bones but also layers of clay that may hold chemical traces — potentially revealing clues about diet, illness, or even cause of death. Experts estimate the coffin alone would have cost the equivalent of £200,000 in today’s currency, indicating the child came from an exceptionally wealthy family. Its east-west alignment further suggests it may be among the earliest known Christian burials in Leicestershire. Wright, a 30-year-old surveyor, recalled his shock and awe upon uncovering the artifact: 'It makes all the hours worthwhile.' The site was guarded by volunteers until excavation began, and no further digs are planned, as the surrounding area shows no signs of additional artifacts. Once analysis is complete, the coffin may be reburied — unless deemed historically significant enough for public display.

Identitet djeteta ostaje nepoznat, ali istraživači pozivaju javnost da pomogne odabrati rimska imena za nju iz šest značajnih opcija: Oriens (‘uspon poput sunca’), Loquor (‘ja govorim’), Aperio (‘otkrivam’), Addo (‘inspiriram’), Accendo (‘osvijetljujem’) i Parvulus (‘dijete’). Predstavnik projekta Stuart Palmer opisao je ovo otkriće kao 'vrlo neobično', napominjući da su sahrane djece iz tog razdoblja rijetko sačuvane. Stručnjaci procjenjuju da bi sam kovčeg koštao ekvivalent od 200.000 funti danas, što ukazuje da je dijete pripadalo izuzetno bogatoj obitelji. Nakon završetka analize, kovčeg će se možda ponovno sahraniti — osim ako se ne smatra historijski značajnim za javnu izložbu.

article_content: School days are often said to be the happiest of your life—but for Tom Parker Bowles, being sent away to boarding school at age seven is an experience he would never subject his own children to. The son of the Duchess of Cornwall recently described his former prep school, Summer Fields in Oxford, as 'a hotbed of the sorts of things that are coming out now,' claiming one staff member allegedly was present during showers with naked boys. However, Nigel Talbot Rice, who served as headmaster from 1968 to 1997, dismissed these allegations as 'complete rubbish,' adding that no formal complaints were ever lodged during his tenure. Clarifying the incident, it is understood the staff member was not himself naked—only present during showers, a practice now widely considered unacceptable. Parker Bowles, now 39 and a food writer and restaurant critic for the Mail on Sunday, attended Summer Fields in the early 1980s before moving on to Eton. He recounted how he confided in his father about troubling moments at school, but nothing was ever formally addressed. 'Perhaps I'm speaking out of turn,' he admitted. His mother, Camilla, later expressed regret over sending him away so young. After his daughter Lola turned seven, Parker Bowles remarked: 'You sent me away eight months after this.' She responded, 'I'd never do it again.' In a wide-ranging interview promoting his new cookbook, Let’s Eat Meat, he also discussed his reaction to the 1992 publication of the 'Camillagate' transcripts—the private phone call between his mother and Prince Charles, in which Charles referred to wanting to be her 'tampon.' 'I didn’t want to read it,' he said. 'You don’t want the world reading intimate things you say to people you love.' He also reflected on his parents’ divorce when he was 18, describing it as a quiet, normal part of life. 'We’ve never really cared what people say about us,' he added. In 1999, Parker Bowles was caught by the News of the World boasting about using cocaine at the Cannes Film Festival. He accepted full responsibility: 'That was entirely my fault.' He hasn’t used the drug since. Despite his distaste for prep school, he enjoyed Eton and plans to send his son there at 13. He credits his academic turnaround to his father threatening to send him to a comprehensive school. 'I was rubbish at everything,' he joked. 'I was good at smoking.' He described his mother as 'a brilliant grandmother,' affectionately noting she is called 'Gaga' by his children. 'She’s worked incredibly hard,' he said. 'She didn’t really have a job apart from being our mother—and suddenly at 55, she started working.' Asked if she might become queen, he replied: 'I have no idea. That’s for far greater minds than mine.' Self-described as a monarchist but not royal, he concluded: 'Christ, no—I’m a good old pleb.'

article_content: After more than a decade of stagnation, Japan’s economy is showing signs of life — and the OECD believes this rebound might finally break the cycle of deflation that has haunted the nation for 14 years. According to its latest forecast, consumer prices are expected to start climbing by the end of 2013, with inflation hitting 2.4% by the close of 2014. This shift is largely thanks to Abenomics, the bold economic strategy introduced by Prime Minister Shinzo Abe earlier this year. At its core are three pillars: aggressive monetary easing by the Bank of Japan, increased government spending, and long-overdue structural reforms. The results are already visible: the Nikkei index has surged, the yen has dropped in value, making Japanese goods cheaper abroad, and businesses are regaining confidence. Among the reforms being pushed are measures to get more women into the workforce — a move seen as vital for sustaining growth. But the OECD also issued a stark warning: Japan’s public debt, now over 200% of its GDP, remains dangerously high. If not managed carefully, the agency fears, this could trigger a loss of market confidence and spark a financial crisis down the line. For now, though, the tide appears to be turning — cautiously, and with no guarantee it will hold.

Prema najnovijoj prognozi, cijene potrošnje očekuju se da će početi rasti do kraja 2013., s inflacijom koja dostiže 2,4% do kraja 2014. Ova promjena djelomično je zahvaljujući 'Abenomicsu', ambicioznoj gospodarskoj strategiji koju je predstavio premijer Shinzo Abe ranije ove godine. U osnovi su tri stupca: agresivno olakšavanje novčane politike od strane Banka Japana, povećanje državnih troškova i dugo zaboravljene strukturne reforme. Rezultati su već vidljivi: indeks Nikkei je skočio, jen se smanjio u vrijednosti, čineći japanske proizvode jeftinijima na inozemnim tržištima, a poslovni subjekti opet stječu povjerenje. Među reformama koje se promiču su mjere za uključivanje većeg broja žena u radnu snagu — korak koji se smatra ključnim za održiv rast. Ali OECD je također izdao jasno upozorenje: japanski javni dug, koji sada prelazi 200% BDP-a, ostaje opasno visok. Ako se ne upravlja pažljivo, agencija se boji da bi to moglo izazvati gubitak povjerenja tržišta i dovesti do financijske krize u budućnosti. Za sada, međutim, prilika se čini da se okreće — oprezno, bez ikakve garancije da će trajati.

article_content: The New York Dolls didn’t wait for perfect conditions to make music — even if it meant recording in a rain-soaked Hawaiian house. Their latest album, 'Cause I Sez So', was born out of chaos: torrential downpours drowned their gear, forcing them to relocate mid-session. Producer Todd Rundgren had promised sunny skies on Kauai. Instead, they got constant rain — and a memorable story. Formed in the gritty streets of early '70s New York, the Dolls were never meant to be polished. With wild stage antics, glitter, leather, and a sound that mashed up the Rolling Stones, Velvet Underground, and girl-group pop, they laid the blueprint for punk — long before anyone called it that. Guitarist Sylvain Sylvain remembers it simply: 'We were bored. Let’s start a show.' Though they broke up before punk exploded — with bands like the Ramones and Sex Pistols riding the wave they helped create — the members never stopped making music. David Johansen became a cult favorite as Buster Poindexter, belting out 'Hot Hot Hot' in tuxedos. After the deaths of original members Johnny Thunders, Jerry Nolan, and Arthur Kane, Sylvain and Johansen kept the spirit alive. Their comeback began unexpectedly: Morrissey, a longtime fan, asked them to play a single show in London. 'We thought, why not?' Johansen says, chuckling. One gig turned into a tour, then a new album. 'Cause I Sez So' dropped in May — raw, playful, and packed with hard rock, pop hooks, and even a reggae twist on their classic 'Trash'. Now, the band — including Steve Conte, Sam Yaffa, and Brian Delaney — plays like a comedy troupe that just picked up instruments. Deadpan jokes interrupt songs. They don’t rehearse like pros; they improvise like friends. 'We’re not recreating the past,' Johansen insists. 'We just play.' Critics agree: Billboard called the album a worthy follow-up to their legendary early work. Audiences? Young and old, showing up with wide eyes — and leaving with balloons and earplugs. 'We give them both,' Sylvain smiles. 'Because rock 'n' roll isn’t about labels. It’s about feeling.'
translated_content: New York Dollsi nisu čekali savršene uvjete da bi napravili glazbu — čak i ako je to značilo snimati u kišnoj kući na Havajima. Njihov najnoviji album, 'Cause I Sez So', rođen je iz haosa: snažne kiše potopile su njihovu opremu, prisiljavajući ih da se premjeste tijekom snimanja. Producent Todd Rundgren obećao im je sunčane dane na Kauaiju. Umjesto toga, dobili su neprestanu kišu — i sjećanje koje neće zaboraviti. Formirani u prljavim ulicama ranog '70-ih New Yorka, Dollsi nikad nisu bili namijenjeni biti polirani. S divljim nastupima, sjajem, kožom i zvukom koji je miješao Rolling Stonese, Velvet Underground i djevojačke grupe, oni su postavili temelje za punk — dugo prije nego što je netko to nazvao tako. Gitaraš Sylvain Sylvain sjeti se jednostavno: 'Bili smo dosadni. Hajde da započnemo nastup.' Iako su se rastali prije nego što se punk proširio — dok su se bendovi poput Ramonesa i Sex Pistolsa uspinjali na val koji su oni pomogli stvoriti — članovi nikad nisu prestali praviti glazbu. David Johansen postao je kultni favorit kao Buster Poindexter, pevajući 'Hot Hot Hot' u frkama. Nakon smrti originalnih članova Johnnyja Thundersa, Jerryja Nolan-a i Arthura Kane-a, Sylvain i Johansen održavali su duh živim. Njihovo vraćanje počelo je neočekivano: Morrissey, dugogodišnji obožavatelj, zamolio ih je da odigraju jedan nastup u Londonu. 'Zamislili smo, zašto ne?' kaže Johansen, nasmijan. Jedan koncert pretvorio se u turneju, pa u novi album. 'Cause I Sez So' izdan je u svibnju — sirovi, igrački i pun hrabrih rock pjesama, pop melodija i čak reggae verzije njihove klasične 'Trash'. Sada, bend — uključujući Stevea Contea, Sam Yaffu i Briana Delaneyja — svira kao komična trupa koja je upravo podigla instrumente. Suho smiješni šale prekidaju pjesme. Ne vježbaju kao profesionalci; improviziraju kao prijatelji. 'Ne ponavljamo prošlost,' tvrdi Johansen. 'Samo sviramo.' Kritičari se slažu: Billboard je nazvao album dostojnim nastavkom njihovog legendarnog ranog rada. Publika? Mladi i stari, dolaze s širom očima — i odlaze s balonima i čepićima za uši. 'Dajemo im oba,' nasmije se Sylvain. 'Jer rock 'n' roll nije o oznakama. Ovo je o osjećaju.'

article_content: A woman has been charged with assaulting an 80-year-old Sikh man in a daylight attack in Coventry city centre, captured on a mobile phone. Police arrested 19-year-old Coral Millerchip on Friday after the elderly man was punched in the face and knocked to the ground on Trinity Street last Saturday. Millerchip, from the Wyken area of the West Midlands, faces one charge of assault and has been remanded in custody. The victim suffered a bloody nose and a black eye. A video of the incident, recorded by a passerby, went viral on social media. The attack occurred around 8:30 p.m. near a supermarket. Police have appealed for witnesses and urged anyone who shared the video or still images to remove them from social media, as they may interfere with the investigation. Millerchip was traced to an address in Gloucester and taken to a West Midlands Police station for questioning. Anyone with information is asked to contact West Midlands Police on 101 or Crimestoppers anonymously at 0800 555111.

article_content: Kaka isn’t just another high-earning footballer — he’s a symbol of resilience, humility, and faith in a sport often driven by money. Born Ricardo Izecson dos Santos Leite in Brazil in 1982, he earned the nickname 'Kaka' as a child because his brother couldn’t pronounce 'Ricardo.' By age eight, he was training with São Paulo’s youth academy, and before turning 16, he signed his first professional contract. His rise seemed unstoppable — until a devastating swimming pool accident in 2000 shattered a vertebra in his spine. Doctors warned he might never walk normally again. But Kaka defied the odds. He credits his recovery to divine intervention, a belief that has shaped his life ever since. He began donating portions of his earnings to his church and lived with quiet integrity off the pitch. By early 2001, he was playing for São Paulo’s senior team, helping them win the Torneio Rio-São Paulo. In 2002, he played a pivotal role in Brazil’s World Cup triumph. His elegant playmaking soon caught the eye of Europe’s elite. In 2003, AC Milan signed him for €9 million per season — a deal that lasted until 2013. With Milan, he lifted the Serie A title, the UEFA Champions League, and the FIFA Club World Cup. In 2007, he was crowned the best player in the world, winning both the Ballon d’Or and FIFA World Player of the Year. He also scored 23 goals for Brazil and was named one of Time magazine’s 100 Most Influential People in 2008. Off the field, Kaka married longtime love Caroline Celico in 2005, and their son was born in 2008. Yet in the season when he reportedly received offers of up to $700,000 a week — the highest in football history — his performance dipped due to a persistent groin injury. Still, clubs like Manchester City and Real Madrid remained eager, pursuing a potential transfer worth $150 million — a figure unmatched in the sport’s history.

article_content: The death toll from the collapse of Rana Plaza in Bangladesh could rise to as many as 1,400, officials warned, as rescue teams continue sifting through the wreckage six days after the disaster. Around 900 workers remain unaccounted for. On the morning of April 24, approximately 3,000 workers — predominantly young women making low-cost clothing for international retailers like Primark and Matalan — entered the eight-story Rana Plaza building in Savar, near Dhaka, despite visible cracks in the walls the previous day. The building, illegally expanded beyond its permitted five stories, collapsed suddenly, trapping thousands inside five garment factories. Emergency crews are now using heavy machinery to remove concrete slabs, expecting to find many more bodies as they reach lower levels. The official death count stands at 386, but authorities believe this number will climb sharply. Hundreds of grieving family members gather daily at makeshift morgues and the disaster site, holding photos and ID cards in hopes of identifying loved ones. Mohammed Sohel Rana, the building’s owner and a youth leader of Bangladesh’s ruling Awami League, was arrested on Sunday while attempting to flee to India. He faces charges of negligence, illegal construction, and forcing workers to enter a structurally unsound building. His father, Abdul Khaleque, was also detained for allegedly aiding him. Rescue workers report no signs of life in the lower floors. Brigadier General Ali Ahmed Khan of the fire brigade stated, 'Our men went inside and saw some dead bodies in the ground floor. But no one was seen alive.' The ambulances once stationed at the site have now been withdrawn, signaling dwindling hope for survivors. Primark has pledged to provide emergency aid and long-term compensation to victims and families of workers employed by its supplier in the building. This includes financial support for injured workers, funeral costs for the deceased, and education funding for children who lost parents. Loblaw, owner of the Joe Fresh brand, made a similar commitment, while Wal-Mart insists none of its products were authorized to be made there — though it is investigating possible unauthorized production. Four factory owners have also been arrested. Meanwhile, protests erupted in Ashulia and Gazipur, where workers burned an ambulance and attempted to set fire to a factory. Authorities responded by shutting down all garment factories in the area. Activists and labor groups say this tragedy is a wake-up call for Bangladesh’s entire garment industry — the world’s third-largest, worth £13 billion annually — and for global brands that profit from its cheap labor. 'If proper safety measures had been enforced, these deaths could have been avoided,' said Ruth Tanner of War on Want. 'They must pay full compensation and sign the Bangladesh Fire and Safety Agreement.'

Otprilike 900 radnika ostaje nestalo. Ujutro 24. travnja, otprilike 3.000 radnika — uglavnom mlade žene koje proizvode jeftinu odjeću za međunarodne trgovce poput Primarka i Matalana — ulazilo je u osmospratnu zgradu Rana Plaza u Savaru, blizu Dhake, unatoč vidljivim pukotinama na zidovima dan ranije. Zgrada, koja je nezakonito proširena izvan dopuštenih pet spratova, naglo se srušila, zarobivši tisuće radnika unutar pet tvornica odjeće. Ekipa za spašavanje koristi tešku opremu kako bi uklonila betonske ploče, očekujući da će pronaći još više mrtvih tijela kad dostignu niže razine. Službeni broj žrtava iznosi 386, ali vlasti vjeruju da će ovaj broj naglo porasti. Stotine žalosnih obitelji svakodnevno se skupljaju na privremenim mrtvačnicama i na mjestu katastrofe, držeći fotografije i lične kartice u nadi da će identificirati svoje bliske. Mohammed Sohel Rana, vlasnik zgrade i vođa omladinske grane vladajuće Awami League, hapšen je u nedjelju dok je pokušavao pobjeći u Indiju. Suočava se s optužbama za zanemarivanje, nezakonito građenje i prisiljavanje radnika da uđu u strukturalno nestabilnu zgradu. Njegov otac, Abdul Khaleque, također je hapšen zbog sumnje da mu je pomagao. Spašavatelji prijavljuju da nema znakova života na nižim razinama. General-pukovnik Ali Ahmed Khan, zapovjednik vatrogasne službe, rekao je: 'Naši ljudi su ušli i vidjeli neke mrtve tijele na prizemlju. Ali nitko nije bio živ.' Ambulante koje su bile smještene na mjestu sada su uklonjene, što ukazuje na smanjivanje nade za preživjele. Primark je obećao pružanje hitne pomoći i dugoročne nadoknade žrtvama i obiteljima radnika koji su radili kod njegovog dobavljača u zgradi. To uključuje financijsku podršku ranjenim radnicima, troškove sahrane za umrle i obrazovnu pomoć djeci koja su izgubila roditelje. Loblaw, vlasnik brenda Joe Fresh, dao je slično obećanje, dok Wal-Mart insistira da nijedan njegov proizvod nije bio ovlašten za proizvodnju tamo — iako istražuje moguću neovlaštenu proizvodnju. Također su hapšeni četiri vlasnika tvornica. U međuvremenu, protesti su izbili u Ashulia i Gazipuru, gdje su radnici zapalili ambulantu i pokušali zapaliti tvornicu. Vlasti su odgovorile zatvaranjem svih tvornica odjeće u tom području. Aktivisti i radnički savezi kažu da je ova tragedija probudni poziv za cijelu industriju odjeće u Bangladešu — treću najveću na svijetu, vrijednu 13 milijardi funti godišnje — i za globalne brendove koji profitiraju od njezine jeftine radne snage. 'Ako bi bile primijenjene odgovarajuće mjere sigurnosti, ove smrti bi se mogle izbjeći,' rekla je Ruth Tanner iz War on Want. 'Morate platiti punu nadoknadu i potpisati Bangladeški sporazum o požaru i sigurnosti.'

article_content: On Christmas Day, thousands of children across the UK were left in tears after a cyberattack disrupted PlayStation Network and Xbox Live — rendering their brand-new gaming consoles unusable. Families who had spent hundreds of pounds on consoles found themselves unable to access online multiplayer features, game downloads, or even initial setup processes. Parents took to social media in anger, demanding compensation from Sony and Microsoft. Many used the hashtag #christmasruined to share stories of shattered holiday hopes. One father, Mark Haynes from Cambridgeshire, described 'tantrums, tears and everything else' after repeated failed attempts to set up his children’s Xbox One. The hacking group Lizard Squad claimed responsibility, stating they carried out the attack 'for the laughs' and to expose weak cybersecurity — particularly on Xbox Live. The group, which had publicly threatened the outage since early December, dubbed itself the 'next-generation Grinch.' The attack, identified by analysts as a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS), flooded servers with traffic, blocking legitimate users. Games like Call of Duty and The Sims 4 became inaccessible, and new Xbox One units couldn’t complete their mandatory online activation. Ros Bruce from Essex said her 10-year-old son had spent weeks planning games with friends — only to cry for hours after being unable to play even 15 hours after opening his gift. 'It’s been his worst Christmas ever,' she said. Another parent in Scotland lamented: '£450 later and the kids have an expensive plastic paperweight.' Microsoft and Sony faced backlash for slow responses. Mark Haynes said he called Microsoft support four times — only to be told by one agent, 'We have no idea what’s going on.' While Xbox later confirmed its core services were restored, PlayStation engineers continued working on lingering network issues. Though unrelated, the timing sparked speculation due to Sony’s involvement in The Interview, a satirical film about North Korea that had triggered a separate, major cyberattack in late 2014 attributed to North Korean state-backed hackers. Microsoft had streamed the film via its Xbox platform, heightening public curiosity — though no credible evidence links the two incidents. With 110 million PlayStation and 48 million Xbox subscribers globally, the outage affected millions. Sony had reported selling one million consoles in the UK alone within eight months of launch, with holiday demand expected to surge. Lizard Squad told Tech website Winbeta the goal was to 'anger and reach the largest amount of people' — and they succeeded.

Obitelji koje su potrošile stotine funti na konzole nisu mogle pristupiti online multiplayer značajkama, preuzimanju igara ni čak početnoj postavci. Roditelji su se na društvenim mrežama izrazili s ljutnjom, tražeći nadoknadu od Sonyja i Microsofta. Mnogi su koristili hashtag #christmasruined kako bi dijelili priče o razbijenim božićnim nadi. Jedan otac, Mark Haynes iz Cambridgeshira, opisao je 'tujama, suzama i svemu ostalom' nakon ponovljenih neuspjelih pokušaja postavljanja Xbox One konzole za svoju djecu. Sa 110 milijuna pretplatnika na PlayStation i 48 milijuna na Xbox, napad je utjecao na milijune. Sony je objavio da je prodano jedan milijun konzola u Ujedinjenom Kraljevstvu u samo osam mjeseci nakon lansiranja, s očekivanim rastom prodaje prije Božića. article_content: A major coalition of Syrian Islamist rebels has announced it will not participate in the upcoming peace negotiations in Geneva, casting doubt on any realistic path to ending the country’s devastating civil war. Meanwhile, reports from Aleppo describe scenes of utter devastation following alleged airstrikes by forces loyal to President Bashar Al-Assad. Residents scrambled through clouds of dust and debris, digging for survivors after entire apartment blocks collapsed under the weight of crude 'barrel bombs'—improvised weapons known for their indiscriminate impact. Though Syria’s primary exiled opposition group, the National Coalition, has agreed to attend the Geneva talks—marking the first formal face-to-face meeting between Assad’s government and its opponents—the Islamic Front, a powerful bloc representing many frontline fighters, dismissed the initiative as meaningless. 'Our future won’t be decided in sterile conference rooms,' declared Abu Omar of the Islamic Front on social media. 'It will be written in blood on the battlefields.' With over 130,000 lives lost and nearly half the population displaced since the uprising began in 2011, the human toll continues to mount. Recent attacks have targeted neighborhoods like Al-Ansari and Al-Maysar, leaving children, elderly, and civilians caught in the crossfire. One image shows a woman clutching a surviving child as they flee collapsing structures; another captures rescuers pulling a lifeless body from the rubble. In a limited gesture, Syrian authorities allowed a small aid convoy to reach Yarmouk, a besieged Palestinian refugee camp where 15 people have died of starvation. But with only 200 food parcels delivered—enough to feed less than 2% of the camp’s 18,000 residents for a month—the move was widely seen as performative rather than humanitarian. Internationally, Russia has backed Assad’s stance, urging dialogue while rejecting foreign intervention. The U.S., once poised to launch punitive strikes after chemical weapon use, has since stepped back, leaving the opposition without crucial external support. Meanwhile, rebel factions have turned on each other, weakening their collective position. As Assad regains territory and gains momentum, the war increasingly resembles a grinding stalemate—with no end in sight and civilians paying the highest price.

Međutim, izvještaji iz Aleppa opisuju scene potpune katastrofe nakon navodnih zračnih napada snaga lojalnih predsjedniku Basharu al-Asadu. Građani su se trcali kroz oblake praha i ruševina, tražeći preživjele nakon što su cijeli blokovi stanova propali pod težinom grubih 'bubnjevih bombi'—neprecizno oružje poznato po svom neodabirnom učinku. Iako je glavna izgnana opozicijska grupacija Sirije, Nacionalna koalicija, složila da sudjeluje u pregovorima u Ženevi—što bi označavalo prvi službeni susret između vladine vlade i njenih protivnika—islamski front, moćni blok koji predstavlja mnoge borce na terenu, odbacio je inicijativu kao besmislenu. 'Naša budućnost neće biti odlučena u sterilen konferencijskim sobama,' rekao je Abu Omar iz Islamskog fronta na društvenim mrežama. 'Bit će napisana krvlju na bojištima.' S više od 130.000 žrtava i gotovo polovice stanovništva protjeranog od početka ustanka 2011. godine, ljudski trošak nastavlja rasti. Nedavni napadi ciljali su kvartove poput Al-Ansari i Al-Maysar, ostavljajući djecu, starije ljude i civilne osobe zarobljenima u križnom vatri. Jedna slika prikazuje ženu koja drži preživjelo dijete dok bije od padajućih zgrada; druga pokazuje spašavatelje kako izvlače mrtvo tijelo iz ruševina. U ograničenoj gesti, sirski autoriteti dozvolili su malu humanitarnu konvoj da dostavi pomoć u Yarmouk, opsadeno palestinsko izbjegličko kamp gdje je 15 ljudi umrlo od gladovanja. Ali s samo 200 paketa hrane dostavljenih—dovoljno da hraniti manje od 2% od 18.000 stanovnika kampa mjesec dana—ovaj korak je široko smatran performansnim, a ne humanitarnim. Na međunarodnoj razini, Rusija podržava stav Asada, pozivajući na dijalog dok odbacuje stranu intervenciju. SAD, koje su jednom bile spremne pokrenuti kaznene udare nakon kemijskog oružja, odustale su od takvih akcija, ostavljajući opoziciju bez ključne vanjske podrške. Međutim, pobunjeničke frakcije su okrenule oružje jedna protiv druge, oslabivši njihovu zajedničku poziciju. Dok se Asad vraća na teritorij i dobiva na snazi, rat sve više liči na iscrpljujući stalemat—bez vidljivog kraja, a civili plaćaju najvišu cijenu.
